Her marriage to Giovanni Volpi (by-named Campana) is not in the book: a son of theirs, Giovanni Volpi «d° Campana», 22, house 54, married Elisabetta Ferrara on 2 April 1845 and names «Sinforosa Defranceschi» as his mother, so the marriage was made by about 1822; the faded row is the only one of those years not read. **Other entries:** on 3 February 1858 (nos. 7 and 8, one spread) Giovanni De Franceschi, house 26, 26, son of Antonio and Maria Bergamo, married Giovanna Cleva of Canfanaro, 18, and Antonio Subiotto, smith, of Gimino, married Veneranda De Franceschi, 21, the groom's sister, daughter of Antonio and Maria Bergamo; on 11 January 1855 (no. 1) Leonardo Palmano married Domenica Crosilla, whose mother is Giacoma Defranceschi, and on 29 January 1856 (no. 9) Giovanni Crosilla married Antonia Motica, whose mother is Giacomina Defranceschi (both read by a reader at level 13); on a page of 1822 a bride Eufemia is called the daughter of the late Domenico Martinsich and the late «Pasqua» (probable) de' Franceschi. **Not found:** no marriage of Anna Maria (b. 1834), Antonio (b. 1839), Domenica (b. 1841) or Vittorio (b. 1844), children of the sacristan, nor of Ermenegildo; no Kovačina or Kalanj in any role (`cover` exit 0 for Defranceschi, Kalanj and Kovačina; near-names only: Caleich 1845, Calcich). **One open question the book makes:** the sacristan, who died 3 September 1849 aged 49, is «fu Antonio» in his marriage of 1825 (age 24) but signs as a witness in January–February 1826 as «fu Domenico» (reader, level 13), and the death book calls the woman who died in 1840 at house 14 «fu Domenico»; the age and the house say one man, the fathers' names say two; **not settled**, and the guess that Maria of 1840 was his sister is not supported until it is. The sacristan appears as a witness on nearly every page from 18 January 1825 («nonzolo» from 1831). The book ends its 1858 run with «Finis Anni» at no. 28 of 29 November 1858; 1859 begins in a second printed book (roll 88 item 4, 1855–1895), of which only four pages were read as a check. Told by worklist 347.

**The godparents of 7 January 1677 (FamilySearch 9R28-2JM, list index 67, right page, p. 61; read at level 13 by me, 23 November 2026).** The last entry of the page, a daughter baptised on 7 January 1677 (her own name and her father's are not in the enlarged cells), names as «compari» «il Sig.r Antº de Franceschi» and «Zuana moglie di Andrè de Franceschi q. Giacomo» (`doc`, clear; the abbreviation before Giacomo reads «q.» (quondam), probable, not compared with the scribe's other quondams). **Zuana is therefore the wife of Andrea de Franceschi q. Giacomo, and the Sig. Antonio is a separate man: the readers' earlier «Ant.o de Franceschi and his wife Joanna» of this page is corrected.** It puts the Andreas q.m Jacobi of the 1668 Pazin marriage and a Joanna together at Svetvinčenat in January 1677, which is what the Pula entry of July 1677 («de franceschi of San Vincenti») leaves open; whether that Pula man is this Andreas stays `inf`. The page's other Defranceschi entry is the baptism of 17 Calends of February 1677 (16 January) of Natalis, son of magister Baptista de Franceschi and Dominica.

**The marriage book 1855–1895 read to its end (FamilySearch 9R28-YWT, item 4, "Liber Copulatorum III", images 186–287; read by a subagent at page size with the Defranceschi cells zoomed at level 13, 24 November 2026).** The book's last entry is 31 July 1895; the next leaf is covered by a loose certificate of 1908 and the item ends with no continuation named. **Defranceschi as groom or bride (`doc`):** **3 February 1858** the sacristan Joannes De-franceschi (house 26, 26 years) married Johanna Cleva (house 24, 18), his parents Antonius De-franceschi, farmer, and Maria Bergamo; the same day his sister Veneranda (21) married the smith Antonius Subiotto. **5 February 1873** Victorius De-franceschi, smith, house 26, 28 years, son of Antonius Defranceschi and Maria née Bergamo, married Maria-Francisca Ottochian (house 51, 20); his age fits the Vittorio baptised in 1844, not the 1832 Joannes Victorius of the same parents (`inf`; register ages are loose). The sacristan's four daughters married in the book: **Maria 22 February 1879** (house 99) to Franciscus-Michael Zaratin, the schoolmaster; **Rosa 14 November 1883** (22 years) to Joannes Vernier; **Euphrosia 28 October 1885** (22) to Andreas Pliscovich; **Anna 23 November 1889** (the entry says 20, where her baptism of 1865 would give 24: not settled) to Eduardus Voran, son of the 1864 marriage of Dr Matthaeus Voran and Benedicta Bergamo. **6 August 1894 (entry 21, page 93):** Maria Defranceschi, possidens, house 95, 21 years, married Dominicus-Joseph Negri, possidens, house 188, 25; her parents read Victorius «Defram-/Defranceschi» (the m or n unsettled) and Maria-Francisca Ottochian, so she is the Maria baptised on 28 November 1873 (`inf` on name, parents and age). **Defranceschi as mother (née):** Jacopa/Jacoba De-franceschi was the mother of Dominica Crosilla (married 11 January 1855), of Johannes Crosilla (1856), of Maria Crosilla (married Vernier 1865) and of Antonius Crosilla (married Maria-Magdalena Vernier 1876); Francisca née Defranceschi, wife of Joannes Bergamo, was the mother of Dominicus (1858), Benedicta (1864), Vincentius (1868), Antonius (1873), Maria (married Aemilius Volpi 1876) and Joannes (1877); Dna Helena Sinphorosa née Defranceschi was the mother of the widower Dr Joannes Volpi, 44, married to Josepha Ferant on 16 November 1867; and Maria née Defranceschi was the mother of Joseph Dobrez, ironsmith, born at Pola, 25, who married Magdalena Ghersich on 2 June 1877. **As witness:** Joannes Defranceschi, aedituus, on nearly every page from 1855 to 1865; Antonius, Victorius and Dominicus Defranceschi «dfti Antonii» between 1868 and 1876 (what the abbreviation means is unsettled). No Kalanj or Kovačina form and no bare Franceschi occurs anywhere in the 101 images (`cover` exit 0 for both on 24 November 2026); the nil covers this item only. Unsettled and not read: ages cut at 1876 and 1877 entries, a marginal note at 1883 #14, the left page of the last leaf. The years 1855–58 were read again here and not compared line by line with the earlier item-3 reading.

**The death register 1887–1918 (FamilySearch 9R2H-DPV, "Deaths 1887-1917", images 7–139; read by a subagent at page size, hits zoomed at level 13, 24 November 2026).** The roll holds 1887 #10 to 1893 and then 1894 to 1918 #2; 1859–1886 and 1887 #1–9 are on the preceding roll, not here. Seven Defranceschi deaths (`doc`): **Dominicus, 1 year, son of Victorius, house 26, 1887 #22** (buried 10 May 1887, «scrofulosi»; the death date was not copied); **Francisca Defranceschi, widow of Joannes Bergamo, 16 October 1887** (#37, «marasmo senile», buried the 17th; a figure 79 and a figure 86 not settled between age and house); **Maria Bergamo, widow of Antonius Defranceschi, 14 February 1890** (#24, house 26, age read 84, «marasmo senile», buried the 16th); **Dna Synphorosa Defranceschi, widow of Dnus Joannes Volpi and of Andreas Vernier, 14 March 1890** (#49, house 62, age read 90, «civilis», buried the 16th), which agrees with the age 49 she gave at her marriage of 1850 and not with the 1829 of the roster; **Victorius Defranceschi, possidens, 25 May 1897** (#25, house 95, page 29 of the house book, «consumptio», age blank); **Joannes Defranceschi, son of Antonius, possidens, 13 March 1902** (#28, house 96, 69 years, «pleuritis», priest Carolus Coronica); and **Antonius Defranceschi, son of Antonius, tailor, 31 July 1903** (#83, house 95 page 29, 64 years). The age of Joannes (69) fits the Joannes Victorius baptised on 20 October 1832, which makes him the sacristan of 1849–73 (`inf`: the entry does not say sacristan); the tailor Antonius (64, b. about 1839) lives in the same house and page as Victorius, so is probably his brother (`inf`). Not found as deceased: Veneranda Subiotto, Ermenegildo, Joanna Cleva, Maria-Francisca Ottochian and Jacoba Crosilla (not a nil: the gaps below). No Kalanj or Kovačina form and no bare Franceschi in any entry (`cover` exit 0 on 24 November 2026). Gaps: 1859–1886 and 1887 #1–9 (other roll); entries under tissue or cut at the foot in 1892 (#123, #124, #137), 1893 #39–48 (dates), 1895 #44 and #82, 1896 #11, #24 and #89; the register continues in a new book not on the film.

name: Umag
lead: The hamlet of Seghetto held one De Franceschi family in 1945. Every one of Umag's 128 registers is digitised.
body: The only parish in this study with a complete digitisation — 128 of 128 books, marriages from 1602. Whatever is here can be read from anywhere.

name: Vižinada
lead: Twenty-three records from 1750, and the parish where the Kaštelir family's children were born.
body: Vižinada holds the name from **1750**, when a Mathæus De Franceschi «of Anton» is buried, and carries it to 1877 — twenty-three records of ours out of twenty-four indexed, across nine volumes opening in 1663.

It is one parish of three. **Francesco Napoleone De Franceschi was baptised here on 7 September 1818**, son of **Giulio and Maria Ceselin**; both father and son then appear in the Kaštelir register, and the next generation again at Tar. See Kaštelir for the household as a whole.

Vižinada also carries the parish of **Kaštelir** in its own books, which is why the death of Mathaeus De Franceschi in 1819 — the one entry this archive found on film 005497893 — is catalogued under Vižinada and took place at Castellier. That confusion cost a day in September and is worth keeping in view.
**And Vižinada is why Draguč looked real.** FamilySearch's place parameter returns the two parishes' record sets identically; Draguč's twenty-five entries were these.

**A Carnia lead, 17 November 2026.** On 2 August 1817 the baptism of Maria Cornea (born 29 July, daughter of Giovanni Cornea and Mattia Sartoretto; Visinada births 1792-1828, film 005497892, image 116) names a godfather: «Antonio de Franceschi di Mattio dalla Cargna, abitante in questa Parrocchia» (`doc`, the surname read at level 13 across the line break). He is a man of the Carnia living in Visinada, and a lead for the father of Maria Defrancaschi, wife of Giuseppe Illovar, who died at Pola in 1860 (`inf`, unproven: her own baptism is not found; the M section of this book is only partly read, images 100-107, 109-110, 115 and 119 onward are unread). See [Maria's page](/person/maria-di-franceschi-wife-of-giuseppe-ilovar-1863/).

Vižinada marriages read 17 November 2026 (FamilySearch 9R2Z-VZZ, 1815-1832, images 3-14, and 9R2Z-SPP, 1821-29 and 1831-88, images 3-41 plus pages 42, 47, 51, 62, 69, 123): the Defranceschi weddings are 8 May 1837 (Aloysius, tailor, widower, and Osvalda Labinaz née Dominj, p. 14), 24 February 1840 (Helena, daughter of Antonius, shoemaker, and Cattarina Benussi, house 106, and Johannes Batta Weber), the nineteenth of June 1848 (Anna, daughter of Julius, tailor, and Maria Cedelini, and Johannes Baichin), 24 November 1852 (Maria, daughter of the late Antonius, and Josephus Dobrez, a sailor turned soldier) and 11 February 1888 (Emmanuel, shoemaker, son of Franciscus, shoemaker, and Maria Stefanutti, and Oliva Saravallo); a Defranceschi mother appears in 1834 (Catarina née Defranceschi, mother of the groom Johannes Miccoli). No Defranceschi wedding appears in the 1815-34 pages read, apart from a witness: Aloysius De Franceschi, tailor, on 6 August 1821 (9R2Z-SPP image 6; reader's reading, 'de Carnea[?]' unsettled). Not walked: marriages after 1834 apart from the pages named, and the 1663-1822 book.

At Vižinada in Istria the Carnia godfather of 2 August 1817, «Antonio de Franceschi di Mattio dalla Cargna», is not a stranger: he is Antonio, son of the late Matteo De Franceschi, «oriundo dalla Carnia», who on 16 May 1822 baptised in the Vižinada register a daughter Elena by Francesca nata Carli (Vižinada births 1792-1828, FamilySearch 9R2Z-FMH, image 51 right page, p. 83; `doc`, the surname, «oriundo dalla Carnia» and «Carli» read on the plate at 1.5×; that he is the godfather of 1817 is `inf`, on the given name, the father's name and the origin within five years in one parish). He belongs to a family of Carnia people in Vižinada and Kaštelir (Castellier): his father Mattio (a shoemaker from the Carnia who died at Kaštelir on 6 August 1819, `doc` on the page read earlier that day by this archive) and his mother Anna née Fajolli (named in the marriage of her son Aloysius, below), and brothers Aloysius, a tailor, who married the widow Osvalda Labinaz née Dominj at Vižinada on 8 May 1837 (parents «Matheus Defranceschi» and «Anna Fajolli», age 47; marriage book 9R2Z-SPP image 47; `doc`), and Giulio (Julius), a tailor, father of Francesco Naplone (baptised 7 September 1818 at Vižinada to Giulio De Franceschi and Maria née Ceselin 'of Venice', 9R2Z-FMH image 56; `doc`) and of Anna (m. Giovanni Baichin, the nineteenth of June 1848, 9R2Z-SPP image 62, `doc`). The brothers' trades (shoemaker for Mattio and Antonio, tailor for Aloysius and Julius) run through the family. Antonio's later life is in the marriage book: «Antonius Defranceschi, sutor» and Cattarina née Benussi are the parents of Helena (aged 18, m. Johannes Batta Weber, 24 February 1840, house 106) and of Maria (aged 20, m. Josephus Dobrez, 24 November 1852, when Antonio was dead, 9R2Z-SPP images 51 and 69; `doc`). That Helena of 1840 is the Elena of 1822 is `inf` (age), and the two registers give different mothers (Francesca Carli in 1822, Cattarina Benussi in 1840 and 1852): a second marriage is the likely reading, not shown. The marriage of Antonio is not in the Vižinada marriage books for 1815-1834 (read for the names; a gap of Mar 1829-Dec 1830 is on no film) and no Vižinada death book after 1831 is online. No link to the Pola woman Maria Defrancaschi (wife of Giuseppe Illovar) is shown by any of this.
**Read 17 November 2026.** On 24 November 1852 Joseph Dobrez married Maria Defranceschi (doc; FamilySearch 9R2Z-SPP, image 69), the parents of the ironsmith Giuseppe Dobrez born 1852.

**Vižinada baptisms, the Maria entries of 1807–1815, read 22 November 2026 (FamilySearch 9R2Z-FMH, the M section of the baptism book 1792–1828; whole spreads of viewer images 110, 113 and 115, both pages displayed and read entry by entry, beside the images 111, 112, 114 and 116–118 of 17 November): no child of a father or mother Defranceschi, De Franceschi or Defrancaschi, and no Tintori, in the entries of 6 February 1807 to 6 March 1808 (image 110), of the end of October 1810 and 2 December 1810 to 31 May 1812 (image 113, which carries p. 231) or of 15 July 1813 to 9 August 1815 (image 115, pp. 234–235).** The Maria of the Pola death entry (about 1810 from the age of 50, 1817 from the census) is therefore **not baptised under M at Vižinada in these years** as far as these spreads go (`doc` for what the entries say). **The section is arranged by the child's first letter**, so a baptism under another first name (Marianna), at Kaštelir (its own book, 9R26-166; the 9R2Z-6TB sometimes named for it is Vižinada births 1815–1830) or in another parish is not excluded. *Not opened:* image 109 (fetched, not read), images 100–107 and 119 onward, and the join between images 112 and 113 (September–October 1810) was not checked across. Terms tried: Defranceschi, Defranceski, Defrančeski, Deffranceschi, Defranca, Defrancaschi, Defranceschy, Defrancesci, Defrancheski, Defranci, Defranzeschi, Defranzesi, di Franceschi, Franceski, Francetchi, Franchessi (`cover` exits 0); Tintori. Every cell begun Fran-, De Fran- or Di Fran- was looked for and none stands; no near-name of the kind was seen.

**Vižinada baptisms 1815–1830 (FamilySearch 9R2Z-6TB, roll 94 item 2), viewer images 4–45 read 24 Nov 2026 (23 October 1815 to 13 September 1827; images 45–75 are told in the next paragraph).** A chronological register (date, house, baptiser, child, father, mother, godparents), not sorted by initial. Every cell of those pages was read at page size and every De Franceschi cell zoomed to level 13, except two cells on image 44. **The tailors' children, read on the plate (`doc`).** Antonio, a tailor «q.m Mathei De Franceschi» (a «Carnicus» in 1822): Helena, baptised 16 May 1822 (house 59; mother Francisca Carli; image 26, p. 45), Antonius Matheus, born 1 September 1823 (house 26; mother Catharina De Carli; image 30, p. 53), Alysius Augustinus, born «heri» in 1825 (entry 25, p. 67, month cut; image 37) and Aloysius, born 22 September 1826 (p. 77, image 42; the surname ending cramped, probable, godparents Barthel(omeus) Sabaz and Maria ux. Aloysii Valentich). The Aloysius of 1826 follows the child of 1825 by a year, so he is a second child of the name, not the same one. Julius, a tailor «q.m Mathei», and Maria Ceselin (daughter of the late Petrus): Petrus, born 14 July 1816 (p. 3, house 27, image 5), Franciscus Napoleon, 5 September 1818 (already told above) and Anna Marina, born at midnight on 5 March 1821 (p. 37, house 26, image 22); the Anna of the 1848 wedding to Baichin is very probably this child (`inf`). **Antonio as godfather** («Antonius fil. Mathei De Franciscis/De Franceschi»): 2 August 1817, 3 March 1819 and 27 February 1825 (the last with Dna Paulina Peruta née Fachinetti; the child's parents are not Defranceschi). **One thing the pages show and nobody has settled:** Antonio's wife is Carli in 1822–1826 and Benussi in the marriage entries of 1840 and 1852 (told above); a second wife, or a different clerk's reading, is not decided here. **For Maria, wife of Giuseppe Ilovar (b. about 1810, d. at Pula 1860):** this volume opens in October 1815, so a baptism of about 1810 cannot be in it, and no Maria daughter of an Antonio and no Ilovar or Tintori is in the pages read. Her baptism is still not found. **Not a nil for the volume:** no Kalanj or Kovačina form and no other Defranceschi form was seen in images 4–45; images 45–75 are read in the next paragraph. Not counted: Calauz (a by-name of the Beacovich and Sepich families), Caliganich, Covaz, Cociancich, Franza, Franzo-, Fachinetti, Flanch.

**Vižinada baptisms 1815–1830, second half (FamilySearch 9R2Z-6TB, roll 94 item 2, viewer images 45–75), read 24 November 2026 once the sign-in was restored; the roll is now read to its end.** Images 44–52 (left page) finish the Vižinada book (pp. 82–98, 18 May 1827 to the end of 1830; its last page says «Vide seq. in libro novo baptizatorum», the new book being 9R2Z-C6K, told next). **From the right-hand page of image 52 a second book starts on the same roll: the baptism book of the filial curacy of Kaštelir** («Liber Baptizatorum in Ecclesia Curata Castellier»; curate D. Gregorius Baichin, later D. Antonius Baichin), its p. 1 dated 5 October 1815 and its last entry 29 December 1830 («Seguitur Annus 1831», image 74); image 75 is the end-of-item slate. So the item holds **two books, and the Kaštelir baptisms of 1815–1830 are on this roll** (told on [the Kaštelir page](/places/kastelir/)); the heading of the paragraph above, «Vižinada baptisms 1815–1830», named only the first. Every page of images 44–74 was read at page size and every De Franceschi cell zoomed to level 13. **One child of Antonio's (`doc`):** Franciscus Antonius, born 13 June 1828 («heri», 1 a.m.) and baptised the 14th, house 26 (p. 89, image 48; the page follows p. 88 of 1828, the year digit of its first entry is cramped); father «Antonius q.m Mathei De Franceschi, Sartor», mother «Catharina Carli», godparents Joannes, son of Natalis Fattor, and Maria Missana, midwife Theresia Urbino. It is the last entry that writes Antonio's wife Carli; the next entries of her name write Benussi (below). **Aloysius, the third tailor of the name, is a godfather five times at Kaštelir (`doc`):** «Aloysius De Franceschi q.m Mathei», Sartor, on 15 May 1822 (p. 20, house 36), 3 October 1822 (p. 21, house 7), 3 February 1824 (p. 26, house 40, the word after the name unsettled), 22 January 1825 (p. 29) and 25 November 1828 (p. 42, house 73, where the line reads «commorans ibi»: living there). He is not a father in these pages. **Julius's daughter Catharina** is baptised at Kaštelir on 9 November 1829 (told on [Kaštelir](/places/kastelir/)). **Not found:** any other child of Antonio or Julius between September 1827 and the end of 1830, any child of Aloysius, and any other Defranceschi household. **Nil for images 44–74, not for the volume:** none of the Kalanj forms (Kalain, Kalanj, Kallayn, Callain, Callajn, Callayn, Callein, Kalagnia, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalayn, Kalianj, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Kallanij, Kallanj, Kallein, Kalan, Calan), none of the Kovačina forms (Kovacina, Kovačina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich), no Tintori, Ilovar or Illovar, and no Defranceschi form beyond the family's own; `cover` exit 0 for Defranceschi, Kalanj and Kovačina on 24 November 2026. Near-names, not counted: «Francaes» (a godmother, 2 September 1827, zoomed: no -sch-), «Calagnia» (a word in the Julius entry of 1829, read as a place, unsettled; written with a C and not a form the Atlas holds), Cociancich, Labinaz, Covaz, Legovich. **Unsettled:** the word after the name in the entry of 3 February 1824; the day of birth in the entry of 9 November 1829.

**Vižinada baptisms 1831–1866, the first 203 pages (FamilySearch 9R2Z-C6K, «Matična knjiga rođenih 1831–1886», roll 94 item 3, list images 4–107 of 185), read 24 November 2026.** One book for Vižinada (Vicinatus) and Kaštelir (Castelier): Vicinatus pp. 1–4 for 1831, then interleaved by date to 1841, then separate runs of pages with the parish written at the top right (from about p. 94), and from about p. 148 no parish written at all, so the parish of pp. 148–203 is judged by house numbers (houses 103, 106 and 136 are Vižinada). Every page of pp. 1–203 was read at page size (pp. 153 and 169 through their second exposures, images 81 and 90), 33 of the De Franceschi cells were zoomed to level 13 and two were read at page size only; **pp. 204–357 (1867–1886) are unread.** **Antonio's household, houses 103 and 106 (`doc`):** Antonio, «q. Mat., Sator» (also written Mercator), and «Cattarina na Benussi» have Maria, born 15 January 1832 (p. 6, house 103), Josephus, born 20 May 1834 (p. 19, house 103) and Mathias, born 13 August 1839 (p. 47, house 106). **The two surnames of one wife are now bracketed:** she is «Carli» on 14 June 1828 (above), «Catharina Defranceschi» stands with Antonio as godparents on 31 January 1831 (p. 1, house 196) and on 8 May 1831 (p. 2, house 212), and the mother is «Cattarina na Benussi» by 15 January 1832; Antonio is also a godfather at pp. 12, 23, 25, 35 and 42 in 1833–38. Carli became Benussi between June 1828 and January 1832; the pages do not say whether this is a second wife or two names for one woman (the first name is the same), and nothing is decided here. **His daughters (`doc`):** *Helena* is the mother «Helena ná Defrances[chi]» (the last letters hidden under the column rule) of Antonius, born 14 February 1842 at house 106, Antonio's own house, whose father is Johannes Baptista Weber (trade word unsettled): the Weber wedding of 1840 told above. *Anna* is the mother «Anna ná Defrances-chi» of Birgitta Elisa, baptised 20 February 1849 (p. 106, house 40), whose father Johannes Baichin Parutta is a woodworker («fab. lign.»): the Baichin wedding of 1848 told above; an «Anna Defranceschj (Sator)» is godmother on 10 August 1844 (p. 77, house 94). *Maria* is the mother «Maria ná Defrances-chi» of the children of Josephus Dobrez, a sailor («nauta»), at house 136: Josephus, baptised 4 January 1852 (p. 120), Catharina, entered at the foot of p. 132 as «September 8» (1853) late, under a decree of 3 February 1879, and Antonius, born 30 March and baptised 1 April 1855 (p. 139). **Maria, born 15 January 1832, is very probably this Maria (`inf`):** the Dobrez wedding of 24 November 1852 calls the bride a daughter of the late Antonius, and no other daughter Maria of an Antonio is in these pages. Two things stay open: the baptism of 4 January 1852 comes before that wedding (the legitimacy cell was not read), and Catharina's entry of 1853 stands on a page headed Vicinatus at house 136, not at Kaštelir as the index placed it. **Franciscus «qdam Antonii», shoemaker, and Maria Stefanutti, house 136 (`doc`):** Emanuel Antonius, born 25 December 1859 and baptised 1 January 1860 by D. Michael Tomsich (p. 162), father «De Franceschi Franciscus qm. Antonii Sutor», mother «Maria n. Steffanutti», godparents Franciscus Prodam and Maria Fachinetti; and Catharina Maria, born 15 August 1864 (p. 188). The couple stand as godparents six times in 1862–66 (19 March 1862, 19 January 1864, 2 August 1864, March 1865, 20 August 1865 and, at page size only, 17 April 1866). Emanuel's father is therefore **Antonius' son Franciscus, not a son of Julius**; the Emmanuel of the wedding of 11 February 1888 (told above) is this child, and the margin of Oliva Saraval's baptism (25 March 1866, p. 199) repeats the wedding in a later hand, read at page size only. Franciscus Antonius born 1828 is the obvious candidate for this Franciscus (`inf`; no entry says so). **Others, godparents only:** Helena (1836, 1839), Osvalda, «Sator» (24 April 1838, at Kaštelir), Anna (1844), Julius, «Sator», at Kaštelir on 5 October 1851 (the last sighting before his burial of 1854), a Franciscus, tailor, at Kaštelir on 13 August 1852 and 1 June 1856 and, a shoemaker, on 2 August 1857; the entries do not say which Franciscus. **Not found in pp. 1–203:** the Franciscus q.m Julii of Kaštelir and his children Joannes Aloysius (1858) and Josephus (1862) (the Kaštelir books 9R26-166 are the other place to look), a later child of Julius and Maria Ceselin, a child of Aloysius, any Dobrez child after 1855. **Nil for pp. 1–203, not for the volume:** none of the Kalanj forms (the twenty-one of the paragraph above), none of the Kovačina forms (the seven above), no Tintori, Ilovar or Illovar, and no Defranceschi form beyond the family's own; `cover` exit 0 for Defranceschi, Kalanj and Kovačina on 24 November 2026. Near-names, not counted: the **Ritossa by-name Calaus / Calanz / Kalanž**, told on [the Kalanj page](/kalanj/); «Maria n. Kovacic» (p. 184, zoomed: -ić, not -ina); Smoglian, Zamolo, Fachinetti, Prodam, Moriconi, Sabbaz, Baichin, Legovich, Beacovich, Labinaz, Filipsich, Juliani, Casali, Deotto, Patelli, Balanzin. **Unsettled:** Weber's trade word and the hidden end of «Defrances…» (p. 62); faint word endings of three entries of 1855–57; the word under «Civ. possid.» of 19 March 1862; the day figure of the entry of March 1865; the two cells of image 105 (p. 199) not zoomed, because a second 401 stopped the reading there: «Franciscus Defranceski et uxor ejus Maria», 17 April 1866, whose ending is unsettled, and the margin note «nupta 11-2-1888 [E]manueli Defranceschi».

name: Vodnjan
lead: Twelve Defranceschi families in 1945, and — since 9 September 2026 — five documented generations behind them. The best-attested cluster in southern Istria, read out of a register nobody has indexed.
body: The 1945 cadastre counts twelve Defranceschi families at Vodnjan, against two at Gologorica and one at Gračišće. For most of this archive's life that was all it knew, and the twelve households were listed as its second open question.

They are not open any more. The parish books of Dignano — FamilySearch catalogue item koha:963267 — hold baptisms from 1815, marriages 1815–1884 and deaths to 1893. The baptism register, read through for this page on 23 November 2026 (below), names the family in about 250 entries between 1815 and 1867. **The marriage register has never been indexed by anybody**, and was read here opening by opening.

What came out of it: a line five generations deep, from a **Pietro** standing behind a marriage of the 1770s, through **Gio. Maria De Franceschi and Michiela Zambaletta**, to their children **Pietro, Cristoforo and Veniera** and the grandchildren married off in the 1820s. A **second, separate line** descending from a Domenico. **Four women of the name married out before the books open** — Domenica, Antonia Maria, Lucia and Veniera — recoverable only because their daughters' weddings named their mothers. And one household of three brothers, all «di Giuseppe»: **Don Stefano the priest**, who witnessed sixteen weddings under the parroco Giovanni Tromba, and **Pietro the ploughman and Cristoforo the weaver**, who signed the same book with a cross.

⭐⭐ **Domenica Manzin, and the two Vodnjan books of 1815–1833 read for her parents (16 November 2026).** [Domenica Manzin](/person/domenica-manzin-vodnjan/) is known as the mother of Bonetta, who married on **19 November 1823** (marriage book p. 40, entry 34, house 654; FamilySearch 9R2D-927, image 192 left, read on the page): the bride is «del fu Pietro De Franceschi q.m Domco e Domenica Manzin q.m Domco giugali», aged 23, and the groom is a **Biasiol**, son of Matteo Biasiol q.m Antonio and Maria Rotta (this archive had told him as a Marich and the house as 684: [corrected](/corrections/)); one of the witnesses is Fabiano Bandovicchio, a shoemaker (`doc`). **So her father was a Domenico Manzin, dead by 1823, and her husband Pietro De Franceschi q.m Domenico was dead by then too.** Neither book gives her parents. The **death book 1815–1833** (181 pages, 4 October 1815 to 31 December 1833, every page seen) holds **no death of Pietro De Franceschi q.m Domenico, none of Domenica Manzin as his widow and none of Maria Luigia Manzin**, the second Manzin wife of the generation (`doc`; so Pietro died before October 1815 or was buried elsewhere). The **marriage book 1815–1830** (pp. 1–70) holds no marriage of a Domenica Manzin at all (`doc`). What the two books do give is a **Domenica Manzin q.m Domenico who was the wife of Giovanni Ive q.m Antonio** when he died on 20 February 1821 (house 389), and **the mother, with the late Giovanni Ive, of Anna, aged 20, who married Antonio Rotta on 25 August 1824** (p. 43, entry 24, house 406); and a **Domenica Manzin q.m Domenico who was the second-vows wife of Sebastiano Bandovicchio q.m Fabiano** when he died on 10 November 1826 (house 48) (`doc`, entries read at the page; the death entries do not state her age). **That may be one woman married three times — to Pietro De Franceschi (Bonetta, born about 1800), to Giovanni Ive (Anna, born about 1804) and to Bandovicchio — because the name and the father's name are the same and the daughters' ages fit (`inf`, not proved: Manzin is a common name at Vodnjan and Domenico a common father's name).** Her marriages to Pietro (about 1799) and to Ive (about 1802–04) fall before the book begins in October 1815; the marriage to Bandovicchio, between 1821 and 1826, is in neither book. Other Manzin women «q.m Domenico» of the same town (Lucia, Vita, Maria, Vincenza, Pasqua, Antonia, Bonetta, Biaggia, Veniera and the Maria Luigia Manzin above) are named in the same books, and nothing says which of them, if any, were her sisters. **Not on the records read:** her own baptism or marriage to Pietro (the Vodnjan books on FamilySearch begin in 1815), her mother, and the Bandovicchio wedding. *Typed:* Manzin, Manzini, Mancin, Mancini. Death book after December 1833 (FamilySearch 9R2H-GPF, 1834–1893, on roll 97) not opened.

⭐ **The Vodnjan death book of 1834–1843 (Liber Septimus Defunctorum, FamilySearch 9R2H-GPF, images 0–79 of 629, 8 January 1834 to 19 November 1843), read for Domenica Manzin on 16 November 2026: no entry calls anyone «widow of Pietro De Franceschi», and one Domenica Manzin fits her age and her father.** On **21 October 1841**, house 48, the book enters «**Domenica Manzin fu Domenico, moglie in 2.do voto di Sebastiano Bendovicchio fu Fabiano**», female, **79**, dead of diarrhoea, buried the next evening by the doctor's order (image 66, p. 115 right, entry 135; read by a reader and again by this session on the page; `doc` for the entry). Born about 1762, she could be the mother of Bonetta (born about 1800), and her father is a Domenico: that she is **the** Domenica is **`inf` only**, because the entry does not say *vedova*, Pietro or De Franceschi. One more thread points the same way: a **Fabiano Bandovicchio**, shoemaker, witnessed Bonetta's wedding in 1823, and this husband is a Sebastiano *fu Fabiano* (`inf`). **A tension is left open:** the 1815–1833 death book above has a Sebastiano Bandovicchio dying in 1826, and a woman dying in 1841 who is still «moglie» of a Sebastiano would be called *vedova* if he were that man; two Sebastianos, or an unusual entry, are both possible. A second Domenica Manzin (13 September 1843, «fu Andrea», wife of a Bergamasco, 74) is **not** her. **No death of Bonetta herself, of Nicolò Giacomo Biasiol, or of a Pietro or Giovanni De Franceschi named as her son** is in these ten years. Several De Franceschi are entered as «fu Pietro» (Giovanni, 81, on 1 February 1839; Domenico, 71, on 15 July 1843; Michiella, wife of Andrea Palin, dead by September 1840): **a Pietro with several children, not shown to be hers, and no relationship is claimed.** *Read at page size with the Atlas `cover` for Defranceschi (nineteen forms) exiting 0; Manzin and Biasiol are not in the catalogue and were searched as written plus Manzini, Mancin, Mansin, Menzin, Manzan and Biasiolo.* **Left:** the Vodnjan marriage book from 1831 for Sebastiano Bendovicchio and Domenica (it would name her first husband), and images 80–628 of this volume (deaths from November 1843 to 1893).

The town's church paperwork ran to the **Ordinariate of Pola**; the banns could be waived by the **Imperial-Royal Circle Captaincy**. Weddings involving Vodnjan people were also held at **Šišan** and **Svetvinčenat**, and a «Matt.o de Franceschi da Dignano» was buried at **Rovinj** in 1728 — the same formula, ninety-six years apart, naming the town only from outside it.

**And the town those households lived in is gone.** Forebears' surname counts for Vodnjan, as of 2014, give the ten commonest names as **Hrelja 208, Macan 146, Šverko 110, Drandić 96, Vitasović 96, Lukić 81, Červar 80, Bliznac 76, Diminić 76, Pereša 76** — one person in thirty-one at Vodnjan is a Hrelja. **Not one of the families this archive read out of the town's own registers is among them.** Not Francin, Malusà, Vellico, Gorlato, Giachin, Ferrarese, Demarin, Biasiol, Damiani, Zanghirella, Codacovich, Moscheni, Forlani or Tromba — the names that fill the baptisms, marriages and deaths of the 1810s to the 1840s, and that this site has spent weeks reading one entry at a time. And no Defranceschi. The 1945 cadastre counted **twelve Defranceschi families here**, the largest concentration anywhere. What the surname list records is the **esodo** — the departure of the Italian-speaking population of Istria after 1945 and the resettlement that followed — visible as an almost complete replacement of a town's family names inside a single lifetime. It is also the plainest answer to a question this archive keeps asking: why a surname documented in one town for five generations has almost no living trace there. The list is the ten commonest names only — an old surname surviving at rank fifteen would not show

**Read 17 November 2026, the Vodnjan marriage book (9R2D-927) from 1830 to February 1838 (pp. 70-113).** It holds no marriage of a Domenica Manzin to a Pietro De Franceschi and none of Sebastiano Bendovicchio to a Manzin; the only De Franceschi name in it is Don Stefano Defranceschi, priest, witness at the wedding of Angelo Gorlato and Maria Delzotto on 3 December 1837 (p. 113, entry 43, `doc`). One caution for the Manzin question: on 13 February 1836 (p. 102, entry 7) a Domenica Manzin q.m Domenico, *widow of Giovanni Ive*, married again, with twin daughters born about 1813, so the Domenica Manzin who died on 21 October 1841 (death book, image 66) may be that widow and not Pietro De Franceschi's wife (`inf`; do not merge on the name). Not yet read: the marriage book after February 1838 and the death book from image 80.

**Read 17 November 2026, the Vodnjan marriage book from 1838 to 1847 (9R2D-927, pp. 114-158) and the death books from 1843 to March 1856 (9R2H-GPF, images 80-189: the 1834-49 book to its end in December 1849, then the 1850-60 book), for the parents of Domenica Manzin.** Her marriage to a Bendovicchio is not in the marriage book, nor is a marriage of a son of Pietro and Domenica, and no Bonetta or Nicolo Giacomo Biasiol dies in these years. One entry is new: on 8 September 1848, at house 139, Domenica, widow of Giovanni Ive q.m Antonio, aged 70, was buried (`doc`). If she is the Domenica Manzin q.m Domenico who was Ive's wife in the 1815-33 books (`inf`), she was born about 1778 and cannot also be the Domenica Manzin aged 79 buried on 21 October 1841 as the wife in second vows of a Bendovicchio. The De Franceschi q. Pietro of these books (Domenico d. 1851 and four more) belong to a Pietro and a Maria Malusa, not to Domenica Manzin (`inf`). The pages were read by sub-readers from 1400-pixel images with the name cells enlarged two to three times, not at level 13, and are not walked: deaths from 27 March 1856 are unread; the marriages from 24 November 1847 to 1884 were read on 22 November 2026 (next paragraph). The books before 1815 are not on FamilySearch.

**The Vodnjan marriage books from November 1847 to 1884 (FamilySearch 9R2D-927, images 261-466, read 22 November 2026), for the parents of Domenica Manzin and for every Defranceschi cell.** The two books (1848-1867, Inv. br. 546, and 1867-1884, Inv. br. 547) were read opening by opening, left and right page, by sub-readers from 1400-pixel images with the name cells enlarged; I re-read at level 13 the cells that carry the argument (`doc`): 17 February 1849 (image 272, entry 13), where the bride Maria Biasiol's mother is «Bonetta Defranceschi, q. Piero» and her father Nicolò Giacomo Biasiol q. Matteo, and 24 February 1873 (image 401, entry 23), Bonna Defranceschi's father Stephanus Defranceschi and mother Mathza Delcaro. The rest of the cells below stand on the readers' transcription (`doc` as read, not yet at level 13). **No Kovačina and no Kalanj in either book**; two cells of 1877 (entry 6, a groom «Co?venick» of Pola, and entry 33, a mother «Co?vaug») were read as Cov- but not settled, and are not counted. **Domenica Manzin's parents are not in them**: no marriage of a Domenica Manzin, no Sebastiano Bendovicchio. What the books do add is the family of Pietro's children (the Defranceschi q. Piero of the entries): on 10 February 1849 (entry 6, house 48) **Pasqua Defranceschi**, 24, daughter of Domenico Defranceschi q. Piero and Zacchera Cerlon q. Francesco, married Angiolo Ferrarese; Domenica of the same parents (house 48) married Fioretto Biasiol in February 1853 (entry 8) and Maria (house 66) Lorenzo Gorlato on 2 December 1854 (entry 40). **House 48 is the house where the Domenica Manzin buried on 21 October 1841 lived** (death book, image 66); Domenico q. Piero and Bonetta q. Piero are both «q. Piero», and this supports, and does not prove, that she is Pietro's widow and the mother of Bonetta (`inf`). Bonetta's own daughter Maria Biasiol is the bride of 17 February 1849, so Bonetta was alive then. Other households read: Stefano q. Domenico and Bonetta Vellico's son Domenico-Giovanni Antonio married Mattea Delcarro on 2 May 1849 (house 725); Giovanni Maria q. Pietro and Lucia Bonaprin's son Pietro (a sergeant's son of the Wimpffen regiment) married on 4 June 1852 and Giovanni on 25 November 1854 (Pasqua Manzin, house 291), and their daughter Veneranda, widow of Antonio Demarin, married Laurentius Biasiol on 21 September 1867 and is the Veneranda Defranceschi named as mother of the Demarin grooms of 1874, 1877 and 1879 (`inf`); the twin brides Teresa Domenica and Domenica Michiela Giovanna, 30, daughters of Pietro q. Giuseppe and Maria Malusa (26 February 1851); Michela q. Cristoforo, mother of Domenico Vellico (1858) and of Bonetta Vellico (1852). From 1873 the name is on the right-hand page only as a mother or as a bride: Lucia Defranceschi is the mother of the Forlani of house 791 (1873, 1878) and, in a second place, of the Damiani brides of house 681 (1875, 1879); a Michaela, a Francisca, a Blancha, a Dominica and a Pascha are mothers of Dellico, Bergamo, Barsisich, Codacovich and Ferrarese grooms (1877-79); Maria Defranceschi, dead by 1882, was the wife of Laurentius Gorlato of house 66, widower of a Maria Defranceschi on 4 March 1867 (`inf`). **Stephanus Defranceschi's daughter Bonna (1873) and Dominicus Defranceschi's daughter Veneranda (21 November 1883) share a house, 481, and a mother's surname, Delcaro:** the first says Stephanus and the second Dominicus for the father, which is unsettled and is not merged (`inf`). **The only Defranceschi groom in the two books is Joannes Maria De Franceschi, 23, of house 495, son of Stephanus Defranceschi and Maria Fortunato, who married Dominica Pinzan on 23 November 1881** (image 452, entry 70). A Dominica «Defranuschi», mother of Matthaeus Biasiol (20 February 1884, image 463), reads -nu- for -ce- and is counted only as inferred. Not walked: the readers worked from 1400-pixel images; entries 31-34 of 1881 are not on image 448 (a repaired page), entry 31 of 1850 is blank and entry 32 is on no image, entry 13 of 1857 is on no image, and the 1867-1884 book's unnumbered Rovinj entry of 24 October 1883 is a late addition. The last page of the book is image 466 (p. 169, 1884, «Finis anni Domini 1884»); image 467 is the end-of-item slate. House 654 and 684 occur only in entries that are not Defranceschi ones (1859 no. 20, 1873 nos. 20-21). The deaths book 1815-1833 follows on the same roll.

**Three more FamilySearch volumes filed under Vodnjan are not parish books, and hold nothing of the three names (read 23 November 2026).** They are the books of the Austrian war-navy hospitals: 9R2Z-KXS, the baptism book of the naval branch hospital at Dignano, 1860-1894 (16 images, about 32 entries, German, fathers naval officers and hospital staff); 9R2C-W3B, the death register of the Dignano naval hospital, 1858-1894 (66 images, printed German forms, soldiers and sailors, a few officers' wives and children); and 9R2C-W35, the death register of the Pula naval hospital's pastoral care, 1862-1874 (193 images, to 24 November 1874). They carry no house numbers and no parents for the dead, so a Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj could stand in them only as the deceased or as a named father or husband. **None does.** Every name cell was read at page size (none zoomed) and checked against every same, attested and rule form of the three families that the Atlas catalogue lists (`cover` exit 0 for all three on 23 November 2026); near-names seen and not counted include a bare Catharina Franceschi born in Venice (1864 baptism, the mother's mother), Kallich/Ballich, Kalassurich, Colanovic and the Kovačić soldiers. **A nil here is a nil for these three naval books and says nothing about the town's parish books**, whose baptisms 1860-1894 and deaths 1858-1894 are not on these rolls. One Manzin appears and no link to Domenica Manzin is claimed: Elisabeth, wife of the corporal Anton Ballich, daughter of Mathäus Manzin and Dominika Chersin of Fasana, baptised her children Anton Josef (September 1865) and Franz (23 January 1868) in the naval hospital (9R2Z-KXS images 5-6). Two men born in places this archive follows appear among the dead of 1872 without any known tie: Johann Vdovičić, arsenal worker born at Gologorica (23 August 1872), and Johann Scattaro born at S. Vincenti (31 July 1872). The Dignano town books still to be read are the baptisms 1815-1866 (9R2Z-GP5) and the deaths 1856-1893 (9R2H-GPF, images 190-628).

⭐⭐ **The Vodnjan death book of 1856–1893 (9R2H-GPF images 190–628), read on 23 November 2026 for every Defranceschi cell.** The town parish's death registers run on from where the paragraph above stopped (March 1856): the 1850–60 book (images 190–223), then the 1860–93 book (Libro IX; images 232–623, ending «finis hujus Libri N. IX» with the entry of 31 December 1893, then a title slate for «Matična knjiga umrlih 1860–1893, item 3», the end-of-roll target and the sign-off sheet of roll 97, which continues on roll 98). Every opening of images 190–628 was read by sub-readers at page size, two jpgs a time, with the name cells enlarged two times (that enlarges the 1400-pixel image and adds no detail; it is not level 13), and I looked again at three of the doubtful cells (1876 no. 114, image 446 left, image 301 right). About **ninety cells** carry the name, in the deceased's cell, as the mother or father of a dead child, or as the spouse; two more are a word the scribe struck out. **No Kovačina and no Kalanj form in any cell of the 439 images** (typed: the Defranceschi, Kalanj and Kovačina forms of the Atlas, `cover` exit 0 on 23 November 2026; near-names seen and not counted: Francin, Franolich, Franzin, Franettich, Fraccanetto, Mazzan, Desanti, Decanova, Dorliguzzo, a bare «Rosa Franceschi» of 1868 at house 1, Skovarich). **Not walked:** the readers could not zoom; the entries under repair strips and the entry numbers cut by the gutter on some right-hand pages are named in the rows; the Manzin lists of images 286–317 and 350–381 were written after a reader's context was reset and are first passes, so **no nil is claimed for a Domenica Manzin in those two stretches** (the other stretches' readers listed every Manzin cell, and none is the Domenica Manzin of the wife of Pietro De Franceschi, who would in any case have been born about 1778 and is searched in the earlier books). Cells settled only at page size, and not enlarged by me: the ending of «Defranceski/-schi» on image 446 left (entry 186, 1879), and «Michaela n. Defrances[…]» on image 301 right (entry 186, 1867), which runs into the column rule.

**The Defranceschi households of the town in these books, as the death entries write them** (`doc` for the entry, `inf` for each link between entries; house numbers are old/new from 1858):

- **House 481/406, the family of Stefano q. Domenico.** Stefano De Franceschi «dei furono Domenico e Veneranda De Rocchi», widower of Bonetta Vellico, died 9 October 1857 aged 65; his daughter **Martina**, unmarried, 6 July 1859 aged 35 (parents «Stefano e Bonetta Vellico»). Three children of **Domenico Giovanni q. Stefano and Mattea Del Carro q. Veniero** died in 1858: Pietro (5 June, 2 months), Stefano (18 October) and Veniero (31 October), and an unnumbered line at the foot of a page of 26 June 1859 names another Pietro of the same parents (age and date probable only).
- **House 478 (new 432; from 1869 the household is also at 495), Stefano and Maria Francin.** «Stefano Matteo De Franceschi fu Pietro d° Chievaro» and Maria Francin di Giuseppe lose Giuseppe (23 May 1858, 40 days) and Pietro (16 July 1858, 18 months); later entries give the father as «Stephanus» and the mother Francin or, in 1869, 1871 and 1884, **Forlanichio**: Philomena (22 September 1868), Lucia (23 March 1869), Christophorus (14 October 1870), Matthaeus (21 January 1871, in childbirth), Antonius (20 March 1871), Petrus (13 July 1871, aged 12, thrown from a horse), a Mathea (17 October 1872), Petrus (9 August 1874, 28 days), Dominica (22 May 1883, aged 18) and Joseph (24 September 1884, house corrected 478 to 495). Whether Francin and Forlanichio are two wives or one woman under two names is **not settled** (the baptism book, below, writes two men called Stefano, each with a wife of one of the two names): the death of «Stephanus Defranceschi q. Petri, husband (1850) of Maria Francin» on 14 March 1893, aged 71, at house 526, names Francin («q. Petri» is a correction over a struck word: probable). Two older members of the house die in 1873 at 478/432: **Christophorus Defranceschi q. Josephi, unmarried weaver, 13 April, aged 77**, and **Maria née Malusà, widow of Petrus Defranceschi q. Josephi, 16 October, aged 91**; «Joseph Stephanus De-franceschi q. Petri et q. Mariae Malusà», 56, died 7 August 1863 at house 178 or 478 (the digit is unsettled). By name and trade these are the household of the three brothers «di Giuseppe» (the weaver Cristoforo, the ploughman Pietro) of the marriage books, and the sons of Pietro and Maria Malusà (`inf`). In 1892–93 the name is also at house 526: Stephanus (16 April 1892, 2½ years; parents Josephus and Lucia Dellico), then Stephanus aged 71 above.
- **House 66, Gorlato.** **Maria Defranceschi q. Domenico**, wife (1854) of Laurentius Gorlato q. Blasii, loses Domenico (31 December 1859), a stillborn Francesco (1 June 1861), Veneranda (6 August 1863, the mother written «Dominica»), Dominicus (26 September 1864 and again 14 September 1866) and dies herself on 28 November 1866 aged 33; a Veneranda Gorlato «Laurentii et Mariae Defranceschi» of 13 September 1875 shows a mother of the same name nine years later (second wife or a different reading: not settled). Beside it, **house 167, Florus Biasiol and Dominica Defranceschi**: Antonius (21 June 1861, 8 months; 2 August 1863, 1 year; 18 December 1873, 3 years) and Maria (16 June 1869).
- **House 418.** «Pasqua Gorlato di Giorgio e fu Domenica Manzin, wife of Domenico De Franceschi q. Giovanni Maria», died 13 July 1856 aged 39. On 13 April 1870 «Dominicus Defranceschi q. Chrystophori, widower of Pascha Gorlato», aged 62, died at 418/378. One man under two fathers, or two Pasquas, is **not settled** (the baptism book of 1839 writes «Domenico di Cristoforo qm Gio. Maria» with Pasqua Gorlato, below); Domenica Manzin here is the mother of Pasqua, dead by 1856, and no other fact about her was found.
- **House 26 then 40, Ferrarese.** Pasqua Defranceschi, wife of Angelo Ferrarese: Domenico (8 October 1860) and Maria (5 May 1870); **Angelus Ferrarese q. Paschalis, husband (1849) of Pascha Defranceschi**, died 18 November 1890 aged 67 at house 40.
- **House 681 and 783, Damiani and Baressich.** Paolo Damiani, married 1852 to Lucia Defranc[eschi] (probable), died 20 October 1860 at 783; **Lucia née Defranceschi, widow of Paulus Damiani**, died 12 May 1884 aged 56 at 681. At 681 also **Pietro De Franceschi** «dei furono Pietro e Martina Cintico(?)», widower of Donetta Vellico, d. 27 November 1856 aged 69, **Alba Defranceschi** wife of Antonio Baressich (Petrus, 23 July 1861) and **Blanche, wife (1853) of Antonius Baressich q. Martini**, d. 9 July 1885 aged 68 (the same woman, `inf`).
- **House 791, Forlani.** Lucia Michiela De Franceschi fu Pietro, wife of Giuseppe Forlani q. Martino: Domenico (11 December 1856) and Domenica (30 January 1858).
- **House 804/701 and 805/733, Giachin.** Domenica nata De Franceschi «dei furono Giuseppe e Lucia Tromba», wife (1813) of Sebastiano Giachin q. Giacomo, d. 1 September 1858 aged 67 (entered after the year's last entry); Sebastianus Giachin, widower, 22 April 1868; their daughter Lucia Giachin, 22 May 1868; and Michaela Defranceschi, widow of Dominicus Giachin q. Jacobi, 9 January 1872 aged 86 at 805/733.
- **House 55/33 and 189, 721, 343.** Dominicus Defranceschi q. Petri, husband (1837) of Maria Olivae Dorliguzzo, d. 15 July 1862 aged 59; their son **Petrus, 26, «Uccisione» (killed), 17 June 1863**; Maria née Dorlizzago, widow of Dominicus, 29 October 1869 aged 55; all at house 55. Michaela n. Defranceschi q. Joannis, widow of Paschalis Moscheni, 13 July 1865 aged 77 at 189; **Bonna n. Defranceschi q. Petri**, wife (1823) of Nicolaus Biasiol q. Matthaei, 26 November 1865 aged 65, and her widower Nicolaus on 20 January 1871, at 721; Michaela n. Defrances[…] q. Chrystophori, widow of Franciscus Vellico, 15 December 1867 aged 67 at 343 (ending unsettled).
- **House 419 and 583, 383, the Joannes Defranceschi and Pascha Manzin household.** **Giovanni Maria Defranceschi fu Pietro, d° «frate»**, husband (1821) of Lucia Bonassin q. Giovanni, d. 7 August 1860 aged 62 at 419; Lucia, «widow of Johannes Maria Defranceschi-Frate», 24 April 1868 aged 75 at 583. At 583: **Pascha** (5 September 1872, 5 years; «Joannis et Paschae Manzin»), **Lucia**, unmarried, 28 (14 July 1885; the same parents), and **Joannes Defranceschi q. Joannis, husband (1854) of Pascha Manzin**, d. 2 March 1887 aged 58 (the dates in the entry do not fit the neighbouring entries; as written). Taken together: a Joannes q. Joannis and a Pascha Manzin, parents of a daughter at 583, son of Giovanni Maria «frate» and Lucia Bonassin (`inf`).
- **House 483 and 480.** Paolina, wife (1812) of Petrus Defranceschi q. Joannis, 19 March 1871 aged 81, and Petrus himself, 25 September 1876 aged 92 («Senectus»), at 483; **Petrus Defranceschi q. Dominici, husband (1844) of Antonia Maria Gorlan**, 30 March 1867 aged 60, and the widow on 29 January 1883 aged 64, at 480. **Petrus Defranceschi q. Joannis Mariae, husband (1832) of Maria Pastrovichio**, 13 December 1893 aged 70 at house 951 (probable).
- **Houses 833, 727/624, 552, 82.** Teresa Domenica De Franceschi fu Piero, mother of Maria Zanghirella (17 August 1856); Domenica De Franceschi fu Domenico, mother of a Codacovich child (14 May 1856) and, as «Dominica Defranceschi, wife (1840) of Dominicus [C]odarovich», d. 16 June 1872 aged 58 at the same house 552 (`inf`); Domenica De Franceschi, wife of Tomaso Marinuzzo and mother of Lucia Marinuzzo, widow of Cristoforo Moscarda, 78, 19 September 1859 at 727/624; Maria De Franceschi, mother of Giovanni Battista Bagozzi, d. 2 September 1856 aged 75.
- **Houses 854, 834, 855, 953, 954, Bonassin, the hatters.** **Maria Defranceschi, wife of Laurentius Bonassin, hatter**, loses eight children (Maria four times, Jacobus, Pacifica, Anna and Joseph) between 1879 and 1893 (6 December 1879, 3 years; 27 April 1882, 15 months, where the surname ends «-ski»; 3 August 1883 and 29 December 1883; 18 November 1890, aged 13; 8 May 1891; 29 November 1891; 2 July 1893, 15 months), at houses 854, 834, 855, 953 and 954 (the numbers vary by a digit between entries and are as written). The household of Jacobus Bonassin, hatter, is at 954 in 1891.
- **House 827 Manzin, 66, 985, 526 in the last years.** **Veneranda Defranceschi, wife of Dominicus Manzin**, loses Euphemia (8 April 1887, 2½ years) and Amelia Maria (19 October 1887, 10 months) at house 827; Josephus Defranceschi and Michaela Zanghirella lose Maria Josepha (30 August 1888, 10 months) at house 66; Petrus Defranceschi and a Maria Veneruggo/Veseriggo (the surname unsettled) lose Stephanus (1 March 1888, 2 days) and Maria (26 September 1889, 8 months) at house 985.

**Struck out:** at 1876 no. 114 (image 407 right) the scribe began the husband's name «Defranceschi» and struck it for «Ferrarese» (read at the enlarged crop: the word is the full surname, struck); at 1873 no. 256 (image 378 left) a mother's «Defranc-» is struck for «Giachin». Neither is counted as a Defranceschi entry. Which of these houses are the twelve households of the 1945 cadastre, and whether any reaches the direct line, is **not yet worked out**.

⭐⭐ **The Vodnjan baptism book of 1815–1867 (9R2Z-GP5), read through on 23 November 2026 for every Defranceschi cell.** The volume is the baptism register of the parish of S. Biagio, FamilySearch waypoint 9R2Z-GP5, **442 images (0–441), one full page to a jpg**. The film's own slates name three books: Item 3 (1815–1827), whose cover is at image 2 and whose entries run from 1 October 1815 (image 4 right) to 26 June 1827 (image 80 left); Item 4 (1827–1846), cover at image 84, from 28 June 1827 to a torn leaf at image 267 right that keeps only the heading «Annus 1847» and one entry; and Item 5 (1847–1866), from image 274 to the last entry, **no. 13 of 26 January 1867** (image 435 right). Slates, a test target and blank pages follow at 436–439, and the film ends at 440–441 with an END OF ROLL target and two blank frames. Loose letters and slips tipped in (images 200 L, 229 L, 237 L, 292 L, 384 L, 411 R, 436 L) and repeated exposures (90, 229 R and 237 R, which repeat the page before, and 412, the page of 411 with its slips moved) were read and counted once; none of the slips names the family.

**How it was read, and what that is worth.** Fifteen readers (subagents) each opened both jpgs of every image in a block of about 32 images and transcribed every cell that carries the name, at page size, with 2x enlargements of the doubtful cells (which add no detail; nobody could zoom). Several lost their context once and re-read the images they could not recover from their own notes. **I have not looked at these cells at level 13 myself**, so every reading here is the readers' (`doc` for the entry as they transcribed it, `inf` for every link between entries), the book is **not** called walked, and a faint name in a crowded godparent cell is the likeliest thing missed. The readers' own counts: **about 250 entries carry a Defranceschi in a cell other than the baptizer's** (195 in the tabled blocks, 25 in images 280–311, 30 in images 312–343), as child and father together in 31 of the 195, as mother (her maiden name) in 43, as father in 47, and as godfather or godmother in about a hundred. The marginal notes the readers transcribed (later hands of 1911, 1930, 1931) are about other surnames; the one beside a Defranceschi mother (7 March 1852, house 361) changes her child's surname Codacovich to Valerio by a decree of 1930.

**Don Stefano De Franceschi, the priest, is in the baptizer column and is not counted.** From the first years to **February 1849** («de Licentia Parrochi», and in 1848–49 «Cooperator») he baptizes in some **680 entries** by the readers' own lists (images 0–311; not re-counted); after 1849 he does not appear. He is never a child, parent or godparent in an entry, and no entry gives him a father: the marriage books (above) are what call him one of the three brothers «di Giuseppe». Two laymen of his name stand in the same cells as godfather or father, **Stefano q. Pietro** and **Stefano q. Giovanni Maria**, below, and a «Stefano De Franceschi fu Pietro» is godfather in 1844 and 1846.

**Kovačina: none, in any role, in any of the 442 images** (typed: Kovačina, Kovacina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina, Kovacsinich). **Kalanj: none as a surname** (typed: Kalanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Kallanj, Kalan, Calan, Calagn, Kalagn, Kalaj, Kalani, Callain, Callajn, Callayn, Callein, Kalagnia, Kalaijn, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalayn, Kalianj, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Kallanij, Kallein). `cover` exited 0 for Defranceschi, Kalanj and Kovačina on 23 November 2026. Because the book was read at page size and not walked, **this is a statement about what the readers saw, not a nil for the book.** The nearest forms are listed as not counted: Palin (a looped P, read at 2x in about a dozen cells, not Calan), Calante or Galante (a Malusà by-name, first letter unsettled), Francin, Franolich, Franzin, De Franchi, De Marin, De Marchi, De Rocchi, Franti or Frank (a noble family of the 1860s), and a **by-name «dto Calan» on a Manzin line**, which is the next paragraph.

**The by-name «dto Calan» in this book belongs to a Manzin line, not to the Kalanj of Ledenice** (`doc` for each reading; nothing in any of these entries ties it to Kalanj, so it is **not counted as a Kalanj finding**; the Atlas rule for Kalan is «decide per record»). It stands in seven places: 23 October 1816 (house 222, «Giovanni Manzin q. Giovanni de Calan(?)», agricoltore); 25 July 1819 (house 788, the mother «**Veniera Manzin q. Domenico dto Calan**», wife of the shoemaker Domenico Fabro, read at a crop; her father is Domenico Manzin and her house at the baptism of 1815 is 188); 22 December 1821 (house 252, «Gio. Manzin qm Gio. d.o Calan»); 14 October 1834 and 10 January 1837 (houses 332 and 390, «Giovanni Manzin di Avvenerio qm Giovanni dto Calan», calzolajo in 1834 and macellajo in 1837; the 1837 entry reads Calan or Calon); 27 December 1838 (house 337, the same man as godfather, «di Venier dto Calan»); and 27 April 1846 (house 418, the same man as father of a baby **Domenica Manzin** born 19 April, mother Maria Franolich or Francolich). That baby is not the Domenica Manzin of this page (the woman who died at 418 in 1856 was already the mother of the grown Pasqua Gorlato), and house 418 is only the same address. What the by-name does give is a **lead and no more** for worklist 335: a Manzin family whose head was a **Domenico**, with a daughter Veniera, living in the town in 1815–19. Whether the Domenica Manzin who was the mother of Bonetta (married 19 November 1823) was a sister of Veniera is not shown by anything read here, and a lead is never a finding. No Domenica Manzin whose father is named Domenico appears as a child in the entries the readers listed (they list Domenicas by eye at page size and Manzin is on nearly every page, so this is not a nil).

**The Defranceschi households of the town in the baptism book, 1815–1867** (`doc` for each entry as the readers transcribed it, `inf` for each link between entries; house numbers as written, two numbers from 1858; this adds the baptisms to the households the death entries gave above, and where they meet it says so):

- **Giuseppe and Lucia Tromba, and their children (houses 319, 376).** An entry of 30 November 1815 (house 319) names «Petrus Josephi De Franceschi et Luciae Tromb[a?] jugalium filius», the ploughman Pietro; the death book calls Domenica Giachin «dei furono Giuseppe e Lucia Tromba». **Pietro di Giuseppe q. Pietro, ploughman, and Maria Malusà** (houses 376, 404, 421, 324) baptize Domenica Maria (b. 1 December 1816), Domenica Michiela Giovanna (1818), Teresa Domenica (1820), **Stefano Matteo (b. 12 March 1822)**, Cristoforo (1824) and Maria (1826, the mother named: Maria Malusà qm Mattea). By name and father the Stefano Matteo of 1822 is the **Stefano q. Pietro** of house 478 below (`inf`).
- **Cristoforo di Giuseppe, the weaver,** is godfather in some thirty entries from 1817 to 1839 (houses 80, 88, 469, 577 and others) and is never a father in this book; and **Pietro di Giovanni, weaver, and his wife Paolina** are godparents from 1817 to 1839. Whether Pietro «di Gio.» the weaver is the third brother «di Giuseppe» or a separate Pietro is **not settled**: the readers could not decide the abbreviation in 1820, and the 1839 entries write «Pietro qm Giovanni».
- **Pietro q. Pietro q. altro Pietro, ploughman, and Maddalena Francin di Giovanni q. Vito** (houses 586, 599, 456): Pietro (1819), Maria Martina (1822), Pasqua (1824), Giovanni (b. 16 February 1827), Lucia (1828); the mother is named from 1824. The **Bianca** born 12 October 1817 (house 441) is probably their daughter and the **Alba or Bianca** of house 681 below (`inf`).
- **Domenico q. Pietro «detto Roman», ploughman, and Zaccheria Cerlon di Francesco, «dto Storto»** (houses 88, 64, 48): Pietro (1817), Pietro (1819), Franco (1821), Domenica (1822), Pasqua (1825), Pietro (1828), Domenica (1830), Maria (b. 20 September 1833). Three children called Pietro in eleven years are three baptisms, not three survivors (`inf`).
- **Giovanni Maria di Pietro q. Gio. Maria, ploughman, and Lucia Bonassin** (houses 356, 363, 286): Veniera (1822), Pietro (1824), Lucia (1826), Giovanni (b. 2 April 1829) and Stefano (b. 26 or 28 December 1831). The two sons are, by name and father, the **Giovanni and Stefano q. Giovanni Maria of house 419** (below), and Veniera is probably the **Veneranda di Giovanni Maria, wife of Antonio De Marin** (houses 397, 322, 474; 1846, 1849, 1851, 1855) (`inf`).
- **House 419, two sons of Giovanni Maria.** **Giovanni** (wife Pasqua Manzin di Antonio) baptizes Lucia (23 March 1857) and Giovanni Maria (16 September 1860); **Stefano** (q. Giovanni Maria, wife **Maria Forlanichio**, once written Fortanichio) baptizes Giovanni Maria (28 July 1858), Pietro (12 September 1860), Lucia (20 October 1863) and Dominicus (10 June 1865, house 495, baptized by the midwife). **This bears on the death book's open question about 478.** Two men called Stefano were living, **Stefano q. Pietro** at 478 with **Maria Francin di Giuseppe** (Maria, 1852; Petrus, 1854; Josephus, 1858; Petrus, 1859; Joseph, 1861; Stephanus Eusebius, 30 March 1863; Dominica, 1865) and **Stefano q. Giovanni Maria** at 419 with **Maria Forlanichio**. The Forlanichio who is the mother in the death entries of 1869, 1871 and 1884 at 478 may therefore belong to the other Stefano's house, or be a second wife (`inf`): this narrows the question and does **not** settle it.
- **Stefano q. Domenico, and Domenico Giovanni q. Stefano and Mattea Del Carro** (houses 406, 423, 325, 481, 491). **Stefano di Domenico q. Pietro and Bonetta Vellico** baptize Domenico Giovanni Antonio (b. 19 June 1819, house 406), Martina (1824, house 423) and Maria (1829, house 325); the baby of 1819 is the **Domenico q. Stefano** who with **Mattea Del Carro di Venier** baptizes Stefano (1850), Venerius (1852), Bona (1855), Petrus (1858), Stefano (7 August 1859, house 491/406), Veneranda (1862) and a child of 1865 whose first name is unsettled (house 481), the household of 481/406 in the death book (`inf`).
- **Domenico di Pietro q. Gio. Maria, ploughman, and Maria Oliva Dorliguzzo fu Agostino** (houses 41, 52, 44): Pietro (b. 17 March 1837), Boneta (1841), Avvenenza (b. 27 September 1844), Agostino (b. 11 July 1847) and Giuseppe (b. 18 March 1851).
- **House 418, and the patronymic that the death book left open.** On 9 April 1839 «**Domenico Defranceschi di Cristoforo qm Gio. Maria**, agricoltore» and **Pasqua Gorlato di Giorgio** baptize Maria at house 286 (the entry is wrapped «Defrance-/schi» and was read at a crop). He is, by name, wife and father, the Domenico of house 418 whose wife Pasqua Gorlato died on 13 July 1856 and who died himself on 13 April 1870 as «q. Chrystophori»; the death entry of 1856 that wrote «q. Giovanni Maria» then names his **grandfather**, and the 1870 entry his father (`inf`). The "one man under two fathers" is therefore probably one man whose father was Cristoforo; the "or two Pasquas" part is not touched.
- **Michiela di Cristoforo q. Gio. Maria, wife of Francesco Vellico** (house 224), baptizes Maria (1826), Bonetta (1828), a child of 1831, Cristoforo (1833), Giovanna (1836), Andrea (1839, her by-name read «Fralle» or «Fratte», unsettled) and a second Andrea (1842): the sister of Domenico di Cristoforo (`inf`).
- **Sisters married out, 1817–1832.** **Domenica di Giuseppe q. Pietro, wife of Sebastiano Giachin** (houses 717, 332, 532: 1823, 1824, 1828, 1832); **Michiela di Giovanni q. Pietro, wife of Pasquale Moscheni** (houses 63, 47: 1819, 1822, 1824, 1831); **Bonetta q. Pietro q. Domenico, wife of Niccolò Biasiol** (house 491, 1825); and a **Michiela Teresa di Giuseppe q. Pietro** (houses 528, 700: 1817, 1818, 1821). These are the "four women who married out" and the Giachin household of the death entries above.
- **The daughters of the next generation, 1842–1865, as mothers.** **Maria q. Domenico, wife of Laurentius Gorlato q. Blasii** (house 66, baptisms from 1857 to 1865, the last on 8 October 1865); **Pasqua q. Domenico, wife of Angelus Ferrarese q. Paschalis** (houses 26 and 15, from 1849 to 1864); **Dominica q. Domenico, wife of Florus Biasiol Dominici** (house 167, 1853 to 1864); and a **Dominica, wife of Domenico Codacovich q. Pauli** (houses 362, 361, 552; 1842, 1849, 1850, 1852, 1856), whose father the entries write «di Domenico», «Dominici», and once (1852) **«q. Francisci»**, so whether she is the same woman as the Biasiol wife, a sister, or a mis-written patronymic is **not settled**. **Daughters «q. Petri»** are baptizing from 1844 to 1859 as Lucia Michiela (Giuseppe Forlani di Martino, houses 523 and 791), Lucia (Paolo Damiani, houses 783 and 520, 1853–58), and Michela Teresa (Pasquale Zanghirella, house 833, 1852–59, twins in 1856); the readers' given names for them differ between entries (Lucia, Michiela, Michela Teresa, Maria Teresia, Theresia Dominica), so **whether these are three women or four is not settled**. **Alba** (1854) and **Bianca** (1860), wife of Antonio Baresich at house 681, are the Blanche of the death entry (`inf`).
- **Cells that stay unsettled** are the ending of the surname in a number of godparent cells («Defrances-», «-ski» against «-schi», one cell cut by the column rule), the house digits where the readers wrote «481/406» or «478/432», and the by-name after «Michiela Defranceschi qd Cristoforo» in 1839. Each is named in the reader's file and none is read as a fact here.

name: Čepić
lead: One family in 1945. The youngest register series in the study — nothing before 1782.
body: Recorded in the 1945 cadastre as Ceppici di Pòrtole, in the Motovun judicial district.

name: Crikvenica
lead: Named for a church: the Pauline monastery of 1412, in the deed that first records the name.
body: Nikola IV Frankopan gave the monastery to the Pauline fathers on 14 August 1412. The order stayed four hundred years, until Joseph II dissolved it in 1786, and for that whole time it was Vinodol's school, pharmacy and library.

A harbour came in 1877, a bathing beach in 1888, the first hotel in 1891 — a Vinodol village that became an Austrian seaside resort inside one lifetime. The Gologorica branch reached here by way of Poreč.

registers.note: Župa Crikvenica, 1798–1908, filmed from the Croatian State Archives. The register begins twelve years after Joseph II dissolved the Pauline monastery that gave the town its name.

name: Rijeka
lead: The largest documented concentration of the surname anywhere in Croatia — 447 records, once Vitipolis is recognised for what it is.
body: The indexed church books give 225 records under Fiume, 178 under Vitipolis and 44 under Rijeka. They are the same city. Vitipolis is the Latin for the city of Saint Vitus — Rijeka's patron, and the saint its cathedral is named for — which is also what the German Sankt Veit am Flaum means. Read together they make Rijeka the single biggest cluster of this family in the country, larger than Pola, Poreč and Omiš combined.

This is where the received account puts three separate arrivals: Domenico from 1614, Valentino out of Carnia made a citizen in 1739, and Giovanni Battista from the County of Pazin around 1740. The registers show de Franceschi children being baptised here from 1626.

***The pier that carries the name is a Croatian naming, not a Habsburg one — 13 November 2026.*** The port of Rijeka has a **De Franceschijev gat**, and this archive has been asking since September which man it honours. Two papers answer the question's frame, if not yet its subject. Mirano Hess, writing in *Pomorstvo* in 2001, titles a section «**Izgradnja gata Zichy (De Franceschijev gat)**» and gives the plan's dimensions, 150 m by 80 m — so the pier built from the 1870s was **Gat Zichy**, and the De Franceschi name is the modern one for the same ground (`doc`). Igor Karaman, in the *Historijski zbornik* of 1986, sets out how the Hungarian port named its quays: before 1868 for figures who had served the city (Maria Theresa, A. L. Adamić), in the 1870s **for the governors of the day — Zichy, Szápáry** — and from the late 1880s for members of the ruling house (Stefanija, Rudolf, Franz Salvator, Marija Valerija). **There was no pier of a private person's name in the Hungarian port at all.** An American consular report of the Italian period lists the moles as Palermo, Napoli, Genova, Ancona, Adamich, San Marco, Stocco and the Cagni breakwater — again no De Franceschi. And Lidija Butković Mićin, in *Ars Adriatica* in 2023, shows the Croatian names arriving after 1945: Adamić's pier was «Gat 1. maja» in 1948, Molo Napoli was still Napoli in 1946 and is today **Visinov gat**. **So the name was given after 1945, and its pair is Visinov gat, for a Croatian sea captain.** *(22 Nov 2026: one chronology says the pier was named for the poet Otokar Keršovani in 1948, so the De Franceschi name may be later still; one unsourced line, not yet confirmed. It does not change that the man is unknown.)* That finishes the demotion of **Ferencz Defranceschi**, the Fiume official this archive once offered as the eponym: he had retired by 1857, and the pier he would have to be named for was called Zichy when it was built. **Who the De Franceschi is remains unknown** — no source yet opened names him, and neither Carlo de Franceschi the historian nor Valentin the shipowner of 1777 has anything linking him to the port. The next step is not another book but the renaming decree itself, somewhere in the city's papers of 1945–55, where he should stand beside Visin.

Kraljevica godfather (1829/1831), five neighbouring cells settled on 17 Nov 2026 at level 13 in the same book (waypoint 9R2Z-VZ9): 1837 'Francisca ... Kovachna' (no i; not Kovacina), 1834 'Catharinae Milosich' (not Kalanj), 1820 'Kollancich' (a different surname), 1841 'Fridericus de Kerner' (not Francisci). The Kova- cell of 12 Sept 1852 (image 240 right) stays unread under a loose slip.
**Read 17 November 2026.** On 28 February 1737 Valentino de Franceschi from Carnia married Helena Turcho (Surcho) (doc; FamilySearch 9R2X-ZNT, image 167, p. 158).

**The printed surname indexes, read in part on 24 November 2026.** The death indexes (FamilySearch 9R2D-L2W and 9R2D-2NL) and the birth indexes (9R26-16X, 9R2X-PYW) were read for the letters C, D, F and K. They list Defranceschi deaths for 1817, 1839, 1848, 1852, 1855, 1857 (written Defranchi), 1860, about 1879, about 1885 and 24 October 1887, and the Valentinus and Ursula children and the 1849 twins in the birth index; most of these are not checked line by line against the people told elsewhere in this archive, and none was opened at the register page. The same indexes carry four Kalanj-form lines: Kalain Maria (4 December 1867), Kalan Antonius (8 February 1895), Kalanj Georgia (10 March 1897) and Kalanj Martinus (29 November 1898); they point at death pages of the Rijeka register not yet read, so they say a person of that name died in Rijeka and nothing more (`doc` for the index line, nothing for who they were). No Kovačina line was met. The marriage index and the letters and years not named were not read, so this is not a nil for the index.

**Catharina De-franceschi, 24 October 1887 (entry 723).** The Rijeka death register 9R2D-7M6 (image 288, p. 227) gives her as a widow, née Bellinich, of Fiume, living at via del Municipio 533, aged 74, buried on the 26th (`doc`, level 13). It is the death the roster already held for Catharina Bellinich, now read at the page. The three Kalanj lines of 1895, 1897 and 1898 cannot be followed to a page on FamilySearch: its Catholic Rijeka death registers stop in 1892, and the Orthodox parish book of Rijeka (9R2D-N3K) is a different church. Whether those men were Catholics of Rijeka is not known.

**Marriage index of the Rijeka parish, 1816–1885 (FamilySearch 9R26-YWT, read 24 Nov 2026): one Defranceschi line, 14 February 1831.** The printed index «Kazalo vjenčanih 1816–1847» (viewer image 18, left page, D section, the 1831 block; ark `3:1:3QS7-899F-QNDF`) reads, at page size and at level 13, «Defranceschi Francesco, e Catterina Bellinich», 1831, 14 Febbraio (`doc` for the index line). It is a groom-keyed index: no page, entry number or register reference is printed, so the marriage entry itself has not been seen. It is the earliest dated record of the pair known here: Franciscus Defranceschi and Catharina Bellinich, whose children are listed in the FamilySearch index at Fiume in 1836 (household h064), and Catharina Bellinich is the widow who died at Fiume on 24 October 1887. That the Catterina of 1831 is the woman of 1887 rests on the shared name and on the match of the two households (`inf`); at about 74 in 1887 she would have been about 17 at the wedding (`inf`, the age in a death entry is approximate). It does not settle whether «Carolina Bellinich», the wife named in the baptism page of 12 November 1849, is the same woman under another given name, and no entry says so. The second part of the index, 1848–1885 (a tabular book, by groom's initial and year), was read for C, D, E, F and K: no Defranceschi, Kalanj, Kalan or Kovačina line as groom or bride. Not counted: Defranza Simon (21 July 1878, Nr 326) and a bride «Defranze» Francisca (9 October 1871, Nr 371, the surname unsettled), the different name Defranza; and the near-names Franceschich, Kalman, Kalcich, Kovacich and Colan, which are other surnames. The other letters of both parts were not read, so this is not a nil for the index.

registers.note: 447 indexed records under three names for one city.

name: Senj
lead: An Uskok garrison on the Habsburg Military Frontier — never Italian, unlike Istria.
body: Taken over by the Habsburgs in 1522 as a state-controlled Militärgrenze, and from the 1530s the base of the Uskoks, the refugee raiders who fought the Ottomans and Venice until an agreement between Habsburg and Venice expelled them in 1617. The Nehaj fortress was built by the Uskok captain Ivan Lenković in 1558.
Records for Senj fall to the State Archives in Rijeka, whose remit covers Primorje-Gorski Kotar plus the city of Senj. That inventory is not yet mapped.

registers.note: The Kvarner gap is now partly closed. FamilySearch holds microfilm of the Senj parish registers 1734–1920 and of Sv. Juraj near Senj 1695–1868, filmed from the Croatian State Archives in Zagreb — plus an Austrian army field-hospital register for 1805–06. The DARI collection itself still has no published parish-level inventory.

name: Mione
lead: A hundred and thirty people at 710 metres — and the Italian end of a documented migration into Istria.
body: First written on 15 June 1185, when Odolrico called Gusetto, Strabo, and Vecellone, son-in-law of Giovanni da Mione, received concessions from Domenico, abbot of Moggio. An independent comune until 1871, now a frazione of Ovaro in the Canale di Gorto.

A stone above the village, at some 1,600 metres, carries Venetic inscriptions — this valley was a route long before it was a parish. From the parishes of Ovaro and Luincis a long series of weavers took the road into Istria; the documents become numerous in the seventeenth century and frequent in the eighteenth.

registers.note: Confirmed dead end: FamilySearch holds only the Napoleonic civil registration for Ovaro's frazioni — Mione, Luincis, Luìnt, Muina, Ovasta, Liariis, Entrampo, Lenzone, Agrons e Cella, Cludinico, Muscletto, Chialina — filmed from the Archivio di Stato di Udine. There are no Ovaro parish books on film anywhere online. The pre-1806 church registers must be asked for at the parish.

name: Imotski
lead: Taken from the Ottomans in July 1717 with a De Franceschi first over the wall. The family has been here three hundred years.
body: Of the seventy Venetians living at Imotski after 1717, only the de Franceschi settled permanently in the Imotska krajina. They held the Perinuša estate — the former begluk of arci-beg Čaušević, with land, houses, a mill and a tower on the Vrljika — and they are still present, physically and in the town's memory, though most of the arable land and the mills are gone and many members have scattered.

There is a long local antagonism to go with it: a persistent belief that the liberation was owed solely to the Imotski Franciscans and the people, which casts the acquisition of Perinuša as a seizure. The estate had in fact been Ottoman crown land, held by begs; who owned it before that is lost in medieval darkness.
Fewer than five people named Franceschi live at Imotski today.

held: FamilySearch film, from HDA Zagreb and Zadar
registers.note: The Podjezerja book runs 1693–1733 and so spans the siege of 1717 itself; Imotski-Glavina picks up in 1731. Both were filmed from the Croatian State Archives.

name: Omiš
