lead: A former pirate town at the Cetina mouth, and the Dalmatian family's first seat — a De Franceschi owned a warship here by 1590.
body: The de Franceschi are said to have reached Dalmatia in the fourteenth century as an influential Italian noble house, and to have established themselves at Omiš, where Gaspar de Franceschi is recorded in 1590 as owner of the warship Vascello and later admiral of the fleet.

Zuane Ivan Franceschi sat on the town council here, and it was as an Omiš councillor that he pressed the Imotski refugees' case with the Venetian Provveditore Generale. His estate at Dobrč — today Pisak, along the coast — is where he sheltered them from January 1715.

registers.note: Župa Omiš, 1588–1894. The series opens two years before Gaspar de Franceschi is recorded here as owner of the warship Vascello, which makes this the one place where the Dalmatian family's earliest claim can actually be tested.

name: Split
lead: Twenty-five Franceschi — the largest single concentration of any spelling of this name anywhere in Croatia.
body: Acta Croatica records about sixty people named Franceschi in Croatia today, in thirty households, against fifty in the middle of the last century — an increase of twenty per cent. They are Croats, from Split, and most were born at Split or Imotski.

This is the mirror image of the Istrian story. The Defranceschi of the Pazin area have fallen from about fifty mid-century to about ten; the Franceski of Rijeka from thirty to a single household. Only the Dalmatian branch is growing.

name: Rovinj
lead: The name from 1619 — and the man «da Dignano» buried at Christmas 1728, three weeks after his wife.
body: Rovinj carries the name from **1619**, when a **Pietro De Franceschi** is buried — the entry this archive holds from another direction as «morì ser Piero di Franceschi da Pola», 27 May 1619, and an early dated Istrian record: the Svetvinčenat baptism of 1628 was found after it, and the godparent cells of the name at Svetvinčenat (from 1605) are older.

It does **not** carry it from 1569. The 1569, 1583 and 1592 entries that a surname search returns are **Fracischetto**, **Francoscheto** and **Franceschero** — three other families, and a caution against reading a fuzzy match as a date.

The household that can be followed is **Mattio De Franceschi and Elisabetta**, who baptise **Martino in 1722** and **Benedetto on 23 October 1726**. **Isabetta is buried on 4 December 1728 and Matto on the 27th of the same month** — three weeks apart. And the archive already held that second entry from outside: «**Ob.to di Matt.o de Franceschi da Dignano**». A man described by the Rovinj priest as *from Dignano* had been in the town long enough to baptise two sons there, and buried his wife three weeks before he was buried himself. That the Isabetta of 4 December is the wife rather than a daughter is an inference from the 1722 and 1726 entries, not a statement of the register.
Twenty-one records of ours out of twenty-five indexed, 1619 to 1864, across **twenty-nine volumes opening in 1553** — the largest unread register in Istria that carries the name.

**Re-read on 13 November 2026.** The 1619 entry was looked at again in the burial lists (film 9R2X-VZ9, image 224, left page, first entry: «Adi 27 Maggio … Morse M(esser) Pietro di Fra-ceschi da Pola», level 13, doc). The year is not written in the cell; it is the page's running year, so the date rests on the reader's anchors. Images 223–226 hold **one** such entry, not two, so the «Pietro De Franceschi» and the «Piero di Franceschi» of 1619 may be one man indexed twice (inf). The volume is a camerlengo's list of burials with the fee, not a death register: it gives no parents and no spouse. Its items run from about 1553 to 1672 and 1722 to 1745, not to 1636 as the catalogue says. Only images 190, 203 and 216–228 of the 645 were looked at, so nothing is claimed for the rest.
**Read 17 November 2026.** On 9 February 1721 Mattio de Franceschi of Dignano married Elisabetta (doc; FamilySearch 9R2X-168, image 148). The bride's surname is not settled.

**Read 23 November 2026: the 1864 death of Petrus De Franceschi, and a baptism that is not there.** The Rovinj death book of 1836–1872 (FamilySearch 9R2X-K65, viewer image 103, left page, entry 9, house 296) records on 12 June 1864 «Petrus De Franceschi», a farmer, aged 74, son of the late Michael: read at level 13 (doc). The birth year 1790 on his roster row is that age (inf). His baptism was looked for in the baptism book 9R2C-3YM (viewer images 585–706, left and right pages, from the book's first page on 15 August 1786 to 27 May 1790) and on the first pages of the next roll, 9R2C-SP8 (to 9 July 1790), by readers at page size: no Pietro with a father Michael or Michiel of any surname, and no Franceschi in any role, on any of those pages (the Rovinj surname Rocco, «de Franc…» after it, is a patronymic, not Franceschi). The one infant Pietro seen with a father named Michiel (14 February 1787) is the son of a man whose surname reads Giotto on the page, another family. This is not a nil for the book: ages in death books are not exact, the pages after July 1790 were not read for him, nothing was read at more than page size apart from a few cells, and a few cells are unsettled (the page notes are in the searched log). The cells the readers could not settle were opened again at level 13: none holds a Franceschi, and none a Michael De Franceschi; the one entry that cannot be read is a whole entry scored out in ink at the foot of the page of 27 May 1790, and one grandfather «Lorenzo Fran…» (2 July 1789) stays an unfinished Fran- surname, not a Franceschi shown. What is left is another parish or the countryside, and a late or misplaced entry.

**24 Nov 2026 — the baptism volume read on to the end of 1792.** The Rovinj baptism book 9R2C-SP8 was read from 10 July 1790 to 31 December 1792 (viewer images 11–90, every left and right page at page size by a reader, two cells zoomed): **no Petrus with a father Michael of any surname, no Defranceschi form in any role** (the only Franceschi is a bare «Mariana Franceschi», wife of the nobleman Alvise Basilisco, godmother on 22 December 1791, level 13), no Kalanj and no Kovačina (`cover` exit 0 for all three on 24 November 2026). The one lead looked at, twin sons of a Michiel Alt/Abba (19–23 June 1791) with an interlined «Petro», is not a Franceschi and is not followed. So his baptism is not at Rovinj from 15 August 1786 to the end of 1792 on the pages as read; the Rovinjsko Selo books begin in 1818 and cannot hold it. What is left is another parish, a late or misplaced entry, or an age far from the death book's.

name: Pula
lead: The see and the port at the foot of Istria — and the town a De Franceschi is called «da Pola» from, in 1619.
body: Carlo's own *L'Istria* lists Franceschi among the noble families of Pola «venuti da Capodistria» before the plague of 1631 — which makes Pula one of the two candidate parents for the southern Istrian clusters, the other being Koper itself.
The earliest dated record this archive holds in Istria names a man of this town rather than of the one he was buried in: **«ser Piero di Franceschi da Pola»**, buried at Rovinj on 27 May 1619.

Pula is also where the church paperwork of the whole south ran. The marriage dispensations entered in the Vodnjan register are issued by the **Ordinariate of Pola** — «dell'Ordinariato di Pola» — and that is the office to write to for what those registers only allude to.

**Pula in the 1890s: two Defranceschi households, one from Ližnjan and one born here.** *The Ližnjan one is told on [the Ližnjan page](/liznjan/#pomer): Antonius, porter of Via Medolino, and his son Antonius Georgius (b. 1894).* **The other is Pola's own — Joannes Baptista Defranceschi, born at Pola on 15 December 1869, a chimney sweep, son of a municipal watchman, Franciscus (dead by 1894), and Euphemia Franca; he married Dominica Francisca Clagnan, a servant of Pola, on 20 January 1894** (`doc`: [the marriage entry](/person/joannes-baptista-defranceschi-1869/), Pula marriages VI, page 139, entry 12). **Their son Alexander Angelus, born 4 January 1893 and baptised in April of that year, was legitimised by the marriage — the baptism entry carries the note** (`doc`: Pula births X, page 19, entry 281; [Alexander's page](/person/alexander-angelus-1893/)). *Three more children are in the index only (Francisca Angela 1891, Angela Regina 1894, Umbertus 1896); the household was in the archive from the index before the pages were read.* *[Households](/households/).*

**Pola's navy parish keeps its own books — and one of them holds a Defranceschi.** *The k.u.k. Kriegsmarine had a parish of its own at Pola; its «Sterb-Register» 1866–1913 and «Trauungs-Buch» 1866–1918 are in German and were read end to end.* **The deaths hold no one of the name. The marriages hold one: on 23 February 1914, in the naval church, Andreas Petešić — a medical petty officer born at Sale near Zara — married [Estella Ida Defranceschi](/person/estella-ida-defranceschi-1893/), born at Gologorica on 11 April 1893, daughter of the farmer Anton Defranceschi and Rosa née Salamon** (`doc`, page 30). *The Gologorica line sends a daughter to Pola's navy; the groom's name is Petešić on the page and «Sečešić» in the later Gologorica census, which this archive has noted rather than settled.*

**Two more Pula burials of the name, read on the pages.** *On 17 September 1877 Francisca, five years old, daughter of a Franciscus, was buried from house 85 (tuberculous meningitis)* — a daughter of Franciscus Defranceschi, **who died two years before her, in 1875, and who is «from Gallignana»** (told next). *On 29 February 1892 a seven-day-old Josephus was buried, «Franciscae domesticae illeg. fil.», the illegitimate son of a servant named Francisca who bore the name — a Defranceschi woman not otherwise placed.* *The Pula civil deaths book has now been read entry by entry, January 1864 to May 1893 (the film has no pages before 1864): **six Defranceschi burials in twenty-nine years, none before 1875** — Franciscus (1875), Francisca (1877), Euphemia and the newborn Joannes (1890), Josephus (1892) and a newborn Antonius (1893); the last four are told above and on the [1890s Pula page](/places/).*

***⭐⭐ And the Pola family comes from Gračišće.*** **On 20 November 1875 «Franciscus fil. Joannis Baptae e Gallignana, uxoratus, diurnista» was buried at Pula, 36, married seven years, of pulmonary emphysema** (`doc`, [the entry](/person/franciscus-liberatus-defranceschi-1840/)). *Gallignana is Gračišće; the father is a Joannes Baptista; the age fits the **Franciscus Liberatus baptised in January 1840 at Gračišće house 5**, a son of Joan. Bapt. Defranceschi, agricola, and Francisca Salomon (`inf`).* **He is the father of the Pola chimney sweep Joannes Baptista (b. 1869) and of the Francisca buried in 1877** — so the first link between the Gračišće line and Pula in this archive is the day-labourer who died there at 36, and the household above is his son's.

***⭐⭐ And his marriage names the parents.*** **On 1 June 1868, in the Pula cathedral (entry 70 of the 1815–1877 marriage book), «Francesco De Franceschi da Gallignana, distretto di Pisino» — 28, a discharged soldier serving as a municipal police guard — married «Eufemia Franca», 25, of Parenzo, a servant who had lived at Pola for thirteen years.** *The entry gives his parents as «Gio. Battista De Franceschi, defunto, possidente» and «Francesca Salomon, defunta»* ([the page](/person/franciscus-liberatus-defranceschi-1840/); `doc`) — the very couple of Gračišće house 5. **So the parentage is no longer an inference; only the choice of which boy — the Franciscus baptised in January 1840, 28 in June 1868 — remains `inf`, and it is a strong one.** Her parents were a Giovanni Franca and a Maria Stifanić. *The Pula civil deaths book, read in order from 1864 to May 1893, holds six Defranceschi burials and none before this man's own in 1875 — the family arrives in the town between the 1860s and 1868.*

***⭐ And the son's baptism, 1869 — the index entry opened.*** **On 26 December 1869, at the cathedral, «Giovanni Battista», born on the 15th, was baptised — the son of «Francesco De franceschi fu Giovanni da Galignano, Daziere» and «Eufemia Franca fu Giovanni da Parenzo»; the godfather is a mason from Tolmezzo, «Matteo Pantelli»** (Pula births 1869–75, Liber VII, p. 92, [image 461](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899F-7DNR?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8); [his page](/person/joannes-baptista-defranceschi-1869/); `doc`). *This is the baptism the births index pointed to and the archive had not yet opened. It confirms the household and the birth date and adds one thing: the father's work in 1869 was **«daziere»**, a customs guard — between the police guard of the wedding in 1868 and the day-labourer of the burial in 1875.*

***⭐ And the daughter's baptism, 1873 — the burial's «about 1872» replaced by a date.*** **On 23 February 1873, at the cathedral, «Francesca Luigia», born on 1 February at two in the afternoon, was baptised by Don Andrea Juranić — the daughter of «Francesco Defranceschi fu Gio. Batta da Gallignana, distretto di Pisino, Daziere» and «Eufemia Franca fu Giovanni da Parenzo»; sponsors «Matteo Potočnik, fornajo» and «Angela Venezia»; midwife Giovanna Chinol** (Pula births 1869–75, Liber VII, p. 378, entry 91, house 87 Duomo, image 606 of waypoint 9R2X-SP8, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899F-78X3?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8); `doc`, read at level 13). *It is the same household as the son's baptism above (the husband, the Gračišće father, the Parenzo mother, the work, a customs guard in both) and it is the girl the archive already held as [Francisca, buried on 17 September 1877](/person/francisca-defranceschi-1872/), «five years old», with a birth «about 1872» guessed from that age: she was in fact four years and seven months.* **It adds no person; it replaces a guess with a date, a first name — Francesca Luigia — and a page; and it turns the «`inf`» that her father is the Franciscus buried in 1875 into `doc`.**

***A Defranceschi mother, named at a Pula wedding.*** **In February 1883 the carpenter Antonius Dobrez — born at Visinada on 30 March 1855 and living at Pola since boyhood — married Helena Antonia Cuntu in the cathedral; his mother is entered «Defranceschi Maria».** *The name is on the page, in the parents' cell, beside «Dobrez Joseph, carpentarius»* ([the entry](/person/antonius-dobrez-1855/); `doc`). *It places a household the index had kept unplaced for a month ([h073](/households/)): a Visinada–Kaštelir family whose carpenter son came to Pola — a second road, besides the Gračišće one, by which the name reached the town.*

**And a year later his sister, and a third Pola family from Friuli.** *Catharina Dobrez, born at Visinada on 5 September 1853 and at Pola «from infancy», married the brass-worker Joseph Vio at the cathedral on 25 February 1884 — and again the entry writes her mother «Defranceschi Maria»* ([the entry](/person/catharina-dobrez-1853/), `doc`). **Seven weeks later, on 14 April 1884, a mason called Joannes Baptista «Di Franceschi» — born at Osoppo in Friuli on 1 July 1842 and at Pola since 1864 — married the widow Lucia Dobrila; his parents are «Di Franceschi Joannes» and «Di Cecco Pascha»** ([the entry](/person/joannes-baptista-di-franceschi-1842/), `doc`). *Friulian *di* for Tuscan *de* — the same «of the Franceschi» — but the form is not one of the twelve declared in the scope list, so it is collected, not counted, until David rules. Nothing joins him to the Gračišće family or to the Dobrez household.*

***⭐⭐ A mason and his wife, both Defranceschi, at the font, July 1891.*** **On 26 July 1891 the cathedral baptised «Aloysius Antonius» — born on 5 June at house 10, Via Campo Marzio, to the driver Osualdus Dinon, from Cavasso nuovo, and Catarina Picoli — with the godparents «Defranceschi Antonius, faber murarius» and «Aloysia ejus uxor»; the child bears their two names** (Pula births 1887–96, p. 569, entry 548, [image 315](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-GSKM?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1)). `doc`. *The first page in the archive with a Defranceschi husband and wife together at Pola. Neither has an age, parents or birthplace written. They are `inf` the Aloysia of March 1887, the Antonius of April 1887 and the mason of September 1898 above and below, a trades-circle of one couple; the page does not say so, and the four rows are not merged. The mason is not the Gračišće stonecutter (a lapicida, dead by 1898).*

***A godmother of the name at the cathedral, March 1887.*** **On 6 March 1887 «Defranceschi Aloysia» stood godmother, with the mason «Detoma Antonius», to «Maria Catharina Ursula», born on 9 February 1887 to the mason Jacobus Dilena and Catharina Brenz** (Pula births 1874–87, p. 1117, [image 669](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99F-QJSM?cc=2040054&wc=9R26-BZQ)). `doc`. *The surname is split across two lines in the patrini column and was read at higher magnification. The entry gives no age, parents or house for her, so it says only that a woman of the name was at a Pola font in the spring of 1887; the other Aloysias in this archive are not tied to her.*

***A godfather of the name at the cathedral, April 1887.*** **On 24 April 1887 «Defranceschi Antonius» stood godfather, with «Bilus Catarina», to «Elvira Catarina», born on 16 December 1886 to Carolus Scagnetti and Aloysia Tomsich** (Pula births 1874–87, p. 1133, [image 676](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99F-QJS8?cc=2040054&wc=9R26-BZQ)). `doc`. *The entry gives no trade, age or house for him, so it says only that the name was at a Pola font that spring; the stonecutter of Gračišće, the Ližnjan labourer and the 1898 mason are all possible and nothing in the page chooses between them.*

***⭐ The chimney sweep's eldest, born before the wedding, 1891.*** **On 15 November 1891 «Francisca Angela», born on 27 September, was baptised at the cathedral — the daughter of «Defranceschi Joannes, qm Francisci, e Pola, camini scopator» and «Clagnan Dominica, qm Angeli, e Pola»; the father declared himself before the priest, and a margin note records her legitimation by the marriage of 20 January 1894** (Pula births 1887–96, p. 645, entry 807, [image 340](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-GSVF?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); sponsors «Sissan Petrus, maritimus» and «Nitzer Maria»; midwife Maria Dobrez). `doc`. *She is the first child of the household told above (h047), until now known only from the FamilySearch index; a second, later note dated 23 February 1914 is not read with certainty.*

***⭐⭐ A daughter of the direct line, at Pola.*** **On 14 January 1888, in the cathedral, «Defranceschi Leopolda, ancilla» — born at Gallignana on 6 November 1865, at Pola since 1883 — married the carpenter Emericus Zuban (Zuppan), of Pirano. Her parents are written «Defranceschi Antonius, lapicida» and «Tornasar Maria».** *They are, `inf`, the stonecutter Antonius of Gračišće house 19 (b. 1825) and Maria née Fernasar/Tornasar (1832–1916) — the couple of [the direct line](/direct-line/), so Leopolda is a sister of David's own ancestor* ([the entry](/person/leopolda-de-franceschi-1865/), `doc`). **It is also the first image of Maria's surname: read «Tornasar», with a T that the scribe's own F does not match** ([the comparison](/maternal/fernasar/)). *A servant from the same village, five years in Pola by the wedding, and her father's brother's family already in the town (h129): the Gračišće Defranceschi who came to Pola came more than once.*

***⭐⭐ Her first child, in July 1888.*** **On 15 July 1888, at the cathedral, «Petrus Matthaeus» — born on 29 June at house 231 (Abbazia) — was baptised, the son of «Zuban Emericus, Matthaei e Pyrrhano, faber ferrarius» and «Defranceschi Leopolda, Antonii e Gallignana»** (Pula births 1887–96, p. 143, entry 473, [image 86](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-GQ95?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); sponsors «Bursich Matthaeus, caterarius» and «Bacich Joannes»; midwife Morin Gabriela). `doc`. *The mother is the daughter of the direct line who had married there on 14 January 1888 (above); the entry gives her father only as Antonius, as the marriage does. A margin note in a later hand — «uxorem duxit Polae 23.II.1914 Annam Pecinić» — says that Petrus Matthaeus himself married at Pola in February 1914. The baptism writes the father's trade «faber ferrarius» (smith) and the marriage entry wrote «carpenter»; the two are as read and not reconciled.*

***⭐⭐ And her second, in April 1890.*** **On 20 April 1890, at the cathedral, «Joanna Maria» — born on 11 January at house 246 (Abbazia) — was baptised, the daughter of «Zuppan Henricus Matthaei, faber lignarius, e Pyrrhano» and «Defranceschi Leopolda, Antonii, e Gallignana»** (Pula births 1887–96, p. 384, entry 261, [image 221](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-G37H?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); sponsors «Angelovich Joannes, ex-subofficialis marinae» and «Calavar Maria»; midwife Zimprich Maria). `doc`. *The scribe first wrote the father «Emericus» and struck it out for «Henricus»; the 1888 marriage and baptism entries have Emericus, so the correction is not explained. A margin note, partly under a stamp, says the girl married at Pola on 3 August 1914. The trade here is «carpenter», as at the marriage.*

***⭐⭐ And her third, in January 1894.*** **On 6 January 1894, at the cathedral, «Francisca Catarina» — born on 26 November 1893 at house 17 (Via Castropola) — was baptised, the daughter of «Zuppan Henricus, Matthaei, e Pyrrhano, faber lignarius» and «Defranceschi Leopolda, Antonii, e Gallignana»** (Pula births 1893–96, p. 114, entry 9, [image 501](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-GQ1Q?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); sponsors «Almerigogna Jacobus, carpentarius» and «Blasovich Francisca»; midwife Limpich Maria). `doc`. *Above the father's name stands «vedi Cop. I. n° 449», and a margin note says the girl married «Cvečan Andrea» on 21 October 1915, the parish written «Monfalcone»(?). The scribe again writes the father «Henricus», as for the second child and not «Emericus» as in 1888 (`inf`: the same man). The FamilySearch index had carried her as an unread lead (6YBR-3QNG).*

***⭐⭐ The wife of the 1894 Antonius is found, 1895.*** **On 8 December 1895, at the cathedral, «Joanna Barbara Angela» — born on 24 September at house 6 (Mercato Vecchio) — was baptised, the daughter of «Longhin Vincentius, Thomae, e Venetiis, faber lignarius» and «Rumsich Helena, qm Matthaei, e Besanova»** (Pula births 1893–96, p. 396, entry 821, [image 650](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-GQND?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); sponsor Ghira Angelus, carpenter; midwife Dobrez Helena). **A margin note reads «nupsit Antonio Defranceschi, Polae 26.X.19?9».** `doc` for the note. *It is the other half of the note on the baptism of [Antonius Georgius, 1894](/liznjan/#pomer) («…Longhini, Polae 26.X.19?9»): the same day and place, each naming the other, so she is his wife (`inf`, firm). The year digits are «19?9» on both, the third a loop that reads as 2 or 0 — most likely 1929, when he was 35 and she 34. No marriage entry has been read.*

***A godmother, December 1895.*** **On 29 December 1895 «Catarina», born that day to the unmarried «Gobbo Catarina, qm Joannis, e Sarmenigga(?)», was baptised at home by the midwife and then received at the cathedral by the canon Pacovich; her sponsors were «Zotel Joseph» and «Defranceschi Catarina»** (Pula births 1893–96, p. 404, entry 865, [image 654](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-GQD1?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); midwife Zapletal Dominica). `doc`. *The entry gives the godmother no age, trade or kin. The archive's one Catharina of the right place and time is the Gračišće servant born in 1869, [married at Pola in 1898](/person/catharina-defranceschi-kostessich-1869/) — `inf` at most, and the rows are not merged.*

***The foundling's third child, 1896.*** **On 16 May 1896 «Stephanus Petrus», born on 6 May at house 69 (Ponte Castagner), was baptised at the cathedral by the dean; the mother column reads «Franceschi Francisca ex orphanotrophio Tergestino», the father's column is empty; sponsors Rosa Gaspar, smith, and Rosa Josepha** (Pula births 1893–96, p. 465, entry 263, [image 686](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-GQXG?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); midwife Simecka Dominica). `doc`. *The mother is written in the same words as at [Paula's baptism in 1884](/person/paula-poliak-1884/) and [Joannes Antonius's in 1894](/person/joannes-antonius-franceschi-1894/): `inf` one woman, three children. The surname «Franceschi» is hers alone — a foundling's, very likely invented — and not «De»: it is a name the one-name study notes and does not count as a line.*

***A Defranceschi husband, named only in a margin, 1908.*** **On 19 July 1888 «Maria Regina», born on 7 June at house 357 (Fondaco), was baptised at the cathedral, the daughter of the stonecutter «De Stefano Antonius, Andreae, e Medun [Udine]» and «Gradara Sancta, Joannis, e Tergesto»** (Pula births 1887–96, p. 142, entry 464, [image 86](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-GQ95?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1)). `doc`. **A margin note beside it reads «Juncta est matrimonio Polae die 5/8 1908 cum Franc… Defranceschi. Juncta est II. cum …aeo die 17 Septembr. 1913»** — she married a Franciscus (`inf`; the forename is abbreviated «Franc») Defranceschi at Pola on 5 August 1908, and married again on 17 September 1913, the second husband's forename ending «…aeo» (Matthaeus? doubtful). `doc` for the note. *Nothing in it says who he was, where he came from or how the first marriage ended; the remarriage in 1913 suggests, `inf`, that he had died or the marriage had ended by then. The 1908 marriage entry is not on a film this archive has reached.*

***A Defranceschi bride, named only in a margin, 1914.*** **On 24 July 1888 «Ricardus Franciscus Andreas», born on 19 October 1887, was baptised at the cathedral, the son of «Bearcco Natalis, qm Joannis, e Tramonti di sotto [Veneto], faber ferrarius» and «Radessich Maria, qm Francisci, ex Lissa»; a margin note reads «copul. Polae in par. … die 21.XI.1914 cum Angela Defran-/ceschi»** (Pula births 1887–96, p. 147, [image 88](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-GQ98?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1)). `doc` for the note. **The woman is now known (25 October 2026): she is Angela Regina, born 4 November 1894, the chimney sweep's daughter** — her own baptism at the cathedral on 6 January 1895 (Pula births 1893–96, p. 264, entry 12, [image 581](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-GQL3?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1); father «Defranceschi Joannes, fil. Francisci, e Pola, caminorum scopator», mother «Clagnan Dominica, qm Angeli», sponsor Fenco Caspar) carries a margin note «copul. Polae in par. … 21.XI.1914 cum Beaco Ricardo»: the same day, from the other side. `doc` for both notes; `inf` for the join, firm. *A stamped note under it adds a second marriage at Pola on 30 August 1943 «cum O[r]nano(?) Antonio»; she is the Angela Ornano of the 1947 IRO file, born Pola 4 November 1894 (`inf`).*

***⭐⭐ Her sister, ten years later.*** **On 31 January 1898 «Defranceschi Catharina, famula» — born at Gallignana on 3 February 1869, at Pola since 1894 — married the porter Joannes Kostessich at the cathedral. Her father is entered «Defranceschi defunctus Antonius, lapicida» and her mother «Fornasar Maria».** *Two daughters of the direct line's stonecutter went into service at Pola — Leopolda in 1883, Catharina in 1894 — and each married there* ([the entry](/person/catharina-defranceschi-kostessich-1869/), `doc`). ***The surname of their mother, which the 1888 entry wrote «Tornasar», is «Fornasar» here*** *([the comparison](/maternal/fernasar/)); the father was already dead by 1898.*

***⭐⭐ And an old man from Ližnjan, dead in the hospital.*** **On 11 March 1895 «Defranceschi Antonius, quondam Matthaei, mendicans, viduus, e Liciniano» died at the Pula civil hospital, aged 72, of senile decline, and was buried on the 13th** (`doc`; [the entry](/person/antonio-defranceschi-fu-matteo-liznjan-house-17-1844-1890-liznjan/)). *He is — `inf`, strongly — the Antonio of Ližnjan house 17, the father of the Pola porter Antonius told above: a beggar and widower who had come to his son's town.*

**And a child with only a mother.** *On 28 July 1896 «Defranceschi Joanna», **«illeg. Catarinae e Tergesto»** — the illegitimate daughter of a Catharina from Trieste — died at fifteen months of hydrocephalus, at house 27 in Via Diana, and was buried in the civil cemetery on the 30th* ([the entry](/person/joanna-defranceschi-1895/); `doc`). *She bears her mother's surname, so her mother was a Catharina Defranceschi — the second illegitimate child of the name read at Pula, after the Josephus of 1892 (son of a servant Francisca).* **The Catharina of Gallignana (b. 1869), a servant at Pola from 1894, is a candidate, and the entry's «from Trieste» is against her; the two are not reconciled.**

***⭐ A child of the name with a mother from the Trieste orphanage.*** **On 31 May 1894, in the Pula cathedral, «Joannes Antonius», born on the 21st, was baptised at house 139 (Monte Serpo): mother «Franceschi Francisca, ex orphanotrophio Tergestino», no father named, godparents the farmer Joannes Hussich and Antonia his wife** (Pula births X, p. 176, [image 532](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-GQT3?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-3T1)). `doc`. *A foundling-home girl's surname is probably an invented one, so this is the name without a known line behind it — `inf`, and no claim of kin.* It is the **last unread stretch of the births index** (F, 1885–95) that turned it up.

***⭐ And the same woman, ten years earlier.*** **On 28 December 1884 «Paula», born on the 23rd, was baptised at the cathedral (house 11, Sobborgo Siana): father «Poliak Paulus qm Pauli e Barbiana, operarius», who declared himself the father before the baptiser; mother «Franceschi Francisca ex Orphanotrophio Tergesti»** (Pula births 1874–87, [image 577](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899F-QJ23?cc=2040054&wc=9R26-BZQ)). `doc`. *The mother is described in the very words used in 1894; that they are one woman is `inf`, and it is the first time this archive has had more than one entry for a foundling of the name.*

***A godmother, at the cathedral, in 1898.*** **On 17 July 1898 «Defranceschi Antonia» stood godmother, with the municipal sub-treasurer Henricus Major, to the baptised child of a Trieste clerk, Josephus Valle, and Maria Manzin** (Pula births 1896–99, [image 200](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-5R95?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-3YS)). `doc`. *No age, parents or house are given, so the entry says only that the name was at Pola that summer; the Gračišće daughters in service there (Leopolda and Catharina, above) are the obvious candidates and nothing proves it.*

***⭐⭐ A Gologorica daughter, married to a man of Gračišće, at Pola.*** **On 7 August 1898 «Elda Maria Aloisia» was baptised at the cathedral (born 23 July, house 20, Via Helgoland): father «Salamon Aloisius, Joannis, e Gallignana, negotiator», mother «Defranceschi Maria, qm Francisci, e Moncalvo [Gologorica]», godparents «Salamon Antonius, negotiator» and «Defranceschi Lina»** (Pula births 1896–99, [image 204](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-55BC?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-3YS)). `doc`. *«Moncalvo» is Gologorica in Italian; the Francis she is the daughter of is probably [Franciscus Xaverius Joseph of house 4](/gologorica-line/) (d. 4 January 1893), but the entry does not say so (`inf`).* **Salamon is the name that stood godfather at the Gologorica baptism of 1843 and runs through [the Gologorica line](/gologorica-line/); the marriage is not yet found.**

***⭐ A fifth child of the Pola chimney sweep.*** **«Julius Petrus», born 19 May 1898 and baptised on 11 September at house 34, is the son of «Defranceschi Joannes, gn Francisci, e Pola, camini scopator» and «Clagnan Dominica, gn Angeli, e Pola»** (Pula births 1896–99, [image 210](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-55B2?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-3YS)). `doc`. *The household of [Joannes Baptista and Dominica](/households/) had stood at four children; the births index ends in 1895, so the 1898 baby could not have been found there.*

***Two more men of the name at the font, September 1898.*** **On the 24th «Defranceschi Antonius, faber murarius» (mason) stood godfather to Valeria Durizzotti** ([image 213](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-55BH?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-3YS)); **on the 28th «Defranceschi Angelus, piscator» (fisherman) did so for Antonius Stephanus Bellulovich** ([image 214](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-5RSC?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-3YS)). `doc`. *Neither entry gives an age or parents. The mason is not the stonecutter of the direct line, who was dead by January 1898 (above); the fisherman is, `inf`, the fish-seller Angelus of the twins buried in 1896 (above).*

**Twins, five days old, of a fish-seller.** *On 27 October 1896 «Defranceschi Carola» and «Defranceschi Victor» — **«Angeli piscium venditoris»**, of house 11 in Via della Valle — were buried, five days old and premature* ([the entries](/person/carola-defranceschi-1896/); `doc`). *The FamilySearch index had them as baptised twins, Carola and Victorius, of Angelus Defranceschi and Angela Comparich (22 October 1896, [h103](/households/)); the page now says how long they lived and what their father did.* **Another Pula household of the name, and one the archive cannot yet place: no Angelus is known to be a brother or cousin of the Gračišće Franciscus or the Ližnjan Antonius.**

***⭐ And a midwife from Pomer, dead in the hospital.*** **On 20 March 1898 «Defranceschi Magdalena, vidua Thomae, e Pomario, villica» died at the Pula civil hospital, aged 85, and was buried on the 22nd** (`doc`; [the entry](/person/magdalena-davic-pomer/)). *She is, `inf` and strong, Magdalena Buić, the widow of Tomas Defranceschi of Pomer house 5 and the village's midwife* ([her household](/liznjan/#pomer)) *— the second elderly Istrian of the name, after the Ližnjan Antonio of 1895, to end in this town's hospital.*

***⭐ A godfather at Pola, in 1869 — before the navy servant's wedding.*** **On 18 April 1869, at the cathedral, «Giuseppe Giovanni», born on the 15th, was baptised — the son of «Vicenzo Deola di Domenico da Villa de Villa, Provincia di Belluno, giornaliero» and «Teresa Dall[…] fu Antonio» of the same village; the godfathers are «Giovanni De-/franceschi, capo e […]» and «Pietro Monace, testimonio»** (Pula births 1869–75, Liber VII, p. 31, [image 430](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99F-7D25?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8); [his page](/person/giovanni-defranceschi-godfather-at-pola-1869-pula/); `doc`). *He is named and nothing more: no age, birthplace, father or house, and the word after «capo e» is a hurried one that I could not read. The Belluno parents are strangers to the name; the godfather was probably a work-mate or neighbour of theirs. **He may be [Johann Defranceschi, the navy servant of Gračišće](/person/johann-joannes-defranceschi-navy-servant-1833/)**, who married in the naval parish on 16 January 1871 and has no civil record before it (`inf`, weak — a navy servant would be at Pola, but «capo» could as well be a foreman of the arsenal; the two rows are not merged).*

***⭐ A baptism of 1871 whose margin names a Defranceschi bride — 1911.*** **On 31 December 1871, at the cathedral, «Giovanni Beniamino», born on the 26th at half past eleven in the morning, was baptised by Don Giovanni Mladošić — the son of «Gregorio Mohorat di Francesco da Bogliuno, pittore in arsenale» and «Rosa Cheba di Giorgio da Barbana»** (Pula births 1869–75, Liber VII, p. 275, entry 558, image 554 of waypoint 9R2X-SP8, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899F-782C?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8); house «Casa Cheba» 25; midwife Domenica Viscovich; `doc`). **A later hand writes in the margin, across the columns of religion and sex: «Die 14.IV.1911 cum Defran-/ceschi Domi-/nica matri-/monio est iunctus»** — on 14 April 1911 he was married to *Dominica Defranceschi* (`doc` for the note, read at level 13 on 26 October 2026: the surname is split across the line end, «Defran-» then «ceschi», and the given name likewise, «Domi-» then «nica»; the father's surname is written «Mohorat» with the last letter struck over, so «Mohorac» is possible, as the sister's baptism below confirms). A printed stamp beside it records that the surname was changed to «Ermacora» (the date read at level 12 as 18.4.1931). **A sister was baptised the next year at the same font: «Anna», born 12 December 1872, baptised on the 26th, daughter of «Mohoraz Gregorio di Francesco da Bogliuno, distretto di Pisino, pittore» and «Rosa Cheba di Giorgio da Barbana»** (Pula births 1869–75, Liber VII, p. 362, entry 537, image 598, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99F-7ZHM?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8); `doc`; midwife Maria Dobrez; a margin figure «22/3 1881» beside it, read at level 12 only and not understood). The father's surname is here written «Mohoraz», so the last letter of the 1871 entry's «Mohorat» is a z or c, not a t: «Mohoraz» or «Mohorac». *The page does not say who she is, and the archive does not yet know.* Two women of the name are on the roster, neither tested: **Dominica Francisca Clagnan, the chimney sweep Joannes Baptista's wife (h047)**, who would be called «Defranceschi» by marriage only if he had died by 1911 (his death has not been read), and **a Dominica born on 3 March 1865, child of Stephanus Defranceschi and Maria Francin (h037, index only)**. The margin notes of this book name a bride by her own surname (the 1920 note on h047's Umbertus reads «uxorem duxit Annam Zulian[i]»), which favours a woman born Defranceschi over the sweep's wife (`inf`, undecided). **The marriage entry itself is not yet found, and the margin does not say where it was made:** FamilySearch's Pula civil marriages stop at 1901, and the naval-parish marriage book of 1866–1918 (read on 16 October 2026) holds one Defranceschi bride, of 1914, and none of 1911 — so the entry is in a register this archive cannot yet read, and the next step is to ask where. *Not counted as a new family: a groom of Boljun and a bride of the name, found only in a margin.*

***The chimney sweep's wife's own family, at Pola in 1872.*** **On 18 August 1872, at the cathedral, «Antonio Giuseppe», born on 3 August, was baptised — the son of «Klagnan Angelo fu Pietro da Pedoglia di Monfalcone, Par. S. Pietro, muratore» and «Delise Maria fu Giovanni da Rovigno»; midwife Elena Gulizia** (Pula births 1869–75, Liber VII, p. 332, entry 359, house 168 Via San Francesco, image 583 of waypoint 9R2X-SP8, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899F-78JP?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8); `doc`, the parents' cells read at level 13). A slanted note in the margin columns reads, as far as it can be read at level 13, **«Legittimato col matrimonio … 4/11 1872»** — the child was legitimated by his parents' marriage, so the marriage was made on 4 November 1872 (`inf` from the note; the day and the month are read, the word before them is not). **These are the parents of Dominica Francisca Clagnan, born at Pola on 3 December 1868, who married the chimney sweep Joannes Baptista Defranceschi in 1894 ([h047](/households/)):** her marriage entry names «Angelus Clagnan, bricklayer» and «Maria Delise»; her own baptism, 13 December 1868 (Pula births, item 3, p. 428, entry 422), names «Angelo Clagnan di Pietro da Monfalcone, muratore» and «Maria De…lise fu Giovanni da Rovigno» — the same couple, the same father's father, the same trades. So the boy is a younger brother of hers; the two grandfathers are «Pietro» of Monfalcone on the father's side and «Giovanni» of Rovigno on the mother's (`doc` for the names; `inf`, firm, that the three entries are one household). An earlier baptism of this couple, «Pietro» of 18 January 1866 (item 3, p. 261, father «Angelo Clagnan q. Pietro, marinaro da Rodignola»), was logged as a near-name when it was read and is not told here beyond this line. *No Defranceschi stands in any of these entries; the household belongs to this archive because the wife of h047 was born into it.* **The marriage of 4 November 1872 is the next thing to look for: Pula marriages 1815–77 (9R28-T3F) was not read entry by entry.**

***A widow «Franceschi» at the font, 1872.*** **On 27 October 1872, at the cathedral, «Gasparo Giovanni Antonio», born on the 18th, was baptised — the son of «Skoblar Gaspare di Giorgio, i. r. sergente» and «Lucia Maria, di ignoti genitori da Zara, domestica»; the sponsors are «Pancovich Giovanni» and «Maria, vedova di Domenico Franceschi»; midwife Maria Dobrez** (Pula births 1869–75, Liber VII, p. 350, entry 468, house 35 Abbazia, image 592 of waypoint 9R2X-SP8, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899F-78J5?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8); `doc`; the sponsor's line read at level 13, the surname plain, «Franceschi», ending in -chi, with no «-ni» and no «De»). A later note beside the entry records that the child was legitimated by his parents' marriage (read at level 12, not transcribed). **This is the plain spelling of the name, and the archive's own scope list counts it** — but a godmother's line gives no age, birthplace or father, only a dead husband's name, and **the archive already holds a «Domenico Franceschini q. Giorgio di Montona, muratore», with a wife «Maria Miletich q. Tommaso di Pola», whose four children were baptised at Pola in 1857–63 (Pula births item 2, p. 304, and item 3, pp. 18, 76, 153)** — house 244, in the same town. **That Maria cannot be the widow of 1872: a later note on her marriage entry says she died on 9 August 1863** (told in the next paragraph). **But the same font has a «Maria Franceschini» as godmother three times more: on 23 November 1871 (p. 265, entry 356, a carpenter's son of Duino), on 19 January 1873 (p. 369, entry 33, «Maria France-/schini», read at level 13) and on 21 June 1873 (p. 405, entry 256, now in Latin as «Franceschini Maria», read at level 13, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99F-7ZYC?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8))** — four times in nineteen months, a Maria of this name standing sponsor at Pola, the second written as the widow of Domenico Franceschi. That leans toward one woman, **Maria Franceschini, widow of Domenico**, with the final -ni dropped once (`inf`, not proved) — and if the Domenico is the Montona joiner, she is his *second* wife, Maria Crismanich, whom he married in 1867 and left a widow in 1868, not the Maria Miletich of the 1857–63 baptisms (next paragraph). *Not merged with the Montona household, and not a Defranceschi: a woman named by her husband, in the margin of a stranger's baptism.* **Next: the death entry of Domenico Franceschini, 1 January 1868 by the note on his marriage entry (Pula deaths 1864–93, 9R2C-T3D, not read entry by entry), would name his wife and settle it.**

***The Montona joiner Domenico Franceschini and his two wives, 1856–68 — it is not Maria Miletich.*** **On 18 August 1856, at the Misericordia church, «Domenico Fran-/ceschini di Montona, falegname, soldato della Riserva», aged 31, of house 146, was married to «Maria Miletich di Pola», aged 19, of house 138** (Pola marriages 1815–57, Liber III, p. 158, entry 21, image 345 of waypoint 9R28-T3F, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-R97S-T?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-T3F); `doc`; read at level 13). Beside his line a later hand writes «nato li 11 aprile 1825 · morto il 1° gennajo 1868»; beside hers «nata li 6 ottobre 1837 · morta li 9 agosto 1863» (`doc` for the notes, read at level 13 on 26 October 2026; the hand is not the register's own, and the notes give no place of death). His parents, on the facing page, are «Giorgio Franceschini» and «Antonia Benvenuti, dead». **On 28 January 1867 the same man married again: «Domenico Francesch-/ni da Montona, falegname militare congedato, vedovo della fu Maria Miletich», aged 42 (the date of birth above makes him 41), a widower, × «Maria Crisma[nich] da Pisino, inserviente nell'ospedale», aged 26** (Liber IV, p. 137, entry 4, image 430, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-R9QC-J?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-T3F); `doc`, the groom's cell read at level 13; the bride's surname «Crisma-» at level 13 and «Crismanich» on the parents' page at level 12). **His parents are again «Giorgio Franceschini, vivente, sarto» and «Antonia Benvenuti, defunta»; hers «Giuseppe Crismanich, campagnolo».** The names of the first wife and of both parents, the town and the trade are the same in both entries, so these are one man (`inf`, firm; the 1857–63 baptisms of this house call him a mason, the marriage books a joiner). **The two together fix the widow of 1872 in one way and leave her open in another:** Maria Miletich was dead nine years before 1872, so «Maria, vedova di Domenico Franceschi» is not she. If the Domenico meant is this one, who died on 1 January 1868, the widow is **Maria Crismanich**, a widow of nearly five years (`inf`, plausible and not proved: the entry gives only a dead husband's name, and another Domenico Franceschi may have lived at Pola). *A near-name, not Defranceschi, and not counted: told because it answers the question the paragraph before it left open.* His brother Luigi-Antonio, a smith of Montona, was married at Pola on 6 February 1861 (Liber IV, p. 29, entry 4, image 375, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-R9QR-Z?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-T3F); `doc`, level 13), the parents given there again as «Giorgio Franceschini» and «Antonia Benvenuti, dead».

***⭐⭐ A second son of Gračišće house 5 — in the Austrian navy.*** **On 16 January 1871, in the k.u.k. naval parish of Pola, «Defranceschi Johann, k.k. Marinediener 4. Cl.» — born at «Galignana in Istrien», son of «Franz Defranceschi, Besitzer» and **Franziska née Salomon** — married Paula Pietra, 19, born at Pola** ([the entry](/person/johann-joannes-defranceschi-navy-servant-1833/); `doc`). *He is, `inf`, the Joannes of 1833 in h116 and the brother of Franciscus (the 1868 civil marriage names the same Franziska Salomon); the father's «Franz» for Joannes Baptista and the age 34 for 37 are the two discrepancies.* **He was missed by the civil read, because the navy married in its own parish: the naval books are where the other Defranceschi men who served at Pola will be.**

***⭐⭐ The first child, in 1871 — and a marriage in 1927.*** **On 19 October 1871, at Pola, «Raimund Johann» was born, son of «Defranceschi Johann, k.k. Marinediener 4. Cl.» and «Paula Petra, daughter of Peter Rocco, Besitzer, from Pola»; he was baptised on 12 November, nine months after his parents' marriage. A note added later records that on 21 December 1927 he married «Sofia Kiroly» [uncertain] in a parish whose name is abbreviated «S. Ant. Taum.» — St Anthony Thaumaturgus, which at Trieste is the Sant'Antonio Taumaturgo** ([the baptism](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-2CRN?cc=2040054&wc=9R2C-K68); [his page](/person/raimund-johann-defranceschi-1871/); `doc`). *The Trieste marriage register of December 1927 has not been read for him.*

***⭐⭐ A baby, in 1874.*** **On 2 October 1874, at Pola, «Defranceschi Anton, ehel. Sohn des Johann Defranceschi, k.k. Marinediener 3. Cl.», born at Pola, aged 7 months, died of convulsions and was buried on the naval cemetery two days later** ([the entry](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-2D2Z?cc=2040054&wc=9R2C-7MW); [his page](/person/anton-defranceschi-1874/); `doc`). *`inf` — strong — that he is the first child of Johann and Paula Pietra, born 14 March 1874 — the naval baptism book has the child as «Peter Nicolaus», son of «Defranceschi Johann, k.k. Marinediener 3. Cl.» and «Paula Petra» ([the baptism](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-2C5R?cc=2040054&wc=9R2C-K68); baptised 10 May 1874; `doc`), the only child of this father in 1874, and a baby born in March is in his seventh month in October; the two books give different forenames, unreconciled. Eight years later their daughter, then their son — three children dead young — two others, Raimund Johann (1871) and Johann Carl (1881), grew up and married.*

***⭐⭐ And the one who grew up, in 1881 and 1911.*** **On 2 April 1881, at Pola, «Johann Carl», son of «Defranceschi Johann, k.k. Marinediener 2. Cl., aus Galignana in Istrien» and «Paula Petra, daughter of Peter Rocco, Besitzer, from Pola», was born; he was baptised on 19 April. A note added to his baptism entry records that on 10 July 1911 he was married in the Pola cathedral to Ida Revelant** ([the baptism](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-PWSZ?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-K6L); [his page](/person/johann-carl-defranceschi-1881/); `doc`). **His bride's own baptism is now read:** *[Ida Rosa Francisca Revelant](/person/ida-rosa-francisca-revelant-defranceschi-1876/), born at Pola on 27 April 1876 to a mason from Tarcento in Friuli and Theresia Fortis of Modena, legitimised by their marriage in Italy in 1878, carries the note «juncta est matrimonio die 10. VII. 1911 cum De Franceschi Joanne»* ([image](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99F-79LK?cc=2040054&wc=9R26-BZQ), `doc`). *He is one of two of the couple's five known children to reach adulthood (the other is Raimund Johann, above). The cathedral marriage book of 1911 has not yet been read for him; it should name his bride's parents and his own.*

***⭐⭐ A little girl, in 1882.*** **On 4 August 1882, at Pola, «Francisca Antonia Defranceschi, ehel. Tochter des Johann Defranceschi, k.k. Marine-Dieners», born at Pola, aged 4½, died of diphtheria and was buried on the naval cemetery the next day** ([the entry](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-RV4S?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-FMQ); [her page](/person/francisca-antonia-defranceschi-1878/); `doc`). **`doc` that she is Johann and Paula's daughter: her baptism at Pola names «Defranceschi Johann, k.k. Marinediener 2. Cl., aus Galignana in Istrien» and «Paula Petra, daughter of Peter Rocco», and gives her birth as 24 January 1878** ([the baptism](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-PWXX?cc=2040054&wc=9R2Z-K6L); baptised 17 September 1878). * Seven months later her mother died of lung tuberculosis (next entry); eight years after that their son.*

***⭐⭐ And his wife, twelve years on.*** **On 27 February 1883, in the civil hospital at Pola, «Defranceschi Paula Pietra, Gattin des Johann Defranceschi, k.k. Marine-Diener 2. Cl.» died of lung tuberculosis, aged 31½, born at Pola, daughter of «Peter Rocco, Landtaglöhner»; she was buried on the naval cemetery on 1 March** ([the entry](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-RN6X?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-6YS); [her page](/person/paula-pietra-defranceschi-1851/); `doc`). *She is Paula Pietra of the 1871 marriage — the husband's name and rank, the birthplace Pola and the age agree, and the father's «Rocco» recurs; no child is named, and his own death and any second marriage are still not found.*

***⭐⭐ And their boy, seven years after that.*** **On 10 November 1890, in the civil hospital at Pola, «Defranceschi Eugen Josef, ehel. Sohn des Johann Defranceschi, k.u.k. Marine-Diener», born at Pola, aged 14, died of a fractured skull; he was buried on the naval cemetery on 12 November** ([the entry](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-RKX2?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-N35); [his page](/person/eugen-josef-defranceschi-1876/); `doc`). **`doc` that he is the child of Johann and Paula Pietra: the naval baptism book has «Eugen Josef», born at Pola 8 December 1875, baptised 26 February 1876, son of «Defranceschi Johann, k.k. Marinediener 3. Cl.» and «Paula Petra»** ([the baptism](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899X-2H4B?cc=2040054&wc=9R2C-K68)). *He was 14 years 11 months old at death. Johann's own death is not found.*

**And the Dobrez brother, a third time.** *On 19 February 1898 Franciscus Paulus Maria Dobrez — a shoemaker born at **Parenzo** on 28 August 1865 — married Joanna Zonta of Veglia; his mother is again «Defranceschi Maria»* ([the entry](/person/franciscus-paulus-maria-dobrez-1865/), `doc`). *Three weddings at Pula (1883, 1884, 1898) now name Maria Defranceschi as the mother of Dobrez children born at Visinada, Kaštelir and Parenzo: she is a woman of the Poreč hinterland, and her own baptism is the entry still to find there.*

***⭐ And the youngest sister, baptised at Pola in 1867 — with her mother's father named.*** **On 15 December 1867 «Egidia Maria», born on 17 September, was baptised at the cathedral — the daughter of «Giuseppe Dobrez fu Antonio da Verpinaz, marinajo» and «Maria Defranceschi fu Antonio da Visinada»** (Pula births 1857–68, Liber VI, p. 362, entry 344, [image 372](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99F-76SQ?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8); [her page](/person/egidia-maria-dobrez-1867/); `doc`). *This is the fifth Dobrez child of the household, and the first read on a baptism page rather than a wedding: the family is **at Pola in 1867**, two years after the youngest brother was born at Parenzo, the father then a sailor (a carpenter on the 1883–84 weddings). And it names **Maria's father — «fu Antonio», of Visinada, dead by 1867**: the first thing the archive has about her own family. The midwife's cell reads «Maria Defranceschi» as well — the same name; whether the mother is written twice, the clerk slipped, or a kinswoman delivered the child, the page does not say. A margin fraction «23/18 over 8/71» may mark the girl's death in August 1871 (`inf`; the 1871 death book is not read).* *The Visinada Antonio is still to be placed: no Defranceschi Antonio of the Vižinada–Kaštelir cluster in the archive has a daughter Maria on a read page.*

***A midwife named Dobrez, in the 1868–71 baptism book — and a second Dobrez family from Veprinaz.*** **Through the Pula births book of 1869–75 (Liber VII, read page by page to p. 377, 23 February 1873) the midwife's cell reads «Maria Dobrez» (written «Dobreg» and «Dobrec» too) on dozens of entries (at least 73 by p. 111, and many more since), and on several she herself baptises «per urgenza».** *Whose wife she is the pages do not say.* Beside Joseph Dobrez of h073, whose wife is Maria Defranceschi, the book holds a second Dobrez household: **«Matteo Dobrez fu Andrea da Veprinaz, distretto di Fiume (Volosca)», calafato in 1868 and falegname in 1871, with «Agostina» (Cergnan, then Fregnar, di Francesco, of Fersato near Fiume)** — a son Francesco Matteo, baptised 16 August 1868 (entry 275), and a daughter «Maria Egidia», born 13 November 1871 and baptised on 3 December (p. 267, entry 156, image 550, the midwife «Maria Dobrez» on that page too). **A third child of Matteo's household is on p. 372: «Nicolò Antonio», born 27 January 1873 and baptised on 2 February, son of «Matteo Dobretz fu Andrea da Leprinaz presso Volosca, falegname» (the village's name read at level 12 as «Leprina…», the Veprinaz of the other entries) and «Giustina Cernjar di Francesco da Fiume» (entry 56, image 603, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99F-7Z7L?cc=2040054&wc=9R2X-SP8); `doc`; the midwife this time Antonia Gotthardi, not Maria Dobrez).** The wife's name has been written Agostina Cergnan and Fregnar before; the Fiume father Francesco is the same. Joseph's father is «Antonio» of Veprinaz, Matteo's «Andrea» of the same village: two Veprinaz Dobrez families at Pola in the same years, and a Dobrez midwife who may belong to either. `inf`, undecided: one reading is that she is Matteo's wife, not Maria Defranceschi, since Matteo's household has children baptised through these same years; but nothing on the pages ties her to either man, and the page of 1867 that wrote «Maria Defranceschi» in the midwife's cell for Joseph's own daughter shows the clerks were not always careful. *No entry of the name Defranceschi was found beside any of them in the 1869–71 pages read.*

***⭐ And a child from Medulin, in the war.*** **On 8 November 1915, at Pola, «Ivan Defranceski», born at Medulin and aged 3½, died of pneumonia and heart failure; he was buried on 10 November** ([the entry](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899F-XDHQ?cc=2040054&wc=9R2F-927); [his page](/person/ivan-defranceski-1912/); `doc`). *The entry names no parents. He is born about 1912, in the parish where the surname otherwise appears only through daughters; the Medulin baptism of that year is not on the film.*

***⭐⭐ And another Ivan, five weeks later — from Ližnjan.*** **On 10 December 1915, at Pola, «Ivan Defrančeski — Antoni e Justina Visdarich», born at Ližnjan, aged 7, died of scarlet fever and was buried on 11 December** ([the entry](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-899F-X8GP?cc=2040054&wc=9R2F-927); [his page](/person/ivan-defranceski-1908/); `doc`). *A different child from the Medulin boy above. His parents are named; the archive has no Justina Visdarich and no Antonio of the right age with a read register, so the family is not yet placed.*

***⭐ A widower's second marriage at Pola, 1824 — the index's Francesco opened on the page.*** **On 18 November 1824, at Pola, «Francesco De Franceschi», agricoltore, aged 48 and a widower («vedovo»), married «Domenica Filipich», aged 38 and unmarried; his parents are written «Michael De Franceschi, morto» and «Maddalena Bubich, morta», hers «Giorgio Filipich, morto» and «Maria Filipich, sua moglie, morta»; the witnesses are «Martin Cetich» and «Francesco Ugo», both unmarried, and the priest Don Giovanni Cuizza, cappellano curato** (Pula marriages 1815–77, Liber III, p. 10 for the groom and his parents and p. 11 for the bride's parents, witnesses and priest, image 269 of waypoint 9R28-T3F, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-R9SN-9?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-T3F); `doc`, read at level 13; no house number is given for either of them). *This is not a discovery: the FamilySearch index already held the couple* — two rows «Francesco De Franceschi, b. 1776, spouse Domenica Filipich, parents Maddalena Bubich and Michael De Franceschi» (6YB5-XFRY and 6YB5-XFRB) — *and the roster holds a Pula burial «Francesco De Franceschi, b. 1775, d. 1827»* (1:1:6BKV-2V6P). **What the page adds is the age, 48, which makes the index's «1776» an age-derived year, and the widowhood.** The man of the burial of 1827 is very probably this one — the same name, the same town, and an age that fits (`inf`; the burial entry itself is not yet read, and the two roster rows are not merged). *What is not known:* his first wife and any children (the first marriage lies before 1815, in the 1685–1818 prose book of the same film, not yet walked); where his parents Michael and Maddalena came from — **Bubich is a surname of Gologorica in this archive's own registers, and nothing on this page links him to that village** (`inf`, no more than a coincidence of a name). **Next: the burial of 1827 at Pola (9R2Z-4WB, Pula deaths 1716–1864) and his first marriage.**

***The Vodnjan weaver Cristoforo De Franceschi as a witness at Pola, 1835.*** **On 30 April 1835 «Giovanni Roditti q. Anastasio and Bernardina da Vanzo», a widower of Dignano, and «Andrianna Biasiol di Francesco and Antonia Francin» (the bride's mother a Francin, the near-name, not counted), of Dignano, were entered in the Pola marriage book — the marriage itself was made at the parish office of Dignano, where the papers lie, and the Pola entry only records it; the witnesses are «Cristoforo De Fran-/ceschi q. Giuseppe, Tessitore» and «Luigi Fabro, Sarto»** (Pula marriages 1815–77, Liber III, p. 41, image 284 of waypoint 9R28-T3F, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99X-R9S2-6?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-T3F); `doc`, the surname split across the line end and read at level 13: «De Fran-» then «ceschi»; the priest was Don Giacomo Dari, curato). *Dignano is Vodnjan, and a «Cristoforo De Franceschi di Giuseppe — Tessitore», a weaver, a brother of the priest Don Stefano, is already in this archive as a witness at Vodnjan in 1818* ([his row](/person/cristoforo-de-franceschi-1824-2/)). **The father's name, the trade and the town agree, so this is almost certainly the same man, seventeen years on (`inf`, firm): a Vodnjan weaver of the name lending his signature, here his name only, to a neighbours' wedding.** *It adds no person; it adds a date to a weaver's life (alive on 30 April 1835) and a second witness-line to the one the archive had.* **The Vodnjan marriage book of 1835 holds the original entry** (not yet read for this couple).

***⭐ A mother «di Franceschi» in a Trieste bride's marriage entry at Pola, 1863 — new in this book.*** **On 4 February 1863, in the cathedral, «Andrea-Nicolò Petris di Pola, Negoziante», aged 32, house 303, was married to «Catterina-Cristina Ilovar di Trieste», aged 25, house 320** (Pola marriages 1858–73, Liber IV copulatorum, p. 61, entry 6, image 392 of waypoint 9R28-T3F, [open](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G99X-R9Q8-5?cc=2040054&wc=9R28-T3F); banns read on 16, 21 and 23 November 1862; `doc`). **The parents' page (p. 62) names the bride's parents as «Giuseppe Ilovar, cattolico, Mastro-muratore» and «Maria di / Franceschi: cattolica: defonta»** — her mother, already dead — the line broken after «di», the surname plain and ending in -chi, read at level 13 on the page image (`doc` for the entry as written). The first letter of the family name is an I-shaped capital in the bride's cell and the same in the father's, so «Ilovar» is the reading and «Novar» is not excluded (`inf`). **The entry gives the mother no age, no birthplace and no father; it does not say where the couple lived, and the only town it names is the bride's, Trieste.** «Di Franceschi» is a spelling the archive's own scope list counts, so it is told here; whether she belongs to the Defranceschi stock the page does not say, and **she is not merged with any row**. Before saying so, the archive's `sources.json`, `searched.json` and `roster.json` were searched for the names Ilovar, Novar and Petris: none stands in them, so this is a first sight and not a re-read. **Next:** the bride's baptism at Trieste about 1837 (aged 25 in February 1863), and her parents' marriage, probably at Trieste in the 1830s, are the two records that could name this Maria's own father and place; neither has been opened. **Updated 15 November 2026: Maria's own death is found — «Maria moglie di Giuseppe Illovar di Trieste, nata Defrancaschi f. Antonio», 20 November 1860, aged 50, house 326, in the cathedral's death book (image 619 of 9R2Z-4WB; told in the paragraph on the registers of 1830–1864 below); so «whether she belongs to the Defranceschi stock» is answered on the name — a Defrancaschi, daughter of an Antonio — and not on the line, which is still not shown.** **Updated 16 November 2026: the census of Pola (item 3 of 9R2D-6YQ) enters the same household twice — in house 320 as «Maria Difranceschi q. Antonio Tintori di Vidusina», wife of Giuseppe Illovar q. Martino of Trieste, dead 20 November 1860, mother of Caterina Cristina (born 3 October 1837), and in house 305 as the wife of Andrea Petris, «della q. Maria di Franceschi di Trieste», dead 20 April 1868; the identity with the dead Maria of the 1860 death entry is now `doc`.**

***The last of the old Pula baptism books, 1800–1817, and the confirmation lists bound behind it — read 13 November 2026 (FamilySearch 9R2X-SPV, film 392388301, 79 images, the continuation of the births book 1767–1817).*** **One book, in two series, no table:** Italian paragraphs under a centred «Adi …», 22 September 1800 to 2 February 1812 (ending «Finis»), then a second series from 2 February 1812 to 16 December 1817; the catalogue's «Baptisms 1773–1825» is wrong for this film, which holds no baptism after 1817. Behind the baptisms are lists of confirmations: Pola cathedral 1773–92, 1792–96, 1797–1801 and 3–6 October 1825, and a list of men dated January 1815. **The baptisms (images 7–54, every page displayed by readers at page size, none of it zoomed except where said): no Defranceschi baptism, no Kovačina, no Kalanj.** **One cell was a candidate on the first reading and is now settled as not the name (zoomed at level 13 and enlarged threefold on 15 November 2026):** the entry is of **1 November 1813** — «Prio 9bre 1813», image 45 right, old folio 165, between the entries of 17 October and 12 November, the child born on the 29th of the previous October; the first pass had it as 1 October, born 29 September, and the [search register](/searched/) row of 13 November still carries that reading — «Francesco Sacco», son of «Domenico De Fran?e q.m Zuanne» and «D.a Margherita nata Baldin…», godparents the Sig.r Antonio S…(?) and the Sig.ra Francesca Artusi (`doc`). **The father's surname is five or six letters ending in -e, «De Frame» or «De Fran?e», with nothing like -schi, and neither the «Franc-» with a flourish of the first pass nor a Defranca or Franceschi; it is not counted, and the letters after the *Fr* are not settled.** **The confirmation lists, where the name stands plainly (`doc`, level 13, checked by me on the saved zooms):** in the list of June 1792 (image 67 right, p. 187) a sponsor «Elena de Francarki», a sponsor «Lucia di Franceschi» and a candidate «… filia Jacobi di Francaschi» (the scribe's *a* and *e* are alike, so the spelling is Francaschi/Franceschi); in the list of 6 October 1825 (image 60 left, folio 180, under the head «idem», i.e. Promontore) «**Nadalina De Franceschi di Gregorio**» and «**Maria De Franceschi q.m Matteo**». **The rest of the 1792 group, zoomed to level 13 on 16 November 2026 (images 67–69; the church is named in every heading: «in Sacello Episcopali» — the bishop's chapel at Pola, the bishop Giovanni Domenico Juras confirming; no parish, so these are not Pomer or Promontore lists):** the June list of image 67 right is dated **3 June 1792** and reads «**Elena de Francaschi**» (sponsor), «**Maria de Francaschi**» (candidate), «**Marina [or Maria] filia Jacobi de Francaschi**» (candidate) and «**Lucia de Francaschi**» (sponsor, twice) — the same word every time, with the *a* of «Franc-**a**-schi» plain at level 13 (my earlier «Francarki» and «Franceschi» were the same word; the scribe's *s* and *r* look alike), so **the spelling of the 1792 lists is «de Francaschi» — the Atlas's attested form Defrancaschi, the particle spaced, which is typography and not a new spelling.** On image 68 (10 June 1792): left page, a candidate «**Nicolina filia Bartholomei de Franc-e/a-sch-?**» (sponsor Margaritta Lucon; the vowel after *Franc* and the ending -schi or -scha are not settled), and on the right page a sponsor «**Michael de Francaschi**» (beside the candidate Franciscus, son of Andreas J…; plain at level 13) and, at the foot, a candidate «**Lucia de Francaschi**» (no parent entered) with a sponsor whose first name is Anthea or Andrea de Francaschi (it is not Mathea). `doc` for each cell as written; the readers' «Mathea» is not supported. **So the cathedral's confirmation lists of June 1792 hold at least six people called «de Francaschi» — fathers Jacobus and Bartholomeus named, a Michael, an Andrea/Anthea, Elena, Lucia, Maria, Nicolina — none with a place and none tied to a household.** They are the same spelling as the 1860 death entry's «Defrancaschi» (images 619 of 9R2Z-4WB), sixty-eight years earlier in the same diocese; **nothing joins them, and the archive does not.** The «Michael» of 1792 may be the Michael of Pomer of 1815 (`inf`, a name only).  **Two more cells of the 1825 and 1799 lists, zoomed the same day:** in the list headed «Annotazione delli Confermati nel giorno 3 8bre 1825 … Vescovo della Diocesi di Cittanova», continued «Adi 4 8bre 1825» (image 55 right, entry 4; level 13, checked by me on the saved zoom): «**Vitorio De Franceschi del fu Vitorio, Fasana**» — a youth confirmed at Pola whose father Vitorio was already dead and who was of **Fasana**; the surname is plain, F-r-a-n-c-e-s-c-h-i (`doc`). It may be the Vitorio of Fasana born 1813 in the family tree's rows (`inf`, not merged; he would have been 12). And in the Promontore list of 1799 (image 74 left, «Adi … 8bre 1799», the scribe writing *n* as a minim stroke) «**Zorzi figlio di Gregorio de Fr[a]xcepli[?] del Prom.te**», padrino Zuanne Blessich: *Franc-e* and then letters that are not settled (-esch-i fits and is not excluded; not -esco, not Francovich) — a **Gregorio of Promontore** whose son Zorzi was confirmed in 1799 and, if the same Gregorio, whose daughter «Nadalina De Franceschi di Gregorio» is in the Promontore column of 1825 (`inf`, weak: the same father's name and place, thirteen years apart; nothing says it is one man).  **Two cells the earlier paragraph called settled stay as they were:** the reader who re-zoomed 1 Oct/1 Nov 1813 (image 45 right) read the father's word as «De Franc-a/o», short, with no -sch- and a mother «Boletin» or «Bolebin» (not Baldin), and the child's second name Sazto, Sacto or Santo — which agrees with the paragraph's «not the name», and I do not count it; and «Michiel Ca?lay» of 24 April 1814 (image 47 left) is a large *C*, a small *a*, a tall blobbed stroke, *a*, *e* or *a*, and a long-tailed *y* — «Calegher», which the same scribe writes elsewhere in the book, is excluded, and Cal-ay or Kal-ay is not; no *n*, so not Kalayn/Callayn; **not counted, not settled.** *Told on this page, in two roster rows, the search register and the worklist.* ***⭐ And the men's list of January 1815 names Pomer.*** **«Francesco De Franc[e]sch[i] q.m Michiel — Pomer — 43 — ammogliato»** (image 77 right, folio 198, signed by the parish priest Giovanni Cuzza; read at level 13, the ending of the surname a flourish — `doc`, the surname's last letters not settled). `inf:` this is the Francesco whom the Pula marriage of 18 November 1824 calls the widower, 48, son of «Michael De Franceschi, morto» and «Maddalena Bubich, morta»: the same father's name, an age (43 in 1815, 48 in 1824) that agrees to within a year, and «ammogliato» — married — in January 1815, which the marriage register now explains: he had married at the cathedral on 15 October 1808 (below). So he was a widower by 1824. It puts the family of Michael at **Pomer** in January 1815, a generation before Tomas «son of the late Michele», farmer at Pomer house 5, married in 1843 ([the Pomer page](/places/pomer/)). The two Michaels are not proved to be one man. Not read or not settled: the margin notes squeezed beside the baptisms on images 21, 23, 24, 26, 27 and 30; faded entries of 1813 (images 43–44); the «Michiel C?kalay» of 24 April 1814 (image 47 left, daughter Maria Luigia, baptised by the vicar canon Vidovich), zoomed on 15 November: a large looped *C*, then «-kalay» or «-kaley», **no *n***, so not the Atlas's Kalayn, Kallayn or Kalanj (which end -ayn / -anj) and not settled beyond that, not counted. Near-names seen and not counted: Fraggiacomo, Frazza/Franza, Francin, Demori, Deghenghi, Calagher/Callagher, Calabro, Calluciola, De Cal-, Cailens, Marinoni «detto Kalizzan» (a by-name).

***The Pula baptism book 1767–1800, read to its end on 13 November 2026 — and one mother of the name, in 1772 (FamilySearch 9R2X-BZ9, film roll 37, 136 images; register images 5–131, 15 August 1767 to 22 December 1800).*** **On 13 December 1772** the cathedral baptised «Antonio Lorenzo», born on the 8th, «figlio di m.r Antonio Vio q. Cro…, e di D.a Maria nata **De Franceschi** di lui legittima consorte», by the curate Don Niccolò Leonardelli, godparents Pietro Cipriotto q. Francesco and Antonio Artusio q. It is the family name at Pula as a bride's, thirty years before the Francesco of the Pomer list: Maria's father, her place of origin and her husband's trade are not given, and nothing joins her to any other person of the archive. **And the marriage book now puts a doubt beside it (13 November 2026).** On **21 May 1769** the cathedral married «M.r Ant.o Vio q.m Piero di q.ta Città in 2.do voto **e Maria de Fran.co da Dignano**, ved.a in 2.do voto» — and at level 13 that «de Fran.co» is the book's ordinary abbreviation for *Francesco*, the same shape the scribe uses for the witness «Fran.co Rota» five lines below, not a surname (`doc`). That statement rests on sonnet readers who displayed every opening (22 folders of six images), not on a walk by eye; the form «Deffranceschi» was not typed to them, and the leads of the Atlas were not; the cells below were not zoomed. Gaps and open cells: the left page of image 125 (page 220, «31 Genaro 1799») is under a pasted flap and almost all unread, an entry of 8 March 1799 is covered by a slip (image 124 right), the same opening was photographed three times (images 42–44, slips of June 1778) and images 65–70 and 95–100 are faded; Cal-/Ca- cells (Calegher, Calich of Pomer, Caligari, Calurri, «Cal?ick» of 4 June 1799, «Catabar/Calabar» of 24 January 1792) were not zoomed and none looked like a Kalanj form. Near-names not counted: Franco, Francovich, Getni, De Mori, Deghenghi, Fragiacomo, Frezza, De Vescovi, a «Francesco de Fran.co» patronymic of Bergamo (1769, zoomed), and a godmother «Agata ved.a di Francesco Fancesi/Pancesi» of 1792 (no r after Fa-, zoomed). The film overlaps the next one by one opening (22 September 1800, folio 232); there are no confirmation lists here, they are bound in 9R2X-SPV.

***⭐ And then the book behind it, all of it — 1716 to 1809, walked backwards to the head of the film (FamilySearch 9R2Z-4WB, roll 45, images 1–451 — 0-based idx 0–450, the last of them the overlap with the morning's reading; read 15 November 2026, every half-page displayed, every doubtful cell opened at level 13).*** The film's first 450 frames are **three successive books**, each with its own vellum cover, archive card and filming slate: the tail of «Mortuorum 1685–1732» (images 7–80 — its folios 1–127, and with them the years **1685 to June 1716**, are on **roll 44** and are *not* on this film), «Mortuorum 1732–1773» (images 86–257) and «Mortuorum 1773–1817» (image 264 on). They are free-running **Italian prose with no index of names** — three to eleven entries a page: a centred date, then the name, the father or the husband, often the village, the hour, «passò da questa all'altra vita» or «volò al Cielo», the age, the sacraments and the grave. The plague is in them — «il peste», from 4 July 1728 — and so is a soul-count taken in April 1732 or 1733: **276 families, about 1600 souls, 485 of them communicants**. *Six deaths of November and December 1773 are written on a loose «Pag: unica» at the front of the third book, «inavvertitam.te ommessi»; pasted slips cover entries of March 1797 and of about 1910, and in each case a second exposure of the same opening shows what is underneath.*

***⭐⭐ «Adì 28 Sett.re 1732: Passò à miglior vita l'Ill.mo Sig.r GIUSEPPE FRANCESCHI in età d'anni 46 c.a, premunito delli SS.mi Sacram.ti della Penitenza et estrema untione, fù sepolto nella Chiesa Cattedrale con l'intervento … di questo Rev.do Capit.o, … il Rev.do Sig.r Can.co V.co … et due Sacerdoti.»*** (Image 87 right, folio 2 of the 1732 book; `doc` — the surname read by me at level 13 on the saved zoom: **F-r-a-n-c-e-s-c-h-i**, with no *de* and no *di*.) Born about **1686**. He is buried **inside the cathedral**, with the chapter, the vicar canon and two priests at the grave, and styled «Illustrissimo Signore»: the funeral of a man of rank. **He is, very probably, the praetor's chancellor this archive already had.** The baptism book of the same parish carries «l'Illmo sig. **Iseppo Franceschi da Venetia, Concelliar Pretorio** in questa Città» at the font on 2 May 1715 and again that September; his wife «la sig.ra **Teresia Franceschi**, moglie del Ill.mo sig. … Cancelier Pretorio» in May and October 1730; and «Iseppo Franceschi» standing proxy for a Venetian count on 17 May 1731 — ***and after 1731 the name leaves that register altogether***, the office passing to Patrielli, Salviani, Zambusi, Minotto and Fornasari (above). **Iseppo is the Venetian form of Giuseppe.** The name, the style, the city and the year all meet: a Venetian chancellor in office at Pula from at least 1715, last named in the baptisms in May 1731, dead in September 1732 at forty-six. *(`inf`. The death entry gives no office and no birthplace; nothing but those four agreements joins the two men, and the register never writes them on one page.)* **Nothing joins him to a line of this archive.** He is of the plain name, counted as this archive counts it — record by record — and the likeliest context is the Pola family of that name among the city's nobles in Carlo de Franceschi's *L'Istria*. His page: [Giuseppe (Iseppo) Franceschi](/person/giuseppe-iseppo-franceschi-chancellor-of-pula-d-1732-d1732/).

***And in ninety-three years, nothing else of this name.*** Across all 451 images — **5 June 1716 to 8 February 1809** — there is **no Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Di Franceschi, Defranceski, Franceski or any other catalogued spelling, in any role**, and **no Kalanj form and no Kovačina form at all**. The terms typed were the Atlas catalogue's own, and `cover` exits 0 for all three families (Defranceschi, Defranceski, Defrančeski, Deffranceschi, Defranca, Defrancaschi, Defranceschy, Defrancesci, Defrancheski, Defranci, di Franceschi, De Franceschi, Franceski, Francetchi, Franchessi, Dafranceschi, Deframeschi, Defrancejchi, De Francesco, Defranceshi, Defrancesshi, Defrancischi, Defrancoschi, Defrancschi, Dofranceschi, Sefranceschi and plain Franceschi; nineteen Kalanj forms; Kovačina, Kovacina, Kovacsina, Kovacin). **The trap of this book is the patronymic.** «Un fanciullo … di And.a Bigolo **de Fran.co**» (October 1742, level 13) is *son of Francesco*, not a surname, and the form recurs through the volume; every reader of this walk was warned of it, and none of them met it as a surname. ***⭐ Maddalena Bubich is not in this register at all.*** With both halves of the film now read, the Pula cathedral parish death register runs unbroken from **5 June 1716 to 13 July 1830**, and in those hundred and fourteen years it holds **no Bubich, Bubbich or Bubich-type surname that can be hers**. Ant.o Corranich**». The death book names the Corranich of **Promontore** twice over as tenants of one Pula farm: on **15 February 1782**, «Zorzi **Corrunich** da Promontore, abitante sopra la Stanza colonica di Domenico de Mori posta presso il Molin appartenente à questa Cura», about forty — *the age cell is written over and is not clean* — with only one sacrament (image 306 left, page 75); and on **9 April 1803**, «Antonio **Coranich**, Colono di Demori», about fifty, «senza aver ricevuto Sacramenti», buried in the cemetery (image 427 right). *All four of these entries date the death to the night or evening before the day they are written under — «jeri sera alle ore 22», «nella scorsa Mattina alle ora 13», «nella scorsa notte» — so the register's date is the burial's, and the death is a day earlier. Whether Agata was of it is not shown by anything read, and the fourth letter of her name on the marriage page remains unsettled between x and z (`doc` for both burials, **open** for the link).*
