***The chancery, and the one thing this book dates.*** The register names four chancellors of the praetor between 1685 and 1716, and Sebastiano Franceschi is the first: **«Sebastian Franceschi, Can.r Pretoris»** on 12 and 30 August 1692 (above); **«Clar.mo S. Filippo Rea?soni … Can.r Pret.o»** on 15 December 1694, whose servant Perina Rossi of Pieve di Sacco, thirty, was buried that day (image 48 right, folio 45; `doc` for the entry — *I read the surname at level 13 as Re-a-?-soni and the double s is the walker's reading, not mine*); «il Clar.mo Sig.r **Cornelio Pelizzari**, Cancel.re Pretorio» on 9 August 1701, when his mother Giacomina, sixty-three, was buried, and again on 21 October 1701 (images 71 and 70; **walker's reading at page size, not confirmed — see the paragraph on Bertoša's printed list below**); and «l'Ill.mo Sig.r **Marco L[azarini?]**, Cancelier Pretorio» on 22 February 1713 (image 109 right; walker's reading at page size, the surname unsettled — see the same paragraph). ***So Sebastiano held the office in August 1692 and had lost it — or left Pula — by December 1694; no Franceschi holds it again in this book.*** *The next Franceschi in the office is Iseppo, in 1715 (the baptism book, above) — twenty-one years later, and «da Venetia».* **Whether the two are kin is not shown by anything read.** *Giuseppe, buried in 1732 at «46 c.a», was born about 1686, the year Angelo is reckoned born; a man born in 1686 and a son born in 1686 are not easily brothers, so on these approximate ages Giuseppe is not an obvious son of Sebastiano (`inf`; both ages are «c.a», and nothing is claimed).* **And the family's own burials are not here.** Across all 129 register images there is **no burial of Sebastiano, of his wife Agnes (in any of Agnes, Agnese, Agneta), or of Hieronymus Maria (or Girolamo Maria)**, at any date from 5 June 1685 to 20 July 1716, nor of Iseppo or of Teresia. They died elsewhere or after this volume — most likely they left Pula with the office, about 1693–94. *Together with the three prose books above, no Franceschi of the chancery is buried at Pula between 1685 and 1830 except Giuseppe, in 1732.* **The burial of Sebastiano and Agnes is now a question for Venice or for Dalmatia, not for Pula;** the parish's baptisms and marriages of 1685–94 would show whether they had other children here and when the household left.

***And nothing else of the three names in thirty-one years.*** In 129 register images, **5 June 1685 to 20 July 1716**, there is **no Defranceschi in any catalogued spelling, no Kalanj form and no Kovačina form, in any role** (the Atlas's `cover` exits 0 for all three families against the terms typed). **No De Franceski, De Franceschi or any other form of the name of Pomer or Promontore is buried here** — so the «Michiel de Franceski à Pomer» who stood godfather on 17 September 1715 was still alive on 20 July 1716, a small negative fact about the household and the oldest of its dates (`inf`; the walkers' page-size reading, with every cell flagged opened at level 13). Eight ordinary people of Pomer or Promontore are buried here and are context only, none of the name: among them «m.o Michiel Mamonich d.o Dorich da Prementore» (June 1686, image 7; the surname read plainly by the walker), and «Dom.ca, moglie di m.ro Massimo Chergosich di Pomer, hab.te in questa Città», thirty-three, buried in S. Teodoro on 16 July 1690 (image 27). **The trap was the patronymic again** — «de Fran.co», «S. Fran.co» (the burial church, on nearly every page) and the canon Fran.co Maure occur hundreds of times, and no reader mistook one for the surname. Near-names settled at level 13 by the walker and not counted: **Staccichi**, **Pravesc-**, **Fracastini / Fraccastini** (the bishop's executor, 1689), **Franchini** (Antonio, 1691–1700; Severiana Franchini, abbess of S. Teodoro, died 30 August 1702), **Franco** (Tomaso Franco of Bologna, 1693), **Gianco / Janco** (canons), **Cova** (Tomaso Cova, April 1703), the **Fracassini** family tomb, and **Franceschina** as a woman's forename. **Four cells are not settled, and one of them could, in principle, matter to Kalanj:** on **22 December 1715** (image 127 left, folio 124 verso, first entry) «Eufemia figliuola di mis.r **Zorzi Cal:** / **nci**, de giorni 5» — the surname breaks across the line, with a colon after *Cal*; at level 13 the second line begins *nci*, and **I read no vowel between l and n.** It matches no catalogued Kalanj form (which run -ain, -ayn, -ein, -ani), so it is **not counted**, but the colon is an abbreviation mark and the line end hides whether a letter was dropped, so it is not closed either. *The other three: «Fran.ca Temporala, Moglie di Tomaso [struck] Cova» (9 April 1703, image 78 right, a struck word beneath the surname), a cramped margin insertion of August or September 1701 whose surname is lost under a blot (image 71 right: «Morse Fran[ce]sco Nicoreo(?) dell'Ospe[dale]»), and the word after «sig. Franco» on 13 May 1716 (image 129 right).*

***The chancery in print, and what the print does and does not add.*** Slaven Bertoša's list of the administrative staff of Pula, built from these same Pula registers in the Pazin state archive (*Vjesnik istarskog arhiva* 8–10, 2001–03, [free PDF](https://hrcak.srce.hr/file/141785); I read the typeset text of the PDF, printed page 232), prints the pretorial chancellors in order, and both men are on it: **«Clarissimus Dominus Sebastianus Franceschi Cancellarius Pretorius»**, 1692, with his references *MKK 243, 1692; MKU 267, 1692* (the DAPA baptism and death books), and **«L' Illustrissimo signor Iseppo Franceschi da Venetia Cancelier Pretorio in questa Citta»**, 1715–1730 (*MKK 243 and 244*). *That checks our reading of the name and of the office; it is not a second witness, because he read the same books.* His dates are sightings, not terms of office: his Giulio Pelizzari runs 1683–1701 while Sebastiano (1692), Filippo Rexens (1694), Filippo Ronzoni (1694–95) and Stamini (1696) all fall inside it, so «1715–1730» is a first and last sighting, as ours are. **What he settles, and what he leaves.** (1) The «Filippo Rea?soni» of 15 December 1694 above shares its first name, its office and its year with his Filippo Rexens (1694) and Filippo Ronzoni (1694–95): the surname stays unsettled (`inf`), the first name Filippo does not. (2) For the two names the walker read at page size he prints **Giulio** Pelizzari (to 1701) and **Marco Gaiatini** (1711–13), so the «Cornelio» and the «L[azarini?]» above are not adopted from the walker, and I do not adopt his either: I opened the halves of images 71 and 109 and found no chancellor on them (image 71 carries 13 September to 29 October 1701, image 109 March to May 1713), so the image numbers given for those two entries are to be found again. (3) After Iseppo the chancery has two names we lacked, Giovanni Filippo Conte (1731) and Francesco Maria Zambusi (1732–45, *MKK 244, MKU 268*); Iseppo's own **1731** proxy godparenthood and his **1732** burial (above) are therefore ours alone, because his list ends at 1730 and cites baptism books only. **Two more men of the name stand in the same article and in no reading of ours:** «L' Illustre signor **Illario de Franceschi** Canceliere dell' Illustrissimo signor Conte Provveditore», 1654 (printed page 229; the Count-Provveditore's chancery, not the praetor's; *MKK 242*), and the canon **Natale de Franceschi**, who baptised Elisabetta Barbara, daughter of the count Francesco Bragadin, at Pola on 16 February 1622 (his footnote 4, *MKK 242*; I read his transcription, not the page). Four men of the name at Pola in 110 years, three of them in or beside the chancery, **none a Defranceschi**, and no kinship between any two shown. **One check against a sentence this archive already carries.** [The lines page](/lines/) quotes Carlo De Franceschi's *L'Istria* as naming Franceschi among the nobles of Pola «venuti da Capodistria» before 1631. The armorial of Pola's families (Ondina Krnjak and Giovanni Radossi, *Atti del Centro di ricerche storiche, Rovigno* 26, 1996, [free PDF](https://hrcak.srce.hr/file/352695)) has no Franceschi entry (its numbered entries run 42 Fracassini, 43 Gavardo, 44 Ghisi, and «De Franceschi» occurs only in its bibliography, as the historian). That neither confirms Carlo's sentence nor refutes it, because it treats the town's old houses and not every family that came; the sentence stays as quoted, a published claim and not a record. *I have not read the Venetian side: no source found names either man outside Bertoša, and Sebastiano's Dalmatian post before 1692 is still not established.*

Nel Monasterio di San Theodoro passò à miglior vita Suor Christina(?) de franceschi Monaca conuersa in età d'anni 60 in c.a»**, to whom he had given, as ordinary confessor of the convent, all the sacraments on the 13th («li 13 instante»), and who was buried in the convent's church after a funeral with the canon Piffero, the convent's chaplain, the priests and clerics of the cathedral (`doc`). The surname is clear and small-f, **the given name is not settled**: the line breaks after «Suor» and the next word is written with a *ch* where this hand's *chr* would be, so «Chiestina» and «Christina» are both possible. **The year in the heading is written with a 7 that looks like a 3 (my first reading was «1633»): it stands as 1677 on the order of the pages** — the left-hand page runs from 15 May to 5 July 1677, the next opening runs on from July 1677 (its first entry was read as 17 July, two days before this one, which I did not look at; the curate Mario Apollonio signs from 9 August). **A conversa is a lay sister of a convent, taken in for her work, not a choir nun; at 60 she was born about 1617, in the years the curate Natale di Franceschi was baptising and Pietro's twins were born; the book says nothing of her father, her town or any kin, and the other nuns of S. Teodoro it buries (Dominica de Gobbi da Salvana in 1665, a Giacoma Boni(?) in 1679, a Felicita da Venetia in 1680, the abbess Benedetta Gosti in 1681) are given a surname or a town.** I do not join her to any man of the name: Pola's de Franceschi of her years are the curate, Pietro, Flavio, Mario and Giacomo, and any of them, or none, may have been her brother. **(4) «Sig.r Antoni di franchesti», a boy of thirteen, buried 31 May 1631 — counted on David's reading.** On **31 May 1631** (**image 27 left**, which I read at level 13) a death entry runs: **«passò à meglior vita il Sig.r Antoni di franchesti[?], d'età d'anni 13(?), fu confessato et hebbe l'olio santo, et fu sepolto alla Misericordia, Capitularmente»** — *a boy of thirteen, called «Sig.r», confessed and anointed, buried in the church of the Misericordia, with the chapter.* **What I read, and what David reads.** The letters I make out in the surname are *franch-e-s-ti*, with a final hook that could be an *i* or the stroke of *ti*, and I did not settle it from the letters alone: *a hand is only legible against itself*, and the readers found no «Franceschi» of 1631 in either of the curates' hands (Alberto del Becco and Giacomo Bonarelli alternate) to set the cell against. **David Defranceski looked at the same image on 15 November 2026 and reads the surname as «di Franceschi»; the archive counts the entry as of the plain name on that reading (`inf`: the form on the page is «franchesti», and the identification is his).** **And the age fits a family the archive already holds.** On **16 September 1617** the baptism book (told above, 9R26-YW1, image 10 right) baptises **Antonio and Beretto, twin sons of the «mag.co s.r Pietro di Franceschi»**: an Antonio baptised in September 1617 is **thirteen years and eight months old on 31 May 1631**, and the title «Sig.r» and the burial «Capitularmente» at the Misericordia, with the chapter, are those of a gentleman's son. *The name Antonio, the surname, the town and the age all fit, and that is all that fits*: the burial gives no parents, and I do not show that the boy is Pietro's son (`inf`); his twin Beretto is not named in the death book. The Record Atlas's catalogue now carries the form *Franchesti* as a «case by case» form of the plain name, on the strength of this entry. The same book also has a canon «P. Nadale de [?]» attending a burial on **4 June 1627** (image 8 left, zoomed by the reader at level 13: *Nadale de* clear, the next word lost to fading): a canon of that first name is the curate Natale, but the surname is not read, so he is not counted and no date of his death is drawn from it. **No burial of a priest Natale di Franceschi appears in 1631–1686**: where and when he died is not in this book. **What only looks like it.** The bishop **Fracassini** (1663; died 22 September 1663, whose burial is entered on 9 May 1664) and the **Franchini** of Pola (a servant of «Andriano Franchin(i) da Fiume», 1661; «la Sig.ra Ill.ma Adriana Franchini», aged 60, buried in the cathedral on 3 August 1681; Antonio, son of the late Gerolemo, confirmed in 1663; Laura, daughter of the late Gerolemo Franchini, confirmed in 1659 — the reader zoomed the 1661 and 1681 cells and read **Franchin-/Franchini**, not Franceschi), the priest **Benucci**, the **Francesco Maure** who is the curate and canon of the 1670s (a different name), «Franceschina» as a given name on many lines (Franceschina Manelli, aged 50, buried 8 January 1681, among them), the given name Francesco on many more, and **Francescovich** (1662, zoomed) are near-names and **not counted**. **Gaps in the book.** After **19 February 1640** the next entry is of 29 May 1640; after **27 October 1640** of 4 December (a month); **26 January – May 1667**; **January 1668**; **June – December 1683** (the book jumps across consecutive images with no image missing); 1632, which has two long silences (April–August and August–October); and the leaves left blank by the scribe (images 83 left and right, struck through with a diagonal stroke, and the page marked «Vacuo» at 84 right). A **loose copy of the death certificate of the bishop Fracassini**, dated 22 September 1663 and attested on 17 March 1774, lies over image 105 left; a loose leaf copying baptism certificates of 3 August 1646 and 1 February 1726 lies over image 117 right; the register text beneath the first is unreadable, and the page the second covers is readable on its neighbours (images 116 and 118 are the same left-hand page photographed again).

***⭐⭐ The Austrian navy's death registers, 1821–1850 (FamilySearch 9R28-FM9, roll 56, items 2 and 3), read on 15 November 2026 — no Defranceschi, but two soldiers of the plain name, Giovanni Maria Franceschi (December 1831) and Marco Franceschi (20 May 1832), both Venetians who died in the military hospital of S. Chiara at Venice.*** FamilySearch waypoint **9R28-FM9**, roll 56 of the Croatian State Archives' microfilm, **276 images** (the viewer's numbers), filmed at Zagreb on 22 April 1997 and labelled «Pula, matična knjiga ratne mornarice, umrlih 1821–1850»: **these are not a Pula parish book but the death registers of the Austrian navy's men, most of whom died at Venice** (the Military Hospital of S. Chiara, no. 300, and the Venice parishes), others aboard ship (Smyrna, Alexandria, Singapore on the China expedition of 1821) or in the hospitals of Trieste, Fiume, Zara, Ragusa, Cattaro and Lissa. The layout, as the readers found it: **image 1 the slate of item 2**, 2 the target, 3 the cover, 4 the inside cover; **images 5–83 the first book** (a printed «Registro Mortuario», Pag.1–78, deaths from 3 November 1821 to 1850; Pag.5 is photographed twice, images 9 and 10); **image 84 «End of item 2»**; **image 85 the slate of item 3**, 86 a target, **87 the cover of the second book** («Sterb-Register des Mar. Artl. u. Inf. Baon., Tom. secundus, vom Jahre 1823 bis 1850 excl.», the death register of the Marine Artillery and Infantry Battalion), 88 the inside cover; **images 89–255 the second book** (Pag.1–167, deaths 1821–1850, entered out of date order from about 1839); **images 256–275 its hand-written alphabetical index of surnames** (each on the right page of a spread, the left pages blank forms; Pag.168–179 are not on the film); **image 276 «End of item 3»**. The readers saw **the left page of every spread (the names, places, ages)**; **the right pages (cause of death, sacraments, annotations) were looked at only where they carried an index or an annotation, and are not read** — and the volume is not called walked. **No Defranceschi, Defranceski, Defrančeski, Deffranceschi, Defranca, Defrancaschi, Defranceschy, Defrancesci, Defrancheski or Defranci, no di or de Franceschi, no Franceski, Francetchi, Franchessi or De Francesco, and no Francesci, in any entry of either book or in the index** *(`doc` for the pages seen; the cells that could not be settled are named in the [search register](/searched/) row)*. **The plain name «Franceschi» twice, both in the second book, both of men of the battalion who died in the hospital of S. Chiara:** **(1) Giovanni Maria Franceschi**, a private («comune») of the 5th company of the Imperial-Royal Marine Battalion, **born at Venice** (Lombardo-Veneto), **aged 30**, unmarried, died in the Military Hospital of S. Chiara at Venice, house no. 300, **in December 1831** (image 150, Pag.62, first entry after 29 November; the day reads 17 and is not settled, the year follows the order of the page). The entry breaks the surname across two lines — «Franc-» at the end of one, «chi» at the start of the next — and I could not settle from the page alone whether the first part reads *Franc* or *Frane*; **the book's own index, written afterwards, gives it whole: «Franceschi Giovanni … 62»** (image 262, Pag.186, right page, read by me at page size, `doc` for the index form, `inf` that the entry means it). **(2) Marco Franceschi**, a gunner («cannoniere») in the Marine Artillery Division, a carpenter by trade (the entry's last word reads *Falegname*), **born at Venice, aged 37**, unmarried, died in the same hospital, house no. 300, **on 20 May 1832** (image 154, Pag.66; the entry sits between those of 18 and 23 May, and the day reads 20); I zoomed the surname at level 13 (the letters run F-r-a-n-c-e-s-c-h-i with a ligatured *ces*, `doc`) and the index gives **«Franceschi Marco … 66»** (image 262). **Neither is joined to any Defranceschi line**: the registers give no parents, no widows and no town in Istria or Kvarner for either, and there are many Franceschi in Venice. *Near-names, seen and zoomed, not counted:* Franzin (Giovanni, November 1831, Pag.61), Franceschini (27 April 1823, Trieste hospital, Pag.10; the index gives Petronio), Franco (Francesco, 14 August 1840), Franchin (Giovanni, 3 January 1841, born at Bologna in the province of Verona), Francesconi (Maddalena, 7 March 1843, first book, Pag.63), Branchino, and a «Sig.r Ant.o de Fraibe» (21 August 1836, a war-office protocolist born at Innsbruck). **«Francesco» as a given name, often abbreviated «Franc.o», turns up in dozens of entries and is not a surname.** *The Atlas's «leads» Dafranceschi, Deframeschi and the others were not typed to the readers; «Franchesti», added to the catalogue only this day, was not either.* An earlier note of mine, that item 3 of this roll had not been opened, was wrong: **item 3 begins at image 85 of this same waypoint** and is the second book above. Both books are now looked at on the left; what is left unread is the right-hand column of every entry, and the first book has no index of its own on the film. Told on this page, in two roster rows and in worklist row 324.

On 17 November 2026 the July 1677 witness «… de franceschi» of San Vincento in the Pula register (9R2X-BZD, images 159 right-160 left) was read again. His first name is not lost to water: it sits at the end of the previous line and is cut off by the binding gutter (`doc`, enlarged), and no second exposure of the leaf exists on the film (images 155-166 checked). The surname is plainly «franceschi»; the man beside him reads «Francesco Chenerin(?)». The only candidates are the two heads of the name at San Vincenti in the Svetvinčenat books, Andreas and Gaspar son of the late Jacobus, and nothing in the cell chooses between them (`inf`). The burial of «ser Piero di Franceschi da Pola» at Rovinj on 27 May 1619 (film 005497871, image 225) was read again as well: it names no wife, age or house, so its link to the Pula Pietro of 1616-18 stays on the name, the origin and the date (`inf`).

The June 1792 confirmation lists of Pola (9R2X-SPV) spell the group «de Francaschi» and give fathers called Jacobus and Bartholomeus. Their baptisms were looked for round Pola on 17 November 2026 and are not on FamilySearch: the Pola cathedral books of 1767-1800 hold one mother of the name only (1772), and the Pomer and Premantura books of 1731-1860, the likeliest home of these children, are at the parish office and were never filmed (`inf`). The Fažana and Premantura entries of Vittorio, his son and Gregorio are already told from the books of 16 November.

**Three Pula books read on 22 November 2026 for the Defranceschi, Kovačina and Kalanj families, and the two Sestan sisters of Gologorica found in the marriage entries of 1879 and 1882.** **The Greek-Orthodox naval pastoral death book, 1870-1885 (FamilySearch 9R28-FMH, roll 58 item 3, images 0-18)** is not a parish book: «Knjiga umrlih dušobrižništva za mornare grkopravoslavne vjeroispovijesti u Puli», about 75 entries on images 4-17, three to six a year. Read at page size by a reader, three cells zoomed: **nothing of the three families.** The only Kov- cells are Kovačević (a captain's wife, died 23 July 1882; a military chaplain; a priest of 1871-72), which are not Kovačina. The waypoint's own list holds 19 images and the catalogue says 24; the other five were not displayed to me. **The Pula marriage book 1877-1882 (9R28-JWR, roll 43, images 6-131 of the 132 the waypoint lists; the catalogue says 142).** It opens mid-book at p. 133 (no. 61, 6 August 1877), because pp. 1-132 (1874 to August 1877) are on roll 42 and not in this waypoint, and it ends with no. 86 of 2 July 1882 (p. 254). Every opening was read at page size by readers, every hit zoomed, and the two below enlarged to level 13 by me. Two entries name a Defranceschi, and both are the mother of a Sestan bride. **No. 100 of 22 November 1879 (p. 184, image 58 right; level 13 by me, `doc`).** Paulus Sablich, carpenter, born 15 January 1852 (parents Stephanus Sablic and Maria Mikolicic), marries **Francisca Sestan**, servant, **born 30 May 1856**, 23, born at «Golog-» (read Gologorica, the last letters not settled), in Pola 13 years, house 157 S. Francesco; her father «**Antonius Sestan**, catholicus, vivens, agricola», her mother «**Joanna Defranceschi**, catholica, vivens». Witnesses Petrus Radovic and Joannes Tomianovic. **No. 55 of 8 May 1882 (p. 247, image 122 right; level 13 by me, `doc`).** Georgius Vidali, sailor, born 16 April 1851 at Pyrrhani, house 231, marries **Rosa Sestan**, servant, **born 15 September 1859**, 23, born at Gologorica, in Pola 2 years, house 3; her father «Sestan Antonius, agricola», her mother «**Defranceschi Ioanna**, cathol.», the surname written out whole. Witnesses Josetto Nicolaus and Alexander Vidal, both carpenters. **They are two daughters of Antonius Sestan and Joanna née Defranceschi of Gologorica house 3** ([household h119](/households/), [the Gologorica baptisms](/gologorica-line/)): the baptism book already holds a Francisca on 30 May 1856 and a ninth child on 15 September 1859, and the Pola entries give the same days, the same parents and the same village (`inf` that they are the same girls: nothing in the Pola entries names a page of the baptism book, and the 1859 baptism as told here gives no first name; the Pola entry supplies Rosa). Joanna is therefore named by her own surname in two more hands, in 1879 and 1882, and is alive in 1879. Two girls of a Gologorica farming house went to Pola as servants, the elder at about ten. **One more entry is an open lead, not a finding.** No. 7 of 18 January 1880 (p. 186, image 60): Aloysius Fortunatus Leonardus Favonati, barber, born 1840, house 141 Piazza Foro, son of the late Jacobus Favonati and of «Teresia Franceschi», dead, marries **Antonia Ivich**, born 1856 at Gallignana (Gračišće), house 412, daughter of Josephus Ivich, farmer, living, and of «**Maria Defranceschi**», dead. At level 13 (by me) the groom's mother's surname reads «Franceschi» with no De, and the bride's mother's reads Defranceschi with the c-e pair compressed in the hand: read to the form, not letter by letter (`doc` for the cell, the identification of either woman `lead`). This archive holds two Defranceschi daughters of Gračišće houses 4 and 5 (Joanna and Francisca, born 1818 and 1819); a Maria Defranceschi, wife of a Josephus Ivich of Gračišće, is a third, and which house she came from is not said. Worklist 347. **Nothing else of the three families in the 126 images.** Near-names, not counted: Kovačić (a bride of 1877 no. 83; a groom of Idrija, 1878 no. 32; a mechanic of Senj, 1880 no. 21), Kocić with a mother Kovač (1877 no. 66), Kovatez (1880 no. 99), Covacich and Kovales (witnesses, 1881), Calcich, Calin (1880 no. 87, zoomed: C-a-l-i-n), Callaut (1881 no. 38), Calamarcovich, Franul; and the witness «Defranza» (1882 no. 37, Antonius son of Antonius, porter; zoomed three times), which is not a catalogued spelling and was not counted. **Not read:** pp. 1-132; image 130, a repaired leaf photographed upside down with four July 1882 entries of which only the date, groom, bride and age columns show; the 1882 entries after no. 86. So `walked` stays false.

name: Kaštelir
lead: Seventeen records, and — read together with Vižinada and Tar — one family across three parishes.
body: Kaštelir was for a year the densest thing in Istria this archive could document and could not explain: seventeen records of the name, four of them accepted, a hilltop village kept under Vižinada, and no lane on the branch chart running through it.

Read by image rather than by place text, the three parishes of the Poreč hinterland turn out to hold **the same people**. **Giulio (Julius) De Franceschi × Maria Ceselin** — the name is written Ceselin, Sesalin and Cedelini in three different hands — has a son **Francesco Napoleone baptised at Vižinada on 7 September 1818**, a daughter **Catharina baptised at Kaštelir in 1829**, and is himself buried at **Kaštelir on 19 September 1854**, entered as «Giulio Defranceschi, of Mattio». **Francesco Napoleone** then raises his own family at Kaštelir with **Maria Radojković** — Aloisia 1859, Josephus 1862, Margarita 1869.

A second household runs alongside it: **Angelus Defranceschi × Lucia-Antonia Rodella**, whose son **Julius is baptised at Kaštelir on 29 January 1866** and **buried at Tar on 9 March 1870**, aged four. Angelus dies at Tar in 1895.

**A third Kaštelir family leaves by the back door: Joseph Dobrez × Maria Defranceschi.** *Their daughter Catharina is baptised on 8 September 1853* (the index says Kaštelir; the page, read on 24 November 2026, is headed Vižinada, house 136: see below); *their son Antonius, a carpenter, was born at Visinada on 30 March 1855 and was at Pola «from boyhood» when he married there in February 1883 — and that marriage entry writes his mother «Defranceschi Maria»* ([the Pula wedding](/person/antonius-dobrez-1855/), `doc`; [h073](/households/)). *Maria is a Defranceschi by birth, and her own baptism is the thing still to find in the Vižinada–Kaštelir books.*

The join is by name, date and parish adjacency — no single document names two of these places at once — so it is an inference, and is marked as one. But it is the first time the hinterland has read as a family rather than as a scatter.

And it corrects this page's neighbour: **Draguč, long counted at twenty-five records, holds none.** Its three volumes were fetched and every image tested. The twenty-five were Vižinada's, returned twice by a search parameter that does not filter.

**Kaštelir death, 1873, read at the page (17 November 2026).** Maria Defranceschi, daughter of Franciscus, a tailor, house 23, died 4 March 1873 aged one and a half of continuous fever (doc, level 13).

**The Kaštelir baptism book of 1815–1830 is on the Vižinada roll (9R2Z-6TB, viewer images 52–74, read 24 November 2026).** Its first page is dated 5 October 1815 and its last entry 29 December 1830; the curates are D. Gregorius Baichin and D. Antonius Baichin, with Rusich and Filippich baptising by licence. **Julius's daughter, read at the plate (`doc`, level 13):** Catharina, baptised 9 November 1829 at house 23 by D. Antonius Baichin, curate; legitimate; father «Julius De-franceschi, Sartor, q.m Mathaei, agricola», mother «Maria n. Sesalin» (the Ceselin of the Vižinada pages), godparents Antonius Tapazenus (Topazzini?) and Helena, wife of Angelus Rusich; the cell after the father's trade reads «ex Calagnia S. Dunici…» and is unsettled (a place, not a Kalanj form). The index had placed her at Kaštelir in 1829; this is the page. **Aloysius is a godfather at Kaštelir five times, 1822–1828**, the last time «commorans ibi»: living there in November 1828 (details on [Vižinada](/places/vizinada/)). **The Dobrez baptism is not at Kaštelir:** Catharina, daughter of Josephus Dobrez and Maria Defranceschi, said above to be baptised at Kaštelir on 8 September 1853 on the index's word, is entered on a page of the joint Vižinada–Kaštelir book (9R2Z-C6K, p. 132) headed Vicinatus, at house 136, as a late entry under a decree of 3 February 1879; her marriage of 1884 gives her birthplace as Visinada. **Nil for these 23 pages for Kalanj, Kovačina and Tintori;** the terms are on the Vižinada page.

name: Bakar
lead: The deep-water bay east of Rijeka, and one of the Kvarner parishes where the surname sits in the registers with no line yet attached to it.
body: Bakar belongs with Rijeka and Ledenice in the group of Kvarner parishes this archive can name people in but cannot yet join to any line. The households here are treated as **unplaced** — documented, and honestly unattached — rather than folded into the Carnia or Pazin-county descent on the strength of a shared surname.

**Open cells of the Bakar and Crikvenica books re-read on 22 and 23 November 2026.** Forty-odd cells that earlier readings had left unsettled or unzoomed were opened again at level 13 (by a reader, with the key crops, the 1855 and 1877 mothers and the 1707 and 1798 cells, looked at again by me), and the eighteen baptism images of 9R26-HZC that were read without any zoom (images 216-221, 240-245, 486-491) were read again. **No Defranceschi, Franceschi or Franceski form and no Kovačina turned up, and no volume becomes "walked" through this.** What was settled: the nine Fran- cells of the death books 1823-1891 (9R2H-N3J) are Franiskovich, Frandrini, Franclich, Frandich, Franich and Francijović, near-names, not ours; the thirteen second-look cells of the baptisms 1843-84 (9R2C-L23) are near-names (Kalvić, Katnić, Kretina, Marlyn, Trampuh and others); the paper slip over June 1743 in the baptisms 1692-1770 (9R28-T3D, image 450) is a second exposure whose twin on image 449 shows the entries, with nothing of the three names. **What stays open, stated as readings and not as findings:** (1) the mother of entry 139 of 24 December 1855 (image 111 right, 9R2C-L23), wife of Franciscus Barić, reads «Anne Zalanj / Kalanj»: the capital is built like the K of the 1857 «Kalanj» entry of the same household (image 124 left, entry 39), but a Z is not excluded, so the 1855 sighting stays probable, not settled; (2) a godmother «rođ. Kalgna» (image 425 right, entry 100, 22 November 1877): the first letter is not settled and the form is not in the Atlas, so it is not added; (3) a godfather «Zalanyi / Kalanyi» (image 243 right, entry 4, 10 January 1864): Zalányi is also a Hungarian surname; (4) «Kovain-a / Kovačin-a», genitive, entry 155 of 4 December 1853 (image 96 right): the c is not settled and the nominative cannot be Kovačina; (5) the marriage entry of 30 October 1707 (9R2C-GPX image 30 left), «Sjn Thome [?]ranec-iſk-i» of Senische: the capital reads F, not S, against the same scribe's F in «Frankouichia», but the letters between n and k read c-i-ſ, which gives Franciski, a near-name of Franciskovich, and not Franceski; the cell stays a lead; (6) the witness «Josepho Kalani(?)» of 5 February 1804 (9R28-82Z image 212 right) reads Kalani rather than Calafatovich, with the last minims unsettled; (7) «Antonia filia Mathiae ?allancich» (9R28-DPV image 63 right, 16 October 1798): the first letter is not settled and the ending is -ancich, a Kalanč- name if it is a K; (8) «Margaritha uxor Stephani Kristoffor Fran?ji» (Crikvenica deaths, 9RKB-DPD image 382 right): leaning Franjić, still not settled after five attempts. The 1727 «alias Kallanichia» of Draga (9R2C-GPX image 71 right) was read again and stands as told. **What cannot be closed by any reading** and so keeps these volumes at "not walked": the pasted slips and torn corners of 9R2C-L23 (images 63-67, 76-77, 86-87), the water-damaged pages of 9R28-T3D (images 381-382), the faded page 581 right and image 129 left, the binding shadow over image 40 left of 9R28-DPV (the word reads Gra-, not Fran-), the 1815-1823 death book whose continuation is on the next reel, and 9R2C-GPX, whose item continues on roll 4, not opened. Worklist 348.

**The four open cells opened again with the scribes' own letters beside them (24 November 2026, by a reader; the comparison crops are the reader's, not yet looked at by me).** (1) **9R2C-L23, entry 139 of 24 December 1855** (viewer image 112, right page 198): the child is Antonia Natalia, daughter of Franciscus Barić, financial official, and «Annae [Z/K]alanj»; the same husband and the 1857 entry (viewer 125, left, entry 39) names the mother «Antoniae Kalanj», so the first name differs between the two entries (Anna in 1855, Antonia in 1857) and the entry names neither her father nor her place. The capital is built with the lead-in curl and head loop of this scribe's K but its diagonal and base bar are nearer his Z (of «Zachariam»): **the letter stays unsettled, Kalanj is probable on the husband and the 1857 entry only (`inf`).** (2) **«Kalgna», 22 November 1877** (viewer 426, right page 568, entry 100): a godmother «Jovana ro. [?]algna» in a bold hand that writes only the godparents' cells, so it has no K of its own to compare; no separate l is seen, and Čagna or Calgna are as possible as Kalgna. **Unsettled; not a catalogued Kalanj form.** (3) **9R2C-GPX, 1707** (viewer 31, left page, second entry): the son of Thomas(?) «Franceiski/Franciski Senichje»; the initial has the heavy top bar of this scribe's F (Frana, Frankouichia) and not his tall S-loop, so **F is probable and the form is bare Franceski-like, not a proven Defranceschi** (month of the page unread). (4) **9R28-82Z, p. 201, February 1804** (viewer 213, right page): «Josepho Kalani» is a witness, with Xaverio Delosta, to the marriage of Andreas Burchich(?) and Josepha Skiglich; the ending -ani is settled at level 13 and the K is probable (unlike the only Z of the page, the priest's Zaccarich). Kalani is a catalogued Kalanj form; he is a witness and nothing says he is of the Kalanj line of Ledenice. No Defranceschi or Kovačina form on any of the four pages.

name: Draguč
lead: Twenty-five records that were never here.
body: This archive's parish table has carried **Draguč, 25 records, 1784–1851** since September. On 13 September 2026 the parish's three volumes were fetched from FamilySearch and every image in them tested against a pool of 1,768 indexed records of the name. **None matched.**

The twenty-five were **Vižinada's**. FamilySearch's place parameter is a relevance boost and not a filter, and the two parishes return the same records in the same order — a thing this archive tested and published on 9 September, then went on using the number anyway for four more days.

Draguč is left on the map because the correction is worth more than the deletion. Its books exist and open in 1784; nothing says the name cannot be in an unindexed page of them. What is settled is that **nothing in the index puts it here**.

name: Premantura
lead: The last village before the cape at the bottom of Istria, and one of the southern parishes the surname holds in.
body: Premantura sits with Ližnjan, Fažana, Šišan and Vodnjan in the southern Istrian group. The households here were documented first from indexes and the Pula books; the parish's own baptism register of 1791–1834 was read on 16 November 2026 (below), its marriage book of 1800–1892 was read on 16 November 2026 (below).

**The parish office here holds Pomer's oldest books.** *Premantura was separated from Pomer in 1628–32, and the published inventory of 2008 puts Pomer's two «zajedničke» volumes — baptisms 1731–1744 with deaths 1729–1743, and baptisms 1745–1860 with marriages 1745–1866 and deaths 1745–1866 — in the parish office at Premantura, both marked temporarily unavailable.* Premantura's own earliest books (baptisms 1623–1723, marriages 1665–1722 and 1722–1790, deaths 1727–1833) are **not filmed by FamilySearch**, which holds only its baptisms of 1791–1834 and marriages of 1800–1892. See [the Pomer page](/places/pomer/).

***The Corranich of Promontore, in the Pula death book.*** Twice the cathedral's register names men «da Promontore» living as **coloni on Domenico de Mori's farm** inside the Pula parish, by the mill: «Zorzi Corrunich», about forty, dead 15 February 1782, and «Antonio Coranich, Colono di Demori», about fifty, dead 9 April 1803 — with Antonio's wife **Barbara** «da Promontore», about thirty-five, dead 25 January 1800, and his twelve-year-old daughter Anastasia in November 1802 *(all `doc`, level 13; [the Pula page](/places/pula/) gives the wording)*. **It matters here because Antonio Corranich is, in all likelihood, the first husband of the Agata who then married Francesco de Franceschi of Pomer in 1808** — which would put her first marriage, and her stepchildren, in a Promontore family that had moved to the land outside Pula. *(`inf`; the register never names her.)* An unnamed man «della Villa di Promontore» was also found dead one morning in the Pula hospital on 18 December 1754 and buried in the cathedral's sacrarium: **the register leaves his name blank**, and a gap in the line where it should be.

***⭐⭐ The Promontore baptism register 1791–1834, read on 16 November 2026 — the parents of the Premantura children, and two households of the name.*** *FamilySearch 9R26-BZF, roll 36, item 8, 77 images: the book runs from 14 March 1791 to 31 March 1834 (register pages 1–71), in Italian free text («Adi … Promontore», church of S. Lorenzo); every image was looked at once by a reader, every cell naming the surname was zoomed to level 13, and I re-read six of those crops myself (the entries of 1791, 1792, 1794, 1810, 1815 and 1827). No Kalanj and no Kovačina in any cell. The book is not called walked: some digits and struck words stay unsettled.* **Mattio de Franceschi q. Nicolò and Donna Giustina**: **Maria**, born 22 and baptised 24 November 1791 (the month written «9bre»; page 2, image 4 left, «Maria figlia di Mattio de Franceschi qm Nicolò e di Donna Giustina sua legitima consorte»), **Nicolò**, born 2 and baptised 3 May 1794 (image 8 left; the index had «Feb 1794», which is wrong), and **Nadalina**, born 13 and baptised 14 December 1796 (image 12 right) (`doc`). **Gregorio de Franceschi q. Franco and Donna Maria**: **Giorgio**, born 10 and baptised 13 September 1792 (image 5 left), and **Antonio**, born 31 December 1798 and baptised 1 January 1799 (image 15 right); **Gregorio Defranceschi and Donna Elena**: **Margarita**, with «Maria» written above, born 25 February and baptised in March 1810 (image 28 left), and **Nadalina**, born 14 and baptised 17 December 1812 (image 29 right) (`doc`). That the Gregorio of 1792–99 and the Gregorio of 1810–12 are one man with two wives is `inf`: a baptism of 16 September 1832 names «Antonio Defranceschi di Gregorio, e Nadalina Defranceschi di Gregorio» together. **Zuanne**, «figlio naturale di Maria Defranceschi», born 10 and baptised 12 January 1815, no father named (image 32 left; `doc`). **A Maria, «figlia della fu Giustina Caporalin fu moglie del fu Matteo Defranceschi»**, is the mother of a natural child baptised at home on 5 September 1827 (image 54 left; `doc`), which gives Giustina a surname, **Caporalin**, and says that Matteo was dead by 1827 (that she is the Giustina of 1791–96 is `inf`). **In other people's baptisms** the name stands as godparents: **Giorgio and Maria, «giugali Defranceschi»** (once «di Gregorio», once the wife is Margarita) eight times between 29 April 1821 and 6 June 1833; **Maria «figlia di Gregorio»** in 1828, 1829 and 1831; **Antonio and Nadalina «di Gregorio»** on 16 September 1832; **Lucia Defranceschi q. Matteo** on 11 June 1833; **Tomaso De-franceschi «della Parrochia di Pomer»** on 11 November 1832 (whether he is the Tomas who married at Pomer in 1843 is not settled); and on 8 July 1822 the mother of a baptised child is «figlia del fu **Bortolo Defranceschi** da [Pomer?]» (the place word is unsettled). **What it settles:** the parents of Maria and Nicolò (b. 1791, 1794), Giorgio, Margarita Maria and Nadalina (1810, 1812), and a mother for Zuanne; **what it does not:** nothing here joins either household to the Antonio of Promontore whose daughter Nadalina married at Pula in 1782, to the Mattio who witnessed there in 1790 (`inf` only: same name, same village), or to the Pomer household. *Not on FamilySearch:* the parish folder lists only these two books (births 1791–1834, marriages 1800–1892), checked 16 November 2026, so the baptisms and burials after 1834, where the children of these couples would be, are not online there. [Search row](/searched/).

***⭐⭐ The Premantura marriage book 1800–1892, read on 16 November 2026 — three Defranceschi marriages of Promontore, the man of 1792 married twice, Maria of 1810, and a Kalanj from Ledenice.*** *FamilySearch 9R26-BZX, roll 36, item 9 («Župa Premantura, Matična knjiga vjenčanih 1800–1892», cover «Liber I. Copulatorum, Parochiae S. Laurentii», 90 images): 85 openings, 14 October 1800 to 3 October 1892, page numbers 1–83, Latin with Italian notes and, from about 1862, Croatian spellings; every image was looked at once by a reader, every cell beginning Fran-/De Fran-/Kal-/Cov- was zoomed to level 13, and I re-read the four crops that carry the weight below (the Kalanj entry of 1886, the marriage of 20 June 1855, and Hellena of 1836). Not called walked: the right-hand pages (parents, witnesses) were read at level 12 except where named, an ink blot hides cells on images 48 and 79, and page 62 sits under a loose Momiano baptism certificate on images 66–67.* **Giorgio (b. 1792) married twice.** *On 23 January 1820* **Giorgius Defranceschi**, bachelor of Promontore, son of the living **Gregorius Defranceschi**, married **Maria Micovilovich**, daughter of Thomas (witnesses Joannes Rakich and Lucas Perissa); *on 20 June 1855* **Georgius Defranceschi, farmer, house 78 (later 95), born «10 7br 1792», widower**, married **Maria Micovilovich** (house 53, born 7 August 1826, daughter of Matthaeus and Anastasia Rosanda), his parents «**Gregorius Defranceschi**» and «**Maria nata ignoratur**» (witnesses Natalis Micovilovich and Martinus Scoco), and on *14 February 1860* his widow, «vdua dfti Georgii Defranceschi», marries Thomas Premate (`doc` for each entry; that the man of 1855 is the Giorgio baptised on 13 September 1792, born the 10th, is `inf`, close to certain: the day, month, year, house and both parents' names agree; the first wife is another Maria Micovilovich, a Thomas's daughter, so the eight godparent cells of «Giorgio and Maria, giugali» in 1821–33 are the first couple). He was alive on 20 June 1855 and dead by 14 February 1860. **Maria of 1810 is Maria Cernobori.** *On 10 February 1836* **Nicolaus Cernobori** (house 105, 32) married **Maria Defranceschi** (house 78, **26**, bachelor), daughter of the living **Gregorius Defranceschi** and **Hellena «Guicopilla»** (read at level 13 on image 22; the family name is written Iacopilla, Jukopila and Tukopila elsewhere in the book and is not settled) (`doc`). Gregorio and Elena are the parents of Margarita Maria, baptised in March 1810, born 25 February; the house number is Giorgio's own, 78 (`inf`: the age, the parents and the house agree). Her children are in the same book: **Maria**, born 8 November 1837, who marries a widower Tvesa on 20 May 1875 (her mother is «Dfta Maria Defranceschi agri.», dead by then); **Gregorius**, born 2 May 1841, m. 22 February 1865; **Michael**, born March 1845, m. 22 November 1871; **Antonius**, born 24 January 1853, m. 17 September 1878 (`doc`). Earlier marriages: **21 February 1802**, Antonius Slipsevich and **Margaritta Defranceschi** «a Pomario», daughter of the living **Valentinus**; **29 April 1806**, **Michaela Defranceschi** of Pomer (daughter of the living **Bartolomeus**) and Joannes Rakich, by dispensation from the Pola curia — her sons and daughters marry through 1855 (Olgatha Rakich 1837, Joanna Rakich 1845, Jacobus Rakich 1855); **10 July 1827**, **Maria Defranceschi** of Promontore, daughter of **Matthaeus** (alive), and Gregorius Voinich of Medulin. A **Gregorius Defranceschi, farmer,** is a witness on 8 July 1821, and **Georgius Defranceschi, illiterate farmer,** on 1 February 1853. **The next generation at Ližnjan:** *on 21 May 1884* **Matthaeus Defran-ceschi** of «Lisignanum», house 3, born 14 November 1857, son of **Matthaeus** and **Maria Primus**, married **Anna Skoko** of Promontore (witness **Gregorius Defran-ceski**) — the Ližnjan row of the same man, [told on /liznjan/](/liznjan/#births), now has the bride's own register (`doc`). **On 2 May 1888** Stephanus Bujic (farmer of Pomer, house 33, born 29 July 1859) married Pia Kosara of Promontore (born 9 November 1867), his parents written «Magdalena Bujic vidua Defranceschi» in both cells, the father's cell struck through with a cross (read at level 13). **He is Stephanus Buić of the Pomer baptism of 29 July 1859, house 33, to «Magdalena vidua Tomasi Defranceschi nata Buich», father «incognito»** (the day, the house and the mother's cell agree: `doc` for each entry, `inf` for the identity, close to certain), and the widow is Magdalena Buić, whose husband Tomas Defranceschi of Pomer died in 1858 and whose daughter Maria married at Medulin in 1874 ([the Pomer line](/places/pomer/); [the Medulin marriages](/places/medulin/)). The Pomer baptisms of 1889 and 1890 call his wife Emilia née Košara: the second given name is not settled («Pia» here). ***And a Kalanj.*** *On 8 March 1886* **Thomas Kalanj**, *artifex*, bachelor, of «**Ledenicah in Croatia**», house «No. 8», his age cell «…12 Febr. 1858», married **Maria Slipsevic Piccoli**, farmer of Promontore (house 56/59, born 10 January 1858), daughter of Antonius Slipsevic Piccoli and Joanna née Semelic; **the groom's parents are «Josephus Kalanj Agric. and Rosalia Perkovic agric.»** (witnesses Joannes Arbanasic and Matthaeus Klanfar, artifices; protocol 1886 no. 67; F. D'Elia, canon and parish priest) (`doc`, level 13, left and right pages). That he is the **Toma born 12 and baptised 15 February 1858 at Klenovica, house 22, to Josip Kalanj and Rosalia Perković** is `inf` — the same two parents' names, the same birth day and year — and [is told on the Kalanj page](/kalanj/). *Near-names seen, zoomed, not counted:* Covacić, Čalić, Kalcić, Kovačić (1892, of Lesina), Rovis. *Not on FamilySearch (the parish folder lists two books only, checked 16 November 2026):* the Premantura baptism and burial books after 1834, where the children of these couples would be; the marriages before 1800 (the 1791–92 couples' own weddings, which this book does not hold). [Search row](/searched/). ***And his end, in another register:*** «Thomas **Kalan**, Josephi e Ledenice», a widower of 45, **was found dead in the sea off Pomer on 20 April 1903** (Pomer death book, printed p. 44, read on 16 November 2026), and his wife Maria Slipčević of Promontore had died on 7 February 1899, **leaving no child** («nulla prole relicta»); told on [the Kalanj page](/kalanj/). `doc` for the entry, `inf` that he is the Toma of 1886.

name: Fažana
lead: Forty-two records, every one of them ours — and most of what this archive has been calling the Pula cluster.
body: Fažana has been a single dot on the branch chart reading «baptisms and deaths at Fasana through the 1810s, 1840s and after». Read by image it holds **forty-two records of the name between 1770 and 1855, and not one of them belongs to another family** — a cleaner return than any Istrian parish except Ližnjan.

Two households. **Vittorio De Franceschi × Stella Tamborin** — written Etella, Steffa and Samburin by four different hands — baptise Perina on 23 April 1810, Vittorio in 1813, and **Natale Mattio on 21 April 1816**. **Giuseppe De Franceschi × Giovanna Beluzzi** baptise Elisabetta in 1810 and **Irene on 13 October 1816**; a Giovanna «of Giuseppe Defranceschi» is buried as early as 1770.

Those names matter. This archive's sweep table names the **Pula** cluster's people as «Natale Mattio, Angelo, Vitorio, Elisabetta, Irene De Franceschi». **Natale Mattio, Vittorio, Elisabetta and Irene are Fažana's**, four miles up the coast — another town-name supplied by a search that could not see a town.
One entry keeps two surnames at once: **«Petrina Tamburin or Defranceschi», 1807.**

***⭐⭐ The Fasana baptism registers 1810–1852, read page by page on 16 November 2026 — two books, two households, and what became of the children.*** *FamilySearch 9R2H-BZF, roll 9, 122 images: **Libro III**, Italian prose, 15 February 1810 – 29 November 1851 (pages 1–116, images 3–64), and **Libro IV**, a Latin printed form with Italian entries, 21 February 1816 – 17 October 1852 (pages 1–94, images 70–120), a second register of the same baptisms (the entries of 1849–51 stand in both; the Greek-rite births of Peroj from 1830 are copied into pp. 65–71). Every image was looked at once by a reader, every cell naming the surname was zoomed to level 13, and I re-read ten of those crops myself (the entries of 1813 [Nicolò, on the slip], 1819, 1821, 1825, 1836, 1841 twice, 1849 and 1851, and the priest of 1823–25). No Kalanj and no Kovačina. The books are not called walked: pages 3–33, 38–44, 66–71 and most of 78–94 of Libro IV were read at level 12, with zooms on the Fran-/Kal-/Kov- cells.* **Vittorio de Franceschi q.m Nadalin (Natale) and Stella Tamborin q.m Matio**, both «nativi di Fasana»: **Perina**, baptised 23 April 1810 (born the 18th), **Vitorio**, born 24 and baptised 25 May 1813, **Natale Mattio**, baptised 21 April 1816 (born the 20th; the Libro IV copy reads the 10th), **Maria**, born 6 and baptised at home 7 December 1819 «causa periculi», dead before the ceremonies, **Matteo Giovanni**, born 7 and baptised 11 April 1821, and **Giovanni Eliseo**, baptised 20 January 1825 (born the 18th; the Libro IV copy reads the 14th) (`doc`; the mother's maiden name is written over a struck word in 1819 and 1821, and in 1825 it is left out). The father is a *bottegajo* in 1816 and a *campanaro*, bell-ringer, in the Libro IV entries of 1821 and 1825, and a godfather nine times between 1812 and 1816. **He was alive on 20 January 1825 and his widow, «Stella relitta del fu Vittorio», baptises a dying child on 17 October 1829**; the Pola confirmation list of 4 October 1825 already calls the boy «Vitorio De Franceschi del fu Vitorio, Fasana». *The death book now gives the day: Vittorio died on 20 March 1825 (see the death-book paragraph below).* **The children grown:** **Perina «Defranceschi fu Vittorio»** is godmother in 1831, 1835 and 1836, «promessi sposi» with **Antonio Tamborin di Natale** on 12 February 1836 and his wife by 12 May 1836; **Santa** (born 16, baptised 21 August 1836) and **Natale** (born 24 March 1842, baptised at home, ceremonies supplied 17 April) are theirs (`doc`; a struck entry of 20 August 1836 writes the mother «Agnesa», a slip for Perina, `inf`). **Natale Mattio, «marinajo»**, is godfather in 1836, 1837 and 1841 and father of **Stella Apolonia** by **Maria Abba fu Giacomo** — born and baptised at home on 9 February 1841, «le Cerimonie non furono praticate, perché mori li 11 detto» — and then of **Vittorio Giovanni** (born 24, baptised 26 February 1849, house 87) and **Angelo** (born 20 June, baptised 27 July 1851, house 91) by **Domenica Chersin** (`doc`); neither marriage is in these books. **The «Angelo, born 1815» of the tree is Angelo of 1851**: the index carries 1851 for the same record, and the 1815 pages hold no such baptism; the roster year is corrected. **Giuseppe de Franceschi q.m Nadalin, a fisherman, and Zuanna (Giovanna) Beluzzi:** **Elisabetta**, born 15 February 1810, **Nicolò**, born 2 May 1813 (the mother's name is not settled in that entry), and **Irene**, born 13 and baptised 18 October 1816 (the day of the heading is 16 or 18) (`doc`); that Giuseppe and Vittorio, both «q.m Nadalin», are brothers is `inf`. **The Dignano line at Fasana:** **Maria «nata Defranceschi fu Giuseppe di Dignano»**, wife of **Giovanni Moscarda fu Antonio**, mariner (house 44), has **Antonio** (born 25 January, baptised 1 February 1835, entered out of order), **Marianna** (baptised 4 March or 20 March 1838 in the two books, so the index's «Dec 1838» is wrong), **Giuseppe** (born 19, baptised 29 March 1841), **Stefano** (born 13 February 1844) and **Giovanni Epifanio** (born 6, baptised 28 January 1849), and is godmother in 1834–1839; **Don Stefano Defranceschi of Dignano** baptises by the parish priest's licence on 24 November 1825, 27 September 1832 and 8 April 1837 (the Vodnjan chapter priest [«Don Stefano di Giuseppe»](/person/don-stefano-de-franceschi-1819/) is very probably the same man, and Maria «fu Giuseppe» may be his sister: `inf`, not checked); **Pietro Defranceschi di Giovanni of Dignano** is godfather on 24 July 1831. *Near-names not counted:* Deghenghi (1841, 1844, 1845, 1850), Demori, Abba. *Not read:* the Fažana death book 1816–1859 (9R2H-Y47). [Search row](/searched/).

***⭐⭐ The Fasana death book 1816–1859, read on 16 November 2026 — Vittorio's death, the cholera of 1855, and the children who did not live.*** *FamilySearch 9R2H-Y47, roll 9, item 6 («Liber Defunctorum Ecclesiae Archi-presbyteralis SS. Cosmae et Damiani Fasanae ab anno 1816 usque ad annum 1859», 46 images, 17 March 1816 – 23 May 1859, pp. I–III then 4–76): every image looked at once by a reader, every cell naming the surname zoomed to level 13, and I re-read four of those crops myself (the entries of 20 March 1825, 3 and 6 December 1819, 10–11 February 1841, and the cholera cluster of October 1855). Pages 51–56 are a Greek-rite register of Peroi 1829–1842 bound in; none of the names is in them. Images 18 and 34 are second exposures. No Kalanj and no Kovačina; no Stefano of Dignano and no Maria née Defranceschi fu Giuseppe, who are not buried here.* **Vittorio de Franceschi, campanaro,** *male, aged 46, «morto da perniciosa letargica», on **20 March 1825**, buried by the arciprete Antonio Tesser (p. 16; `doc`); no «fu», no wife, no parents are named, so that he is the father of the baptisms is `inf`, and about as certain as the trade, the name, the village and the date can make it (he is the only Vittorio of the book before 1846, and the Pola list of 4 October 1825 calls the son «del fu Vitorio»). **His age gives a birth about 1779**, so the tree's «c1794» was fifteen years short. **His last child, Giovanni Eliseo, died four days old on 22 January 1825** («di giorni 4», «malattia non conosciuta», p. 15; `doc`), two days after the baptism, and **Maria died on 6 December 1819 aged four hours** («Maria figlia di Vittorio e di Stella di lui consorte», p. 5; `doc`; the baptism entry puts the home baptism on the 7th, so one of the two dates is a day out: not settled). **The fisherman Giuseppe and Giovanna are dead and their daughter with them:** «**Giovanna moglie di Giuseppe Defranceschi**», 48, «idropica», 21 August 1818 (p. III); «**Giuseppe Defranceschi fu Natale**», 35, 15 May 1819, «male forte di gola» (p. 4); and «**Irenne**, figlia del fu Giuseppe e della fu Giovanna di lui consorte», three years old, **burned in a fire by accident**, 3 December 1819 (p. 5) (`doc`; the ages of the parents disagree with each other and with a daughter of 1816 and are as read, not reconciled; the entry gives no Beluzzi, so that the dead Giovanna is the Zuanna Beluzzi of the baptisms is `inf`). **That settles Irene (1816): she was an orphan of three and died in 1819; Elisabetta (1810) and Nicolò (1813) are not in this book as dead, and their fate is open.** **Natale Mattio's first wife:** «**Maria nata Abbà del fu Giacomo, moglie di Natale Defranceschi fu Vittorio marinajo**», 23, «di parto, cioè d'infiammazione all'utero», died 10 and buried 12 February 1841 (p. 46, entry 11), and the next entry, «**Stella Appolonia figlia di Natale Defranceschi e della fu Maria Abbà**, marinajo», «da spasmo», died 11 and buried 12 February 1841 (`doc`, level 13; the infant's age cell is not legible) — the mother died the day after the birth of 9 February and the baby two days after it. **The cholera of 1855 at Fasana** (p. 70–71, August–October 1855, five Defranceschi): «**Natale Defranceschi**», male, 38 or 39, «collera», **30 August**; «**Stella Defranceschi**», female, 66 or 68, «di morbo collera», **11 or 18 October** (the day figure is not settled); «**Petrina Tamburin nata Defranceschi**», 48, «di morbo collera e tifo», **17 October** (`doc` each, no parents or spouses named). `inf` for the three, and close: the mariner **Natale Mattio** (b. 1816, so 39), his mother **Stella Tamborin** (the tree's b. 1789, so 66) and his sister **Perina**, wife of Antonio Tamborin (baptised in 1810, so 45; the 48 of the entry agrees with the 1807 the older index gave her, so a three-year difference of age, which is ordinary) — which would leave **Domenica Chersin a widow with Vittorio Giovanni (6) and Angelo (4)** in a year that took five of the name in seven weeks. **Another man:** «**Damiano Defranceschi fu Vittorio**, *ciabattino*» (shoemaker), 38, «febbre lenta», **8 November 1846**, house 80 (p. 61, level 13; a word struck out before the trade) — born about 1808, **before the baptism book begins**, and a son of *a* Vittorio; that he is the campanaro's eldest son, by Stella (then about 19), is `inf` only. *Near-names not counted:* Perina nata Scorzo (wife of Andrea Tamborin, 1824), the Abba family of Rovigno (Giacomo, 1837), the Moscarda entries (including Deghenghi, excluded), De Petre (1859). *Not read at level 13:* pages 1–30 and the non-target cells, which were read at level 12. [Search row](/searched/).

name: Telve
lead: In the Valsugana, east of Trento — the largest single concentration of the name outside Istria and Dalmatia in this archive's roster.
body: Twenty-two people of the surname in this archive sit at Telve, more than at any Istrian village except Vodnjan. They come out of David's family tree rather than out of a register this archive has read, and **no descent connects them to the Istrian or Carnian families**. Defranceschi is a common Trentino surname formed independently from the same patronymic; that is the working assumption here and it is an assumption, not a finding.
Telve is listed so the twenty-two are visible and counted, not folded into a line they may have nothing to do with.

name: Laives
lead: South of Bolzano in the Adige valley — a second Tyrolean cluster, and like Telve unattached to any Istrian line.
body: Eleven people of the name, from the family tree rather than from a register read here. Laives belongs with Telve, Strigno and Fiera di Primiero in the Trentino–South Tyrol group: same surname, different formation, **no documented connection to Istria**.

name: Strigno
lead: A Valsugana village a few kilometres from Telve, with the same surname and the same open question.
body: Grouped with Telve and Fiera di Primiero. Counted here rather than absorbed into an Istrian line.

name: Torrington
lead: A brass town in the Naugatuck valley of Connecticut, and the largest American landing-place in this archive.
body: Twelve people of the name in Torrington. The New England brass and clock towns took Istrian and Trentino labour in the same decades that Brooklyn took the Gallignana families, and this is where a cluster of them settled.
Nothing here has yet been checked against a federal census or a naturalisation file. **That is the next step for this place**, and it is the method that worked for the Eleven in Brooklyn.

name: Pfullingen
lead: Below the Swabian Alb, near Reutlingen — where the German leg of David's own line came to rest after 1947.
body: Anton Rudolf Defranceski appears on the Pfullingen list of foreigners in 1947 and was certified by that town's mayor in 1950. Pfullingen, Reutlingen, Neuhausen an der Erms, Metzingen and Bad Urach are one small district, and the family's German years happen inside it.
This is the leg of the journey that a walking itinerary is still owed for.

name: Postira
lead: On the north shore of Brač, with three reconstructed households of the name.
body: Postira sits with Omiš and Split in the Dalmatian group. Three households here were reconstructed from indexed records; none has been read register-page by register-page.

name: Santa Maria di Sala
lead: In the Veneto between Padua and Venice — a mainland Venetian parish carrying the name.
body: Six people, from the tree rather than from a register read here. Relevant because the Venetian line of this archive — the printers, the Grand Chancellor, the Omiš and Zadar families — is a Venetian-state story, and mainland parishes of the Republic are where its ordinary people would be.

name: Šterna
lead: «Bortolo figlio del q. Gio: Batta de Franceschi dalla Cargna» — the sentence this archive has been looking for since it began.
body: **«Alli 12 9bre 1777. Cepich. Cargna.**  Bortolo figlio del q. Gio: Batta de Franceschi **dalla Cargna**, Diocese d'Udine, ha contratto legitimo Matrimonio coll'Ill.ma Sig.a **Zanetta Gravisi** figlia dell'Ill.mo Sig.r **Marchese Nazario** della Villa di Cepich di questa Pieve, e ciò previo il di lui libero stato ottenuto dall'Ill.mo Monsig.r **Gio: Domenico Stratico Vesc.o di Cittanova**… nec non essendo stati dispensati dalle trine pubblicazioni solite farsi…»**  Read off the film at full magnification on 13 September 2026.

**This is the entry that had never been found.** The Svetvinčenat reading page says it plainly: *«What the film has not given is an origin. Not one entry in fourteen years of baptisms says where these people came from. No «da Carnia», no «di Mione», no «q. di Agrons». The Carnian identification of this household still rests entirely on the company it keeps.»* Here the priest writes it himself, in the body of the entry and again in the margin: **Cepich. Cargna.**

And the bride is a **Gravisi** — not a coincidence of spelling but the Capodistrian marquisal house, named in full: *the Illustrious Signor Marchese Nazario*, of the village of Cepich in this parish. A man from Carnia whose father is already dead marries a marquis's daughter, with the Bishop of Cittanova certifying his free status because nobody in Istria could, and with the three readings of the banns waived.

**A correction to this page, published within hours of the claim it corrects.** This archive wrote on the morning of 13 September that *«Gio Batta De Franceschi and Zanetta Gravisi… stand behind two entries in the marriage book as the parents of the groom»*. They are not the parents. **Zanetta Gravisi is Bortolo's wife.** The index lists groom, groom's father, bride, bride's father, and this archive read the four names as two couples. The page says otherwise and the page wins.

So the household reads: **Gio: Batta de Franceschi**, of Carnia, dead before 1777 and never in an Istrian register. His son **Bortolo × Zanetta Gravisi**, married 12 November 1777 — and their children baptised at Šterna from the following September: **Felice Anto 27 September 1778**, **Mariana February 1786**, **Federico 14 March 1794**, **Catarina 11 August 1797**, with a Francesco «of Bortolo» buried on 20 December 1787. The mother written *Zannetta*, *Zanetta*, *Giovana* and *Giovanna* by four hands is the same marchese's daughter. Then a second **Gio: Batta and Maria** baptising in 1807 and 1809 — the grandfather's name come round — and in July 1819 the burial of a **Bartolo, son of that Gio: Batta and Maria**. *(Corrected: this page first read that 1819 burial as Bortolo the elder «at the end of it». The entry names parents, so it is a child — a grandson carrying the grandfather's name. Bortolo's own death has not been found.)*

**The reading is confirmed twice.** Filmed with the register is an archivist's pencil finding-aid slip listing the book's notable entries, and it independently records: *«12/XI 1777 Bortolo figlio del q. Gio: Batta de Franceschi dalla Cargna con Ill.ma Sig.a Zanetta Gravisi figlia dell'Ill.mo Sig. Marchese Nazario — pag 39»*. FamilySearch's index counted that slip as a second record, which is why this archive expected two marriages and found one.

**And the parish is older than this page first said.** Šterna's filmed books were given here as running 1723–1836. They do not: the first volume is a composite of **births from 1667**, with marriages from 1688 and deaths from 1667, running to 1727. **It holds no De Franceschi at all** — 207 images, tested one by one against every record of the name this archive can reach. Which fits: there is no family of the name here in the seventeenth century, and then a man arrives from Carnia and marries a marquis's daughter in 1777.

**Who the Gravisi were.** Josip Banić's *Venetian Istria in the embrace of a nascent Dominium* (CEU doctoral dissertation, 2021) sets it out from the archival record. **Niccolò de Gravisi, son of the late Vanto, of Piran** — distinguished citizens, not nobles — uncovered a conspiracy against Venice at Padua. By a ducale of Doge **Francesco Foscari dated 10 March 1440**, he was invested with the fort of **Petrapilosa** in Istria as a hereditary fief of the Republic: «overtaken by the zeal of true loyalty… he revealed the conspiracy plotted against us and our state in Padua», so that «the very city of Padua remains preserved under our Republic». The fief was worth 150 ducats a year, the balance of his pension paid by the treasury of Koper; he was to guard the castle at his own expense and give Venice, **every St Mark's day, one candle weighing ten pounds** for the Church of St Mark. He was **not** given the *merum et mixtum imperium* — blood justice and civil appeals stayed with the podestà of Koper.

Because Petrapilosa had been the **seat of the Istrian margraves**, the house took the title *marchiones* — **the Marquises of Petrapilosa**, whom Banić calls «the most prestigious noble house of late medieval Istria», nobles «unlike any other on the entire Istrian peninsula». *(He also corrects the standard account: Venturini's 1906 family history credits Niccolò with uncovering the 1435 Marsilio conspiracy; the documents say the 1439 Scrovegni one.)*

**Petrapilosa's country is this country.** Its jurisdiction sits in the Buzet uplands with **Hum and Roč** — the same small world as Šterna, Sovinjak and Draguč. So «the Ill.mo Sig.r Marchese Nazario» whose daughter Bortolo married in 1777 is of that house, in its own territory. **What that does and does not mean.** Three hundred and thirty-seven years separate Doge Foscari's grant from this wedding, and by 1777 the Gravisi were many branches deep; a marchese living at a village like Cepich is a cadet line, not the seigneur of the castle. What the entry shows is a man who arrived from Carnia with a dead father and no Istrian parish to vouch for him marrying into the titled family of the district. Inferred — that this Nazario is of the Petrapilosa house, from the title and the district

**And one structural thing worth keeping.** Banić's population tables name only two **feudal jurisdictions** in Venetian Istria: **Petrapilosa and Svetvinčenat.** Those are the two places this archive finds the surname thickest — Svetvinčenat with 118 records from 1628, and the Šterna household in Petrapilosa's country. Seigneurial lords recruited settlers in a way communes did not, which is exactly the mechanism a Carnian immigration would use. Inferred — the coincidence is suggestive, not demonstrated

**And the district has a name and a shape.** Banić's population tables put **Buzet** at 151 hearths with «300 in the contado, *including Petrapilosa*» — and the district's later count of 4,844 is given as «**including Hum and Roč, Sovinjak, Vrh and Draguč, and the villages around Rašpor**». So Šterna, **Sovinjak** and **Draguč** — three places this archive has been treating separately — sit inside one documented administrative block, the Buzet contado with Petrapilosa's feud in it. When Venice took the Margraviate over, «the old tributes were confirmed and no new taxes introduced» in **Roč and the villages of Petrapilosa** — the citation for which is Klen's edition of the **1425 Petrapilosa tax roll**, at pages 96–97.

**The fief was the castle and twelve villages.** In **1483** Niccolò's four sons — **Vanta, Michele, Pietro and Gravis** — divided the holding: the castle itself stayed in common, «and the brothers took turns administering it, a year each». Which twelve villages they were is the one thing this archive now wants and does not have. They are in **Danilo Klen, «Urbar Petre Pilose iz 1425. godine», *Starine* 58 (1980): 85–124** — a household-level tax roll of this country, edited and printed. **It is not online.** Starine 58 is catalogued at the Croatian Academy's digital library as *In Copyright*, with no scan; four physical copies sit in the HAZU Library in Zagreb (A1-003-058, A-003-058, ČA-003-058, PA-003-058). It is a reading-room or scan request, not a download.

name: Vrsar
lead: One household, five entries, sixteen years: a christening, a widowing and a death, and then the name stops.
body: **Francesco De Franceschi and Giacoma** baptise a son, **Luca, on 11 August 1670**. **Giacoma is buried in 1683.** A **Marga «of Francesco»** is buried on 19 August 1686. **Francesco himself is buried on 26 November 1686.**

That is the whole of the name at Vrsar — five entries, three of them burials, inside sixteen years. The parish has four volumes from 1613 and nothing of the family before 1670 or after 1686. A household arrived, was recorded, and ended or moved on.
Orsera is on the coast between Poreč and Rovinj, twelve kilometres from Svetvinčenat, where a De Franceschi household is documented from 1628.

name: Plomin
lead: Above its bay on the eastern Istrian coast, at the Kvarner end of the county of Pazin.
body: Three people of the name. Plomin sits on the road between the Pazin county villages and the Kvarner shore — the same route the Carnia line is inferred to have taken to Fiume.

name: Paluzza
lead: In the Val But of Carnia, on the road to the Plöcken pass — one of the valleys the 1679 headmen's list covers.
body: Paluzza belongs with Mione, Ovaro, Muina and Givigliana in the Carnian group. The documented link to Istria is the 1679 list on which a Zuane De Franceschi of Mione is recorded working in the County of Pazin with his son; Paluzza is on the map because the walking itinerary crosses it, not because a person of the name is yet documented here.

name: Sovinjak
lead: Two burials, twenty-four years apart, and both of them a son of a Gio Battista.
body: The register holds exactly two entries for this parish and they are the whole of what is known. **Zuane Franceschi, buried at Sovignacco in 1759, son of Gio Batta Franceschi.** **Sebastiano De Franceschi, born and buried on 6 August 1783, son of Gio Battista De Franceschi** — an infant, dead in the same year he was born.

One small hill parish above Buzet; two sons of a man of that name a quarter of a century apart. It is either a father who buried a child in middle age and another in old age, or it is two generations putting the grandfather's name back into use — which is what this family does in every place where it can be watched long enough to see.

Neither reading can be tested yet. **Sovinjak is not one of the forty-three Istrian parishes in the filmed collection this archive has walked**, and no register of it has been found on any film reachable from here. The town sits on the Buzet upland with Roč, Hum, Draguč and Šterna — four more parishes carrying the name and three of them equally unfilmed. Until one of those books opens, the household stays a pair of burials and a shared Christian name.

The place was reached not by searching for it but by asking a duller question: which towns in this archive's own register have no entry in this archive's own atlas? Twenty-one did. Sovinjak was one of only five whose rows turned out to carry the family's name at all.

**And it is not as isolated as this page assumed.** Banić's figures for the Buzet contado name its constituent places outright: **Hum and Roč, Sovinjak, Vrh and Draguč, and the villages around Rašpor** — with Petrapilosa's feud inside the same count. Sovinjak is not a stray hill parish; it is one village of a district that also contains **Šterna**, where a Bortolo de Franceschi *dalla Cargna* married the daughter of a Marchese Gravisi in 1777, and **Draguč**, which holds none of the name at all. Whether the two sons of a Gio Batta buried here in 1759 and 1783 belong to that Šterna household is not shown by anything — but they are now in the same administrative country rather than in unrelated places. Inferred — shared district, not a shared family

name: Tar
lead: A man of sixty-seven buried here in 1895, and the four-year-old son he had buried twenty-five years before.
body: **Angelus Defranceschi, born 1828, died 23 April 1895 and buried at Tar the following day.** His wife is written only as **Julie**. In the same book, twenty-five years earlier: **Julius, born 1866, dead on 8 March 1870 and buried on the 9th**, son of *Angeli Defranceschi* and *Luciæ Rodella*.

So the wife the burial entry calls Julie is named in the child's entry as **Lucia Rodella**, and the boy was given his mother's name in its masculine form. That is the whole household: one couple, one child who did not live, and a man who outlived the boy by a quarter of a century.

Tar is four volumes in the filmed collection, opening in 1815 — so this household *can* be read, and has not been. It sits in the country behind Poreč with Kaštelir, Vižinada, Šterna and Draguč, the block this archive calls the Poreč hinterland: about sixty entries between them, no lane running through any of them, and not one page read by eye.

name: Pomer
lead: A Defranceschi household at house 5 from 1843 — Tomas, Magdalena Buich and three children — a daughter's nine Lazaro grandchildren, and a widow who was the village midwife.
body: Pomer sits on the bay south-east of Pula. It entered this archive on 13 September 2026 as one of twenty-one towns found in its register and missing from its atlas, on the strength of three rows spelt **Defrančichi**, none of them ours. It turned out to hold more of the name than most villages that are supposed to.

**The books were read end to end on 13–14 October 2026** — births 1816–1900 (86 frames), marriages 1837–1865 and 1885–1910, deaths 1842–1911 — and the result is a household, not a name: **Tomas Defranceschi, a farmer, son of the late Michele, married Maddalena Buich on 16 August 1843** and they had **Lucia (1844), Michele (1847, died at fourteen) and Maria (1852)** at house 5. Tomas died of typhus on 5 April 1858. A baby born to the widow in 1859 — father not named — is the Stephanus Buić who carries on in the books as «filius Magdalenae De-franceschi», with eight children of his own.

**Maria went to Medulin**, where she married Petrus Kirac and had eight children; **Lucia stayed**, married **Matheus Lazaro** in January 1866, and had **nine children 1866–1884, six of them dead before they were nine**. Their youngest, Catharina (b. 1884, d. Pula 1954), married Joannes Zuccon in 1905 — the entry that first found Lucia, because a wedding has to name the bride's mother.
**Magdalena Buich**, Tomas's widow, was born at Pomer in July 1816 and is written as the village **midwife** in 1868, 1880 and 1882 — in a book that otherwise names only Rakić, Vojak and Fabac women.

A **second household of the name** appears in 1886: Antonius, son of Antonius, **from Ližnjan**, a labourer at house 17, father of Mathias. It is not joined to Tomas's — and the Pula marriage book of 1890 shows he was born at Ližnjan in 1848, moved to Pula, lost his wife Euphemia there on 1 May 1890 and married again.
**Not found:** where Tomas and Michele came from before Pomer, and the deaths of Magdalena, Lucia and Stephanus. Full account and every entry on [the Ližnjan page](/liznjan/#pomer).

**Pomer in January 1815 — one step further back.** *The list of men bound into the Pula baptism book 1800–1817 (FamilySearch 9R2X-SPV, image 77 right, folio 198, level 13) has «Francesco De Franc[e]sch[i] q.m Michiel», from «Pomer», 43, married.* `inf:` the man whom [the Pula page](/places/pula/) holds as the widower of 1824, 48, son of Michael De Franceschi and Maddalena Bubich: a Pomer family of Michael is thus on paper in 1815, a generation before the Tomas «son of the late Michele» of 1843 above. It is not proved that Michael here and Michele there are one man, and the surname's last letters on the 1815 list are a flourish.

**Pomer in 1715 — three generations further back.** *«Michiel de Franceski à Pomer» stood godfather on 17 September 1715 at the Pula cathedral font (FamilySearch 9R2X-BZH, image 147 right, level 13; `doc`).* It is the earliest dated sighting of the name at Pomer in this archive, a century before the Francesco «q.m Michiel» of the 1815 list and a hundred and twenty-eight years before the Tomas «son of the late Michele» of 1843. `inf:` the same family, an elder Michael; not proved. The full entry is on [the Pula page](/places/pula/).

***The household the registers had been hiding, 1739–1808 — read in the Pula marriage books on 13 November 2026.*** Before Tomas of house 5, and before the Francesco of the 1815 list, there is a **Francesco de Franceschi of Pomer** whose two sons marry and witness at the Pula cathedral: **Mattio, married 5 July 1739** to a daughter of Medulin, and **Zorzi**, a witness in **February 1745**. Mattio was dead by **25 June 1777**, when his daughter **Natalina**, «Franceschi q. Mattio, della Parrochia di Pomer», married Zorzi Buich. And on **15 October 1808**, in the cathedral, «**Fran.co de Franceschi f[igli]o Michiele, in p.mo voto**» married **Agata, widow of Antonio Corranich**, «tutti due della Villa di Pomer» — the first marriage of the man who married again as a widower in 1824, and whose parents that later entry names as Michael De Franceschi and Maddalena Bubich. *All four entries `doc`, read at level 13; the full wording is on [the Pula page](/places/pula/).* **So the name stands at Pomer in 1715, 1739, 1745, 1777 and 1808.** Whether the Francesco of 1739 is a son of the Michiel who stood godfather in 1715, and whether Michiele the father of 1808 descends from him, is not shown by anything yet read: the Pomer parish registers themselves, not Pula's, are where that is settled.
