***And Pomer's own registers before 1816 survive — at Premantura (15 November 2026).*** This archive has read Pomer's books only from 1816, and assumed that was the start of them. It is not. The published inventory of Istrian parish registers (Jelinčić, Poropat and Doblanović, «Popis matičnih knjiga», *Vjesnik istarskog arhiva* 11–13, 2008) lists for **POMER**, under «zajedničke matične knjige» — one volume serving all three kinds at once — **baptisms 1731–1744 with deaths 1729–1743**, and **baptisms 1745–1860 with marriages 1745–1866 and deaths 1745–1866**, both held at the **parish office of Premantura** (`doc`, read in the published list). Pomer is a parish of its own, first named in 1632, and Premantura was separated from it in 1628–32, which is why the mother parish's books sit in the daughter's office. **The second of those volumes is where this family's own entries should be**: Natalina's marriage of 1777, the wedding of «Fran.co de Franceschi f.o Michiele» on 15 October 1808, and the baptisms and deaths of the household between them. The inventory marked both volumes «privremeno nedostupno» — temporarily unavailable — in 2008, which is not the same as lost, and nobody has asked since. **Nothing of Pomer before 1729 is in them**, so the «Michiel de Franceski à Pomer» who stood godfather at Pula in 1715 and Mattio's marriage of 1739 lie outside Pomer's own surviving books — the Pula cathedral's, where they were found, and Premantura's unfilmed baptisms of 1623–1723 are the only places left for that generation. None of Pomer's pre-1816 books is on FamilySearch: the three films this archive has read (births from 1816, marriages from 1837, deaths from 1842) are all it holds.

***And the household's three deaths, 1821–1827.*** *Michiel De Franceschi died at Pula on 29 May 1821, aged 60; Agata, «moglie di Francesco De Franceschi da Pomer», on 4 May 1824, aged 66; and Francesco himself, «nativo da Pomer», on 20 March 1827, aged 50, of a catarrhal rheumatic fever* (Pula parish death register; `doc`, all three read at level 13 — the full entries are on [the Pula page](/places/pula/)). **The men of this household died at Pula, not at Pomer**, and Pomer's own death register does not begin until 1842, so the village's books could not have told it. *Maddalena Bubich is not in the Pula register between October 1808 and July 1830.*

***⭐ And Natalina's husband, very probably, dying in the city in 1798.*** On 25 June 1777 «Zorzi **Buich** q. Michiele» married «Natalina Franceschi q. Mattio», both of the parish of Pomer ([the Pula page](/places/pula/)). The Pula death book, read to its end on 15 November 2026, has under **3 May 1798**: «**Zo[?]re Buich da POMER**, [interlined: *abitante in q.ta Città*], *in età de 42 anni in circa, heri di notte alle ore 6 passò … all'altra vita, premunito dei Sacramenti*» — so he died **on the night of 2 May** and was entered on the 3rd (image 403 left, `doc`). **⚠ The surname, the village, the age and the interlined «living in this City» I have read myself at level 13 on the saved zoom. THE GIVEN NAME I HAVE NOT SETTLED**: after a plain «Zo» the letters could make *Zorze*, *Zovre* or *Zoure*, the walker read *Zorze*, and I have not done what this archive requires of a doubtful word — found the same curate writing both candidates elsewhere in the book and compared them at one magnification. *So the join to the wedding rests on three things, not four: forty-two in 1798 puts his birth about 1756, which makes him twenty-one in 1777; the surname and the village are the wedding's; and no second Buich of Pomer is anywhere in the volume (`inf` — and the entry names neither his father nor his wife, so it is not proved).* **If it is him, a Defranceschi daughter of Pomer was widowed in the city at about forty-six**, and what became of her is not in this register: no Natalina, Nadalina or Franceschi of any spelling is buried at Pula between 1716 and 1830. *A «Michiel Buich detto Chirel-» of 1812 is in the later book and is a different man.*

***And the one thing the Pula books can no longer be asked.*** With the cathedral's death register now read whole — **5 June 1716 to 13 July 1830**, three prose books and the printed Liber Defunctorum, roll 45 images 1–498 — the deaths of this household that are **not** in it are as firm as the three that are: **Maddalena Bubich**, Francesco's mother; **Francesco the elder** of the 1739 and 1745 marriages, and his sons **Mattio** (dead by 1777) and **Zorzi**; **Natalina**; and the **Antonio** of Premantura whose daughter married in 1782. *None of them died in the Pula parish.* The pre-1816 Pomer registers, held at **Premantura** ([the Premantura page](/places/premantura/)), are now the only place left to ask.

***The three Pomer books read again for Kalanj and Kovačina, 16 November 2026 — and one death at sea.*** The books were first read end to end on 13–14 October for Defranceschi only. Read again entry by entry for the Kalanj and Kovačina forms (187 images): **no Kovačina, and no Kalanj in a baptism, marriage, godparent or witness cell — only one death: «Thomas Kalan, Josephi e Ledenice in Croatia, murator, viduus», found dead in the sea on 20 April 1903, aged 45** (death book, printed p. 44), the Toma Kalanj of Ledenice who married at Premantura in 1886 (`inf`); he was a *vagus*, living on a hill called «Zotter», and is not of a Pomer house. Told on [the Kalanj page](/kalanj/). Gaps, said there: the names half of the first marriage sheet of 1885 is not on the film.

name: Krbune
lead: One volume, 124 images, and a De Franceschi daughter's whole family inside it.
body: Krbune is a hamlet in the County of Pazin, four kilometres from Gologorica — the same small country this archive's own line lives in. FamilySearch has **one book** of it, 124 images.

That book holds **Mariana De Franceschi and Vincentius Marziol**: **Maria**, **Rosaria** 1833, **Franciscus** 21 November 1836, **Anna** 16 November 1839, **Antonia** 17 March 1843 — and four further entries where the couple stand godparent to other families' children.

She looked like several women because the index spells her husband four ways — *Marziol*, *Marizo*, *Marjas*, *Marjiol* — and her own name *Mariana*, *Marianna*, and in the Croatian orthography of the 1830s **«Marianna Defrančeški»**. One woman, one village, eleven entries.
She is **not** the Mariana De Franceschi born at Šterna in February 1786; that one would have been fifty-seven at the last of these births.

name: Dubrovnik
lead: Fifty-six records with no town written on them, and a family of the name in the old Republic.
body: Dubrovnik is the largest thing in this archive's index that has never had a page. Resolved through the films their images sit on, **fifty-six records** of the name belong to the city parish and to **Pile** outside the western gate — against the twenty-two and sixteen the parish table has carried. Not one of them says «Dubrovnik» in its place field.

The household that can be followed is a **Marietta Defranceschi**, daughter of a **Pietro Defranceschi**, who marries **Matteo Persich** — later written **Peršić** — and whose children are baptised in the city: **Cattarina Teresa Vittoria Maria in 1863** and **Giustino Antonio Alberto Lucciano in 1871**. An Antonio Persich marries a Maria Defranceschi in 1853. The 1829 entry that names Pietro is a marriage, forty-two years before the last of the children, so more than one generation of Persich is in these rows and this page will not pretend to sort them yet.

Nothing joins any of it to the Venetian line at Zadar, Omiš and Imotski, or to Istria. Ragusa was a separate republic with its own patriciate and its own trade, and a Franceschi there needs its own argument, not an inherited one.

name: Labin
lead: The oldest books in the Istrian catalogue — from 1536 — and a family that only shows up three centuries into them.
body: Labin's eleven volumes open in **1536**, the earliest of any Istrian parish FamilySearch has filmed, and they have never been read here.

The archive has carried «Labin 1615 — Aloÿsius Defranceschi» as **the single earliest indexed occurrence of the surname anywhere in Istria**. Read by image against the parish's own books, that entry is not in the pool this archive can see, and the records that *are* run **1826–1866**. The 1615 is not withdrawn — it may sit in a harvest this pass did not reach — but it is not confirmed either, and the honest statement is that Labin's confirmed run begins two centuries later than the page has implied.
Six of the fourteen indexed hits are **Franceschich, Francescich, Francocich** — Slavic formations of the same root, and not this family.

What is here is a married-out daughter and her family: **Dominica Defranceschi × Antonius Zustovich**, with children baptised **1853, 1857, 1861, 1864 and 1866**. Earlier, in 1824 and 1827, a **Maria Defranceschi** stands in two marriage entries as the mother of the parties.

name: Medulin
lead: Four records at the southern tip, and a Maria Defranceschi whose children married Voinich.
body: Medulin is the third of the southern-tip parishes, with Ližnjan and Premantura, and its books open in **1648**.

Four records of the name, and they are marriages rather than baptisms: **Josephus Grafalich (Grahalich) on 1 February 1858** and **Martinus Rakich on 12 October 1859**, both weddings in which a **Maria Defranceschi** and an **Antonius Voinich** stand as the bride's parents; and **Lucas Kivac in 1874**, whose mother is a Maria Defranceschi married to Petrus Kivac.

Which means the De Franceschi presence here is visible **only through daughters** — the surname never appears on a child of the name, only on the mothers of other families' children. It is the clearest small example of what the lost-daughters queue was built to catch. **One qualification, from Pola: a boy «Ivan Defranceski», born at Medulin about 1912, died at Pola on 8 November 1915, aged 3½** ([the entry](/person/ivan-defranceski-1912/)) — so the name was borne by a child in Medulin in the 1910s; the books on the film stop in 1890, so he cannot yet be placed.

***The Medulin death book, read again end to end on 15 November 2026 — and a woman of the name nobody had.*** **«18 November 1873, house 139: Maria (Defranceschi), wife of Ant. Voinić, 77 years, mors ordinaria»** (entry 30; `doc`, level 13). Born about **1796**, and her widower is in the same book — «Antonius Voinić q. Georgii», 74, of the same house 139, in 1878. `inf:` she is plausibly a sister of the **Mattheus Defranceschi «q. Ant. fil., miles»** who died in the same register in 1833 aged 40, both of them children of an Antonio — and the Antonio who gave his daughter Nadalina in marriage at Pula in 1782 is «Antonio de Franceschi della Parrochia di Promontore», next door. Nothing proves either link. **Settled on 16 November 2026 (level 13 on the month column, read by me): page 12, year 1833, entry 9, house 43, day 19, month «Xbris» = December.** *The month cell of entry 8 (13th) reads «Xbris»; entries 9 (19th) and 10 (25th) are ditto marks under it, and entry 6 above stands in «9bris», November, so the column runs August, November, December. The October «entry 43» was the house number, and the November «Apr» was a misreading of the «Xbris».* The age (40), the man and the date are no longer in doubt. Otherwise the book holds nothing of the three names in the ninety-eight years that are on its images (pages 68–69, the 1899 entries 2–29, about January to November, are on no image of this waypoint: see the next paragraph), and **Pomer's dead are not entered here**: in the whole volume Pomer appears only in three priests' subscriptions, «Econ. Pomeri», of 1838, 1843 and 1846.

***⭐ The Medulin marriage book 1831–1899, read again end to end on 16 November 2026 with every spelling typed — the same four women, two weddings dated, and nothing of Kalanj or Kovačina.*** *FamilySearch 9R2H-444, roll 24, item 5 («Župa Medulin, Matična knjiga vjenčanih (1831–1899)», 41 images, 68 pages, 11 August 1831 to 25 November 1899): every image was looked at once by a reader, every cell naming the surname or the Kirac family was zoomed to level 13, and I re-read the four Defranceschi entries on the crops myself. The October reading, made before the Kalanj forms were typed, is verified by this one, not replaced. Not called walked: all other cells were read at level 12. The register records «no marriage in the parish» for 1834 and 1853; images 25–26 are two exposures of pp. 41–42 (a pasted slip of 1921 covers p. 41 on the first); ink smears on images 24–26; later footnotes of 1928–33 record the Prefect of Pola's surname decrees (Lazarich → Lazzari, Radosevich → Ardossi: not variants).* **The name is on four entries, always a wife or a mother:** **(1) 1 February 1858**, Josephus Grafalich (30, house 70) × **Maria Voinich** (22, house 74), her parents «Antonius Voinich cath. poss.» and «**Maria Defran-ceschi** cath. poss.» (witnesses Vitus Radosevich and Antonius Kiraz); **(2) 12 October 1859**, Martinus Rakich (28, house 51) × **Catharina Voinich** (23, house 79), the same parents (witnesses Matthaeus Radosevich and Blasius Kiraz); **(3) 30 July 1874**, Petrus Kirac, son of Simon (29), × **Maria Defranceschi q. Tommasi** (22), both at house 143, her house cell adding «oriunda e [Pomer]» (the second letter is not settled even at level 13), her parents «def. Tomas Defranceschi (cat. agr.)» and «**Magdalena Buić** (cath. agr.)», his Simon Kirac and Catharina Lazaric (witnesses Matthaeus Kirac and Joannes Priurat); **(4) 21 September 1897**, Lucas Kirac (23) × Fusca Demarin (22), his parents «Petrus Kirac agr. cath.» and «**Maria Defrance|sco** rustica cath.» (the last syllable written small above the line after the break), hers Thoma Demarin and Maria Lorenzin (witnesses Giacomo Priorat and Giacomo Chirac; Andreas Bylica, parish priest) (`doc` for each). **(3) and (4) were already told** — Maria of Pomer, born 1 June 1852 to Tomas and Magdalena Buić (the Pomer baptism), and her son Lucas of 1874 — **and this reading finds them again.** **(1) and (2) are the same couple as the death of 18 November 1873**, «Maria (Defranceschi), wife of Ant. Voinić, 77, house 139»: the Medulin marriage cells name their mother Maria Defranceschi, `poss.`, a landowner's wife, and the two brides, 22 and 23, would be born about 1836, when she was about 40 — **twins, or an age a year out** (`inf`; no baptism is read). *The years 1828 and 1831 this page gave for the two weddings are the grooms' birth years in the FamilySearch index («b. 1828», «b. 1831»), not the dates of the weddings; both are corrected above and on [the corrections page](/corrections/).* **Not in this book:** a marriage of the soldier Mattheus (b. 1793, d. 1833) or of Antonio (b. 1819); a Fusca Lazarich married to a Defranceschi (a Fusca Lazarich, 24, of house 13, daughter of Simeon Lazarich and Antonia Michalovich, married **Antonius Mohorich of Lisignano on 19 November 1845** — the same Fusca, born about 1821 at Medulin, as the Mohorić mother of [the Ližnjan house 75](/liznjan/) (`inf`: the name, the father's name and the age agree; the Ližnjan page has her baptism as the next check)); and **Gregorius Voinich × Maria Defranceschi, who married at Premantura on 10 July 1827**, before this book opens ([the Premantura page](/places/premantura/)). **No Kalanj and no Kovačina form in any cell.** *The Kirac family fills the book* (Kirac, Kiraz, Chirac and Chiraz as groom, bride, parent or witness on almost every page: some thirty marriages, none with a Defranceschi except the two above and the two brides' mother); **Fusca Kiraz, daughter of the late Antonius, married Michael Lorenzin on 1 February 1870 aged 29**, and a Fusca Kirac is the mother of Fusca Lorenzin (married 20 November 1894) — whether either is the tree's Fusca Kirac of 1836 is not decided (age 29 would be 1841). *Near-names read and zoomed, not counted:* Kalcich (1869), Kirich or Skirich of Albona (1848; the first letter is unsettled), Kiralich (1859, level 12 only). *Unsettled:* the struck groom of 15 February 1882, the blot over the Mohorich status cell (1845). [Search row](/searched/).

***⭐ The Medulin death book 1801–1899, read a third time on 16 November 2026 with every spelling typed — three entries again, one settled, one gap named, and nothing of Kalanj or Kovačina.*** *FamilySearch 9R2H-HZ7, roll 24, item 6, 40 images (0–3 slates, resolution target, cover, inside cover; 4–38 openings pp. 1–71; 39 end slate), 19 February 1801 to 31 December 1899, Latin «Liber Defunctorum» (headed «Liber mortuorum» from p. 56), no name index, numbering restarting each year, house numbers and causes from 1831: every image looked at once by a reader, every doubtful or target-like cell zoomed to level 13, and I re-read the 1833, 1896 and 1899 cells myself. The Kirac entries (every year) were read at level 12 and not transcribed. **Not called walked, and the October «read end to end» is corrected: pages 68–69 are on no image** — p. 67 ends 29 December 1898 and the next image is p. 70 (the page number read at level 13), which holds 1899 entry 1 (12 January) and entry 30 (11 November), so **the 1899 entries 2–29 are not on this waypoint** (whether pp. 68–69 exist in the book, the film does not say); the gutter strip of the left pages (the *Adnotanda* cells) was looked at only on images 4–9 and 14.* **The name is on three entries, all already told:** **(1) 19 December 1833** — «Matheus Defranceschi q. Ant. fil. miles», 40, «chronicis mor[bus]», the administrator Petrus Mianich, entry 9, house 43 (settled above); **(2) November 1873** — «Maria (Defranceschi) Ant. Voinic(h) uxor», house 139, «mors ordinaria», the day overwritten (probably the 18th) and the age 77 or 71, with her widower «Antonius Voinic q. Georgii», 74, of house 139 on **6 March 1878** (`inf` that he is hers: the house; another Antonius Voinic q. Georgii, 64, of house 138, died on 21 June 1877); **(3) 30 September 1896** — «**Fusca Kirac filia Petri et Mariae Defrancesco**, agr. cath.», ten months, buried 1 October (Bylica, house cell empty): the only Fusca Kirac who died in 1896, so **no grown Fusca Kirac of 1836 died at Medulin that year**. **Not in the book:** a death of Tomas Defranceschi or Magdalena Buić (Pomer's dead are not entered here), of Maria Defrancesco, wife of Petrus Kirac (not to the end of 1898; 1899 entries 2–29 are the gap), and of Mattheus's wife or children; **no Kalanj and no Kovačina form in any cell.** *Near-names, zoomed, not counted:* Maria nata Buić, widow of Klarić and of Georgius Lazarić, 83 (11 January 1884, house 112); Bašić (1883); Koloz/Kobz of Moschienizze (1859). *Unsettled:* 1889 entries 9–12 (struck through; «Matheus Grahalić» and «Giuseppe Chiraz» read, neither a target); the priest of 20 April 1893 (not zoomed); the cut-off left edges of pp. 52 and 63. [Search row](/searched/).

name: Galižana
lead: One entry, and it carries the surname this archive spent a day chasing at Vodnjan.
body: Galižana holds a single record of the name, a marriage of **1824**, and it is worth a page for what is in it: the groom is **Giacomo Giachin**, and a **Domenica Defranceschi** is named among the parties.

**Giachin** is the surname behind an open question at Vodnjan. A *Michiela De Franceschi fu Giuseppe* is named in the Vodnjan death register of February 1833 as the mother of a **Giacomo Giachin**; and the Vodnjan marriages carry a **Sebastiano Giachin × Domenica De Franceschi**, 1817–1832. Here is a Giacomo Giachin marrying at Gallesano in 1824 with a Domenica Defranceschi in the entry.

The index writes one of the parties as **«Sebastiano Defranceschi»**, which is almost certainly wrong — a Giachin father given the mother's surname by a transcriber, a failure this archive has seen before. **The page will say and the index will not**, and until the page is read this is a coincidence of names in a neighbouring parish and nothing more.

name: Kršan
lead: Two De Franceschi women marry two Domazetović men in twelve years — and one of them is a Gologorica woman.
body: Kršan holds five records of the name and they are all of one kind. **Anna Maria Francisca De Franceschi × Thomas Joachimus Clemens de Domazetovich** — children baptised **1881, 1883 and 1887**. **Clotildis Adelaidis Defranceschi × Rudolfus Stanislaus de Domazetovich** — children in **1893 and 1894**. Two women of the name, two men of one family, inside twelve years, in a parish where the surname appears nowhere else.

And the first of them is not a stranger. This site's Gologorica page has carried her since September: **«Anna Maria Francisca, born at Gologorica 28 October 1860, married a Domazetovich, died at Trieste on 22 June 1941.»** The roster had her birth as 1880 — which would have made her a year old at her first child's baptism — and the two records were never set beside each other until the pedigree gate refused to draw her chart and the refusal had to be explained.

So the Kršan marriages reach back to **Gologorica**, the village of this archive's own line, thirty kilometres north-west. Whether Clotildis Adelaidis is her sister the register does not say, and this page will not guess.

The index spells the husband's name four ways across three entries — *Thomas Joachimus Clemnet*, *Thomas Joachimus Celmes De Domazetovich*, *Thomas-Joachimus-Clemens Domazetovich* — which is the ordinary condition of this material and the reason a name alone settles nothing.
